A group of family members is facing jail time after orchestrating a £4.5 million fine-wine scam that targeted dozens of elderly investors. Daniel Snelling, 38, deceived victims into investing thousands of pounds in Australian wine, describing it as ‘the best money could buy.’ Together with his sister Dina Snelling, 35, and their cousin Rebecca McDonald, 42, he assured investors that their wine would be sold for significant profits after being stored for three years in ‘premium’ facilities.

Operating under the company Nouveau World Wines, the trio collected £2.5 million by selling thousands of bottles, but the scheme ended before investors could recover their funds. The proceeds were then funneled into a second fraudulent venture, Finbow Wines, which sold cheap Italian wine at events like the 2010 World Cup. They typically took about £5,000 from each mainly elderly investor, convincing some to buy as many as 10,000 bottles at a time.

After a two-month trial at Southwark Crown Court, Daniel and Dina Snelling were found guilty of two counts of conspiracy to defraud. Daniel was also convicted of two counts of converting criminal property, while Rebecca McDonald was found guilty of one count of conspiracy to defraud. Sentencing for all three is set for September 9.

Simon Dempsey, 43, was acquitted of any involvement in the Finbow Wines scheme.

Daniel Snelling launched Nouveau World Wines in January 2007 as sole shareholder and director. Dina was the office director, and McDonald, a former KPMG employee, was business development manager. They used cold calls to market the venture, promising high-end investment opportunities with high returns and low risk. The company claimed to have offices in Mayfair’s Berkeley Square, but actually operated from Greenwich, south-east London.

Investors were enticed with promises of 30 percent profits and assured that the wine would be safely stored in Australia. But between January 2007 and August 2009, only a fraction of the promised 39,000 bottles of wine actually existed.

Prosecutor Julian Christopher told the court that when investors tried to sell their wine or sought information, most found the wine did not exist. Facing pressure from £2.5 million in investments, the defendants shifted profits to Finbow Wines, their next fraudulent venture, promising profits from selling Italian wine in China and at major sporting events. Again, investors saw no returns; of 50 supposed shipping containers of wine, only two were sent to China.

Police intervened on March 4, 2010, just as the group prepared another fraudulent venture. Daniel Snelling, of Sutton, south London, denied the charges but was convicted. Dina Snelling, from Chislehurst, and McDonald, of Bexleyheath, were also convicted. The jury could not reach a verdict on a second conspiracy count against McDonald, which remains on file. All three will be sentenced in September, while Dempsey was cleared of all charges.

article_content: Leadership fundamentally shapes the direction and success of teams and organizations. Two prominent models—transformational and transactional leadership—offer different yet influential ways leaders can operate. The effectiveness of each approach depends on the organization’s culture, needs, and goals. Transformational leadership is rooted in inspiring team members to achieve excellence and personal development. Leaders who use this style often have strong charisma, a clear vision for the future, persuasive communication skills, and support innovation and independence in their teams. They prioritize fostering relationships and encourage both professional and personal growth among members. Teams led this way often experience greater satisfaction, increased creativity, and higher achievement. On the other hand, transactional leadership operates through a defined structure of rules, rewards, and corrective actions. Transactional leaders set precise expectations, recognize achievements, and swiftly address any deviations from standards. This approach excels in tightly regulated settings and situations where meeting clear, immediate objectives is crucial. While it provides stability and clear direction, it can result in less creative input and adaptability. The two styles differ notably: transformational leadership focuses on internal motivation and a long-term vision, while transactional leadership is more about external rewards and immediate goals. Transformational leaders act as mentors and visionaries, whereas transactional leaders manage tasks through compliance and monitoring. Transformational leadership’s strengths include inspiring teams, nurturing new ideas, and fostering growth. However, it may lead to teams heavily dependent on the leader and, if not aligned with organizational goals, can cause conflicts. Transactional leadership brings clarity and efficient outcomes, but can reduce engagement and stifle creative thinking. Selecting the most effective leadership style involves considering the team’s structure, the company’s objectives, and task nature. Transformational leadership works best where innovation and team development are priorities, whereas transactional leadership suits environments prioritizing clear standards and short-term performance. Many leaders blend both styles—adapting based on circumstances—to combine innovation with accountability. Effective modern leaders also cultivate emotional intelligence, support an inclusive environment, and encourage ongoing learning and adaptability. This means leading by example, embracing diverse perspectives, and staying open to change. Frequently asked questions highlight leadership’s role in setting direction and inspiring teams, best practices such as strong communication and inclusivity, the significance of emotional intelligence, and the need for leaders to adapt to evolving technologies and challenges.

De gwo modèl—lidèchip transfòmasyonèl ak transfaksyonèl—ofri diferan, men enfliyan fason lidè yo ka jere ekip yo. Efikasite chak apwòch depann de kilti, bezwen, ak objektif òganizasyon an. Lidèchip transfòmasyonèl konsantre sou enspire manm ekip pou yo rive nan ekselans ak devlopman pèsonèl. Lidè ki sèvi ak estil sa a gen anpil karisma, gen vizyon klè pou lavni, pale ak konviksyon, epi ankouraje inovasyon ak endependans. Yo bati bon relasyon ak ankouraje devlopman manm yo. Ekip ki gen lidè konsa anjeneral plis satisfe, pi kreyatif, epi reyalize plis siksè. Okontrè, lidèchip transfaksyonèl baze sou estrikti ki klè—règ, rekonpans, epi aksyon disiplinè. Lidè sa yo tabli atant ekzak, rekonpanse reyalizasyon, epi entèvni byen vit si estanda pa suiv byen. Metòd sa a pi efikas kote gen anpil règ oswa objektif ki dwe akonpli tou swit. Pandan li bay estabilite ak direksyon klè, li ka limite kreyativite ak adaptabilite. De estil yo diferan sitou nan motivasyon ak objektif yo: transfòmasyonèl mete aksan sou motivasyon enteryè ak vizyon long tèm, tandiske transfaksyonèl a se pou rekonpans ekstèn ak objektif kout tèm. Lidè transfòmasyonèl se modèl ak gid, pandan ke transfaksyonèl jere epi kontwole aksyon. Avantaj transfòmasyonèl: enspire ekip, ankouraje inovasyon, epi ankouraje devlopman. Dezavantaj yo gen ladan depandans sou lidè a, ak risk dezakò si vizyon pa metafon ak objektif òganizasyon an. Avanaj transfaksyonèl: bay klarte ak efikasite men li ka desann angajman ak limit kreyativite. Pou chwazi stil ki pi apwopriye, ou dwe konsidere estrikti ekip la, objektif konpayi an, ak nati travay la. Lidèchip transfòmasyonèl pi bon kote inovasyon ak devlopman enpòtan, pandan transfaksyonèl la adapte ak anviwònman ki bezwen règ sevè ak objektif rapid. Anpil lidè melanje de stil yo, chanje depandan ak bezwen sikonstans yo, pou amelyore inovasyon ak responsabilite. Lidè modèn ki reyisi ogmante entèlijans emosyonèl yo, bati mètdam enklizif epi pouse aprantisaj ak adaptasyon. Yo bay egzanp, apati kominikasyon ouvè ak akseptasyon divèsite. Kesyon ki pi poze yo mete aksan sou wòl lidèchip nan oryante ak enspire ekip, bon pratik tankou kominikasyon ak enklizyon, enpòtans entèlijans emosyonèl, epi kapasite lidè pou adapte ak chanjman ak teknoloji nouvo.

Liverpool midfielder Joe Allen asserts that the team will not fear Europe’s top clubs as the Reds return to the Champions League next season. Securing second place behind Manchester City marks Liverpool’s first entry into Europe’s elite club competition since 2009. Over the past year, Brendan Rodgers’ side has demonstrated they can compete with the best, particularly at Anfield, and Allen is eager for the upcoming challenge.

Allen believes Liverpool can continue progressing after narrowly missing the league title. The team is motivated to play Champions League football. “I can’t wait. As a young footballer, you dream of playing in the Champions League,” said the Wales international. “It’s what you strive for every day. I’m looking forward to next season starting and experiencing one of the pinnacles of club football.

“Although this season is finishing, being in the Champions League next year is a major reason to celebrate. As a player, you set goals, and competing in the Champions League is a big one. I can’t wait, and I’m sure the fans feel the same.

“Last year, our record against the big teams was rather disappointing, but this season, we felt confident going into any match, home or away—that’s been a major difference. From an attacking standpoint, scoring 101 league goals is incredible. Our record at Anfield this season will be significant as well. We look forward to making Anfield a tough place for any team to visit, whether in the Premier League, Champions League, or cup matches.

“Liverpool missed out on a first league title in 24 years by just two points, with our fate in our own hands until late April when we lost at home to Chelsea. Still, the progress since finishing seventh a year ago means we are confident the squad can contend again next season, even with the Champions League challenge.

“Nobody would have predicted how far we’d come this year. There is some disappointment after coming so close, but we have much to celebrate,” Allen added. “Our belief has grown over the season. At the start, we would have accepted a second-place finish, but as the year went on, we realized our strength as a team.

“We can’t become complacent—that would be a risk. Instead, we’ll use this experience to push on next season. This was an important year to showcase our talent, and it’s great to see Liverpool back at the top. The most exciting part is there’s still more to come. The experience from this season will help us in the coming years.”

More than 80% of patients on some hospital wards in England say they would not want their loved ones to be treated there, according to official government data. The statistics show that, in 19 hospital wards across the country, at least half of patients surveyed last month would not recommend the care their ward provides.

The worst performing ward is Ward 12 at Blackpool Victoria Hospital, which specializes in illnesses of the stomach and intestines. None of the patients surveyed said they would recommend it to others. Similarly, at the Woodpecker ward in Swindon’s Great Western Hospital, only six out of 41 patients surveyed last month would be happy for loved ones to receive care there.

The government implemented the ‘friends and family’ test in April to measure patient satisfaction and provide more transparency about hospital standards. The test, which is open to any patient visiting A&E or staying on a ward, asks a simple question: ‘How likely are you to recommend our ward or A&E department to friends and family if they needed similar care?’ Patients tick one of six boxes, ranging from ‘extremely likely’ to ‘extremely unlikely’ or ‘don’t know.’

Hospitals, A&E departments, and wards each receive a score between -100 and 100, reflecting the number of positive minus negative responses. Scores above 0 are considered good, while scores above 50 are rated as excellent. The latest results reveal an average score of 50 for A&E units, and 72 for hospital wards.

This survey is often regarded as the NHS’s version of Tripadvisor, where the public can view hospital scores and read patient comments on the NHS Choices website. The government expects hospitals to have at least 15% of patients complete the assessment. However, results show patchy participation, with just four out of 3,547 A&E patients at Medway Maritime Hospital and only six out of 3,367 at Milton Keynes A&E completing the survey last month.

These response rates have raised concerns that staff might be handing the forms primarily to patients they expect to give positive feedback. Despite such concerns, NHS England says that response rates have gradually increased since the survey was introduced six months ago. The survey also allows patients to suggest improvements. At Hillingdon NHS Trust in West London, staff introduced quieter-closing bins and dimmer night lights after feedback about noise and brightness.

Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt has described the surveys as giving ‘real patient power’ and pushing hospitals to improve standards. Hospitals routinely scoring poorly may be referred to the Care Quality Commission for further review.

Pi move salk la se Ward 12 nan Blackpool Victoria Hospital, ki espesyalize nan maladi lestomak ak trip. Okenn pasyan ki te reponn pa ta rekòmande li. Menm jan an, sou salk Woodpecker nan Great Western Hospital nan Swindon, sèlman 6 sou 41 pasyan di yo ta vle moun yo renmen resevwa swen la.

Gouvènman an lanse tès ‘zanmi ak fanmi’ an avril pou mezire satisfaksyon pasyan yo epi bay plis transparans sou nivo lopital yo. Tès la disponib pou nenpòt pasyan ki pase A&E oswa dòmi sou salk, epi li poze yon kesyon senp: 'Ki posiblite pou ou rekòmande salk nou an oswa depatman ijans (A&E) bay zanmi ak fanmi ou?' Pasyan yo chwazi youn nan sis repons, soti nan ‘ekstrèmman posib’ rive ‘ekstrèmman enposib’, oubyen ‘pa konnen’.

Chak lopital, depatman A&E oswa salk jwenn yon nòt ant -100 ak 100, depann de kantite repons pozitif mwens negatif yo. Nenpòt nòt pi wo pase 0 konsidere kòm bon, epi pi wo pase 50 konsidere kòm ekselan. Dènye rezilta yo montre nòt mwayèn 50 pou inite A&E, ak 72 pou salk lopital yo.

Gen anpil ki konsidere tès sa tankou vèsyon NHS Tripadvisor paske piblik la ka wè nòt yo ak kòmantè pasyan sou sit NHS Choices la. Gouvènman an vle omwen 15% pasyan ranpli sondaj la. Sepandan, rezilta yo montre patisipasyon pa toujou bon: sèlman 4 sou 3,547 pasyan A&E nan Medway Maritime Hospital ak 6 sou 3,367 nan Milton Keynes te reponn sondaj la mwa pase a.

Pousantaj sa yo soulve enkyetid ke gen posiblite staf yo ap bay fòm yo prensipalman bay pasyan yo panse ki satisfè. Malgre sa, NHS England di kantite repons yo ap monte depi lansman an 6 mwa de sa. Sondaj la pèmèt tou pasyan yo bay sijesyon pou amelyorasyon. Nan Hillingdon NHS Trust nan lwès Lond, yo mete bwat fatra ki pa fè bri ak limyè pi fènwa lannwit apre plizyè plent sou bri ak limyè.

Sekretè Sante Jeremy Hunt di sondaj sa bay 'vrè pouvwa pasyan' epi ede lopital amelyore sèvis yo. Lopital ki toujou resevwa move nòt voye bay Care Quality Commission pou revizyon.

article_content: BRUSSELS: The European Union is preparing to provide Ukraine with €50 billion ($53.4 billion) in aid, even if Hungary attempts to block the package, according to EU officials. As Ukraine continues to resist Russia's invasion nearly two years into the war, the European Commission has proposed increasing budget support to help Ukraine pay salaries and cover essential expenses. The EU's 27 member states are expected to vote on the aid at a summit scheduled for December 14-15. However, concerns remain that Hungary, led by Prime Minister Viktor Orban—who has maintained close ties with Moscow and previously objected to similar aid—could veto the package. Approving payouts from the EU budget requires unanimous agreement among all member states. Hungary has not officially commented on the matter. Should Budapest exercise its veto, EU officials indicate they can bypass the block by having each of the other 26 EU governments arrange their own aid agreements with Kyiv, collectively matching the proposed amount. 'Hungary risks pushing its luck. We would prefer their cooperation, but there is a limit to members tolerating Budapest holding up decisions. The workaround is cumbersome, but we can implement it if necessary,' an EU official stated. Another official agreed, affirming that support for Ukraine will be delivered one way or another. If unanimity cannot be reached through the EU budget, alternative arrangements such as intergovernmental agreements or national guarantees will be explored. Last year, Hungary vetoed a similar proposal for €18 billion in financial support to Ukraine but eventually conceded after securing concessions and learning that the EU was prepared to use a workaround. Asked whether the EU would pursue that path again, European Trade Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said, 'Last year we considered a 'Plan B' but ultimately avoided it. I hope we can do the same this year.' Orban, who has led Hungary for over a decade, has clashed with other EU members over issues including democratic standards, foreign policy, migration, and LGBT rights.

Tout depans sou bidjè Inyon an mande inanimite. Ongri poko bay okenn repons ofisyèl. Si Budapest ta mete veto, ofisyèl Inyon an di yo kapab kontoune sa si chak nan lòt 26 peyi yo fè pwòp akò ede pa yo ak Kyiv, pou monte menm montan an. 'Ongri ap riske chans li. article_content:
Skip Sanzeri, founder, board chair, and COO of QuSecure—a leading post-quantum cybersecurity firm—warns that quantum computing presents a serious threat to the encryption methods that keep our data secure and private. Quantum computers leverage fundamentally different operations from standard computers and are mathematically proven to potentially break public-key infrastructure (PKI), the cryptography protecting online data exchanges. At present, RSA 2048 is the most widely used and trusted encryption standard. To date, quantum computers have not been able to break RSA 2048.

Nevertheless, there is a tactic called 'Steal Now, Decrypt Later' (SNDL), where encrypted data stolen today is stored for later decryption once technology is capable. Given that adversarial nations are likely saving today's encrypted data, enterprises and governments have strong reasons to move toward more advanced cryptography.

On September 18, the cybersecurity field was startled by news from San Diego-based MemComputing. At the request of the US Air Force, MemComputing used its technology to investigate vulnerabilities in PKI. They published a white paper, 'Scaling up prime factorization with self-organizing gates: A MemComputing Approach,' detailing the use of in-memory processing ASICs (Application Specific Integrated Circuits) to simulate breaking RSA encryption in real time. Their software emulation addressed factorization problems from 30 to 150 bits; results indicated the approach scaled up to 300 bits, with factorization time following a second-degree polynomial relative to bit count. According to MemComputing’s findings, their ASIC chip could potentially break RSA 2048 in under two years using classical computing—an extraordinary claim compared to millions of years required by today’s best supercomputers.

If accurate, this represents a fundamental breakthrough, suggesting that attackers could undermine global public key encryption and compromise data traveling across the internet. Prior to this, concerns focused on quantum computers eventually reaching this capability—often dubbed 'Q-Day,' estimated to occur within 5 to 10 years, once quantum computers become powerful enough.

However, MemComputing's advance demonstrates that new forms of classical computing may also threaten encryption, highlighting the need for proactive defense.

In response, the US government is not idle. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has spent over seven years developing and testing quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms—based on mathematical problems distinct from current encryption’s prime factorization—for future standards. These are designed to withstand both quantum and innovative classical attacks such as those described by MemComputing.

On December 21, 2022, President Biden enacted the 'Quantum Computing Cybersecurity Preparedness Act' (Public Law 117-260), mandating the migration of federal systems to quantum-resistant cryptography. This marks a significant step toward comprehensive federal upgrade of cryptographic protections.

The current environment makes it critical for organizations—and government entities—to begin transitioning now, recognizing that full implementation could take years or even a decade. With emerging threats from both quantum and advanced classical computing, time is of the essence. Organizations are advised to:

1. Learn about new cryptographic standards from NIST, as these use different mathematical structures and are not reliant on factoring large numbers.
2. Test new NIST algorithms promptly, as there is little risk and significant benefit to early adoption and familiarization.
3. Stay 'crypto-agile' by preparing for adjustable and flexible cryptographic systems, anticipating that new algorithms may evolve as standards are refined.
4. Choose deployment partners that enable gradual upgrades—integrating new algorithms over existing ones to minimize disruption.
5. Secure the entire network, including servers, cloud systems, mobile devices, and other endpoints—any weak link can serve as a point of attack.
6. Look for scalable solutions that do not require endpoint replacement, reducing inconvenience and improving protection.
7. Consider a hybrid approach that uses both existing and upcoming quantum-resistant encryption during the transition.

The MemComputing development amplifies the urgency for testing and deploying advanced cryptography. If public-key cryptography fails, the consequences could be grave for national security and beyond.
translated_content:
Skip Sanzeri, fondatè, prezidan komite direksyon, ak COO QuSecure—yon gwo konpayi sekirite enfòmatik apre kwantik—avèti ke òdinatè kwantik reprezante yon gwo menas pou ankripsyon nou itilize pou sekirize ak pwoteje done nou yo. Òdinatè kwantik yo fonksyone yon jan diferan ak òdinatè klasik epi yo pwouve matematikman ke yo kapab an menase enfrastrikti kle piblik (PKI), kriptografi ki pwoteje echanj done sou entènèt la. Kounye a, RSA 2048 se estanda ankripsyon ki pi koni ak ki bay plis konfyans. Jiskaprezan, òdinatè kwantik poko rive kraze RSA 2048.

Men, gen yon estrateji yo rele ‘Vòlè Kounya, Dekode Pita’ (SNDL), kote done ankripte yo vòlè kounya, epi konkirè sere l pou l dekode li pi ta lè teknoloji a pèmèt sa. Peyi advèsè yo ap sere done sa yo, kidonk antrepriz ak gouvènman yo gen bon rezon pou yo chanje rapidman pou nouvo kriptografi ki pi solid.

Sou 18 septanm, kominote sekirite enfòmatik la te sezi ak nouvèl MemComputing soti San Diego. A demann Lame Ayeryen Etazini, MemComputing teste teknoloji li sou frajilite PKI. Yo pibliye yon rapò, ‘Scaling up prime factorization with self-organizing gates: A MemComputing Approach,’ ki esplike kijan yo itilize chip ASIC (Application Specific Integrated Circuits) pou imite dekode ankripsyon RSA an tan reyèl. Lojisyèl yo teste problem faktorizasyon ant 30 ak 150 bits; yo montre ke teknik la mache jiska 300 bits, ak tan faktorizasyon an mache sou yon polinòm dezyèm degre selon kantite bits. MemComputing di chip yo kapab kraze RSA 2048 an mwens de ane ak òdinatè klasik—sa ki fò anpil diferans ak milyon ane super-òdinatè pran pou menm travay la.

Si sa vre, atakan ta ka kraze sekirite tout kominikasyon entènèt la epi menase tout done k ap sikile sou rezo a. Avan sa, prepokipasyon an te plis sou òdinatè kwantik tounen ase pisan, yo rele sa ‘Q-Day’, ki ka rive nan 5 a 10 lane.

Kounye a, devlopman MemComputing lan moutre gen lòt teknik klasik ki kapab menase ankripsyon an tou, epi sa mete aksan sou bezwen pou pi bon defans kounya.

Anfas sa, gouvènman ameriken pa chita ap gade. NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) ap travay plis pase sèt lane pou prepare ak tès nouvo algoritm kriptografik ki rezistan ak kwantik—baze sou lòt pwoblèm matematik. Algoritm sa yo fèt pou reziste ak atak kwantik ak nouvo atak klasik tankou sa MemComputing eksplike a.

Sou 21 desanm 2022, Prezidan Biden siyen 'Quantum Computing Cybersecurity Preparedness Act' (Lwa 117-260), ki fòse tout sistèm federal pou migrasyon sou kriptografi ki reziste ak òdinatè kwantik. Sa se premye etap pou ranfòse sekirite tout sistèm federal yo.

Sitiyasyon aktyèl la fè li kritik pou òganizasyon ak ajan gouvènman kòmanse tranzisyon depi kounye a, paske sa ka pran plizyè ane. Avèk menas òdinatè kwantik ak nouvo teknik klasik, chak minit konte. Rekòmandasyon pou òganizasyon yo:

1. Aprann sou nouvo algoritm NIST paske yo itilize lòt matematik epi pa depann de faktorizasyon gwo chif.
2. Teste nouvo algoritm NIST vit, risk la prèske pa egziste epi benefis lan entèn.
3. Rete krypto-agile pou adapte sistèm rapidman si algoritm yo chanje oswa evolye.
4. Itilize patnè ki ka mete nouvo algoritm yo oubyen ansyen yo ansanm san brase tout sistèm nan.
5. Sekirize tout rezo a: serveurs, cloud, telefòn, tout ekipman—itilizatè oubyen aparèy ki pa pwoteje ka kreye risk.
6. Chèche solisyon ki pa mande chanje aparèy itilizatè pou bay plis sekirite pi fasil.
7. Adopte yon apwòch 'hybride' kote ou itilize tou de vye ak nouvo ankripsyon pandan tranzisyon an.

Devèlopman MemComputing lan ogmante dijans pou teste ak deplwaye nouvo kriptografi. Si ankripsyon kle piblik kraze, konsekans yo riske grav pou sekirite peyi ak mond lan.

article_content: If you enjoy playing with the froth on your coffee, here’s a challenge: could you create something as impressive as these 3-D latte sculptures? Japanese barista and latte artist Kazuki Yamamoto, currently working at Cafe10g in Osaka, has taken coffee art to new heights by shaping animals and cartoon characters from steamed milk foam. Yamamoto, 26, crafts three-dimensional designs such as rabbits, hippos, and giraffes, some of which even seem to climb from one cup into another. His temporary masterpieces often depict popular figures, from South Korean pop star Psy to Disney characters like Mickey Mouse, Goofy, and Pinocchio, as well as iconic images like a Salvador Dali-inspired melting clock. Each creation takes about three to five minutes to make. Yamamoto shares his work regularly on Twitter, where more than 82,000 followers eagerly await his latest designs. He hopes to someday open his own café in Tokyo, where his art would be more than just a perk of the job. He’s not alone in this artistic pursuit: Kohei Matsuno, a 23-year-old originally from Osaka and now working at a café in Tokyo, also crafts detailed latte art, drawing inspiration from anime, Lady Gaga, and even Edvard Munch’s 'The Scream.' Using tools like cocktail pins, spoons, and toothpicks for detail, Matsuno first piles milk and foam, then adds shading with espresso. While many appreciate the creativity, some in the coffee community debate whether focusing on latte art detracts from the importance of taste. Regardless, these intricate creations—ranging from cartoon characters to sleepy bears and even grumpy cats—delight customers and showcase the evolving artistry of coffee.

Yamamoto, ki gen 26 an, fè eskilti twa dimansyon tankou lapen, ipopotam, ak jiraf—gen kèk ki sanble ap soti nan yon gode pou antre nan yon lòt. Travay tanporè li yo souvan montre pèsonaj popilè tankou Psy, yon vedèt Koreyen, ak karaktè Disney tankou Mickey Mouse, Goofy, ak Pinocchio, epi li fè tou imaj tankou yon revèy Dali k ap fonn. article_content: The article reviews key evidence and arguments in the murder trial of Amanda Knox and Raffaele Sollecito:  Knife: Prosecution claims a knife found in Sollecito’s home had Amanda Knox’s DNA on the handle and victim Meredith Kercher’s DNA on the blade, suggesting it was the murder weapon. Defense argues the knife does not match Kercher’s wounds or the knife outline at the scene, and that the DNA sample is too small to be conclusive.  Kercher’s bra clasp: Prosecution says a bra clasp found on the floor had Sollecito’s DNA, proving his presence. Defense insists the clasp was contaminated due to being moved and left at the scene for over six weeks.  Knox’s statements: Prosecutors highlight that during interrogation, Knox spoke of hearing Kercher scream and accused Patrick Lumumba, who was later cleared. They use these statements as evidence of her involvement. Defense claims Knox was pressured and made these comments while being asked to imagine the events; her confession was later excluded because she did not have a lawyer present.  Bloody footprint: Prosecution attributes a bloody footprint on a bathroom rug to Sollecito. Defense, supported by forensic experts, says it matches Rudy Guede, who was convicted separately, and does not match Sollecito’s known hammer toe.  Broken window: Prosecution believes Knox staged a break-in by breaking a window. Defense argues Rudy Guede, with a history of break-ins, broke the window from outside, supported by expert testimony that a burglar could have done so.  Crime scene contamination: Defense contends key DNA evidence was compromised by improper handling, such as investigators not using gloves and disturbing remains. Prosecution maintains all evidence was properly handled and that the burden is on the defense to prove mishandling.  Bloody shoe print: Prosecution claims a shoe print near Kercher’s body belonged to Sollecito. Defense argues it matches shoes owned by Guede, backed by expert testimony challenging the initial attribution.

Defans lan di kouto sa pa matche ak blesi Kercher yo oswa tras kouto a, epi echantiyon ADN lan twò piti pou fè prèv solid.  Klèp soutyen Kercher: Akizasyon di ADN Sollecito te sou yon klèp atè a, sa ta montre li te sou sèn krim nan. Defans lan di klèp la te kontamine paske li te deplase epi li te ret la pandan plis pase sis semèn.  Deklarasyon Knox: Pwokirè yo mete aksan sou pawòl Knox te di pandan entèwogasyon kote li di li te tande Kercher kriye epi li akize Patrick Lumumba, ki te vin libere pi ta. The Obamacare website may still have technical issues, but journalists are working diligently. Across the country, as Republicans share stories of Americans losing their health insurance and facing higher costs, journalists investigate these claims. They contact policyholders and check insurance exchange websites to clarify facts in the public debate about Obamacare.

Here are a few stories journalists have helped clarify about the Affordable Care Act (ACA):

Deborah Cavallaro appeared on television discussing her canceled insurance plan. Los Angeles Times columnist Michael Hiltzik found her plan cost $293 per month, had a $5,000 deductible, and covered only two doctor visits per year with annual out-of-pocket limits of $8,500. On the California exchange, she could get a 'silver' plan for $333 per month—a $40 increase—but with a $2,000 deductible, $6,350 out-of-pocket maximum, and all doctor visits covered. Hiltzik concluded this was a significant improvement over her previous plan.

Dianne Barrette appeared on CBS news, disappointed her $54-per-month plan was canceled. Nancy Metcalf at Consumer Reports found her plan provided minimal real coverage, only paying for hospitalization in limited situations. Metcalf determined Barrette could get a 'silver' plan for $165 per month that would offer real protection for various illnesses.

Edie Littlefield Sundby, a cancer survivor, blamed ACA for losing her policy in a Wall Street Journal op-ed. However, Igor Volsky from Think Progress reported that her insurer, United Healthcare, withdrew from California's individual market due to business reasons unrelated directly to ACA. United cited their small market presence and said state law prevents re-entering the market until 2017.

Dylan Scott from Talking Points Memo reported on Donna from Seattle, whose insurer sent her a cancellation letter guiding her to a more expensive plan but did not mention the state insurance exchange. By switching via the exchange, she avoided spending about $1,000 more per month. Washington regulators even issued a consumer alert about such insurer practices.

These examples show the importance of fact-checking in the heated debate over Obamacare. Despite ongoing criticism and challenges, journalists continue to help Americans understand their actual choices and benefits under the law.

Editor's Note: This article includes United Healthcare's explanation of its withdrawal from California's individual insurance marketplace. The opinions expressed are those of Sally Kohn.

Curious about what kind of relationship advice artificial intelligence could give, I decided to consult two different AI chatbots—OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Meta’s Billie—about moving in with my boyfriend of three years. Both bots offered advice, but their approaches were noticeably distinct.

Meta’s Billie, fashioned after Kendall Jenner, introduced herself as a supportive 'older sister' and communicated in a laid-back, conversational manner. She encouraged me to share personal details and even asked me to “spill the tea.” Billie’s relaxed demeanor made her guidance feel like it was coming from a friend. She raised specific points about the importance of communication in a relationship and highlighted my boyfriend’s gaming hobby as a potential issue, suggesting I address it directly if it affected chores or shared responsibilities.

Billie is part of Meta’s suite of celebrity-based AI assistants, designed to help users with varied topics such as relationships, cooking, or fitness, using familiar personalities. Her approachable style made her advice feel more digestible and personal.

In contrast, ChatGPT by OpenAI responded with comprehensive lists that outlined general relationship advice and factors to consider before living together, such as compatibility, finances, long-term plans, and task-sharing. While informative and impartial, ChatGPT’s replies felt more formal and less customized to my situation, making the experience less engaging.

The differing philosophies behind these chatbots were also noted: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has advised against forming close emotional bonds with AI, pointing out that their chatbot’s design was deliberately non-human. Conversely, Meta’s Chris Cox supports giving AI more playfulness and room for self-expression.

In the end, both chatbots recommended open discussion with my partner before making a big commitment like cohabitation, wishing me luck in my decision-making process.

Billie, ki pran aparans Kendall Jenner, prezante tèt li kòm yon "gwo sè" ak pale avè m fasil tankou zanmi. Li mande m rakonte l tout detay epi ba m konsèy ki senp. Li mete aksan sou kominikasyon epi li raple jwèt videyo mennaj mwen ka kreye pwoblèm si sa anpeche li fè devwa lakay.

Billie fè pati nouvo asistan entèlijan Meta ak figi selebrite pou ede sou anpil sijè—relasyon, manje, oswa fè egzèsis. Fason li pale a fè tout konsèy li yo sanble pratik ak zanmitay.

article_content: The Labour Party has welcomed the 2023 presidential candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Atiku Abubakar's proposal for a merger of opposition parties, describing it as a good idea worthy of consideration. However, the New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) expressed terms for joining such a coalition, stating it would only participate if Atiku agrees to support Rabiu Kwankwaso, former Kano governor and NNPP leader, as the joint candidate to challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in 2027. These statements come in response to Atiku’s public call on Tuesday for opposition parties to unite to remove the APC from power. The Punch reports that Atiku made this suggestion during a meeting with the National Executive Committee of the Inter-Party Advisory Council of Nigeria. The former Vice President cautioned about the risk of Nigeria becoming a one-party state, saying, "We have all seen how the APC is increasingly turning Nigeria into a one-party dictatorship. If we don't come together to challenge what the ruling party is trying to create, our democracy will suffer, and the consequences will affect future generations." In an interview with The Punch, acting National Publicity Secretary of the Labour Party, Obiora Ifoh, called Atiku's proposal a good one, arguing that most Nigerians want a move towards true democracy. Ifoh remarked, "Anything that will make Nigerians experience genuine democracy is welcome." Conversely, NNPP’s National Publicity Secretary, Yakubu Shendam, described Atiku's call as 'medicine after death,' insisting that the only acceptable basis for collaboration is backing Kwankwaso for the presidency. Shendam said, "We are comfortable as a party with Rabiu Kwankwaso as our national leader. We urge Atiku, as an elder statesman, to support Kwankwaso if he wants relevance in 2027." Meanwhile, the APC maintains it is unthreatened by Atiku’s suggestion. APC Publicity Director, Bala Ibrahim, said, "Atiku has lost both in court and the court of public opinion. The PDP and Atiku lack the capacity to threaten the ruling party." In summary, Nigeria’s main opposition parties are debating Atiku’s proposal, with Labour Party expressing support, NNPP setting preconditions, and APC dismissing any threat posed by opposition unity.

Men, New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) mete kondisyon pou patisipe nan koalisyon sa, pou di ke yo sèlman dakò si Atiku dakò sipòte ansyen gouvènè Kano a, Rabiu Kwankwaso, kòm kandida inik pou kontre Pati Pwogresis an Pouvwa a (APC) an 2027. Deklarasyon sa yo soti apre apèl piblik Atiku te fè madi pou tout pati opozisyon yo mete tèt ansanm pou wete APC sou pouvwa. The Punch rapòte Atiku te fè pwopozisyon sa pandan yon reyinyon ak Komite Egzekitif Nasyonal Inter-Party Advisory Council of Nigeria. Ansyen Vis Prezidan an te mete aksan sou danje peyi a ka vire yon eta ak yon sèl pati, li di: "Nou tout wè kijan APC ap tounen Nijerya yon diktati sèl pati. Si nou pa mete tèt ansanm pou n konbat sa yo ap eseye etabli a, demokrasi nou an ap soufri, e sa ap gen konsekans sou jenerasyon kap vini yo." Nan yon entèvyou ak The Punch, Sekretè Piblikite Nasyonal Adjouen Pati Travayè a, Obiora Ifoh, rele pwopozisyon Atiku a yon bon ide, li di pifò Nijeryen vle viv anndan yon demokrasi reyèl. Ifoh deklare: "Tout sa ki ka pèmèt Nijeryen viv yon demokrasi vrèman, se aksepte." Okontrè, Sekretè Piblikite Nasyonal NNPP a, Yakubu Shendam, deklare apèl Atiku a se 'medsin apre lanmò', li ensiste sèl fason yo kapab mete tèt ansanm, se si yo sipòte Kwankwaso kòm kandida prezidan. Shendam di: "Nou, kòm pati, konfotab ak Rabiu Kwankwaso kòm lidè nasyonal nou. Nou ap mande Atiku, kòm gran frè, pou l mache ansanm ak Kwankwaso si li vle rete enpòtan an 2027." PDP ak Atiku pa gen kapasite pou menase pati ki ap dirije a." Pou rezime, pati opozisyon prensipal yo ap diskite sou pwopozisyon Atiku a: Pati Travayè sipòte l, NNPP mete kondisyon, pandan APC rejte posiblite opozisyon an mete menas sou pouvwa yo.

article_content: Eric Lawson, recognized for his role as the Marlboro Man in late 1970s cigarette commercials, passed away this month at 72 due to respiratory failure related to smoking. He is among at least five individuals who promoted Marlboro cigarettes and later died from smoking-related diseases. Others include David Millar, the 1950s Marlboro Man, who died of emphysema in 1987; David McLean, who succumbed to lung cancer in 1995; Wayne McLaren, a former rodeo rider and later anti-smoking advocate, who died of lung cancer in 1992 before his 52nd birthday; and Dick Hammer, a real-life firefighter and TV actor from 'Emergency!', who died of lung cancer at 69 in 1999. Lawson, who started smoking at age 14, served as the Marlboro Man from 1978 to 1981. He died at his home in San Luis Obispo, California, on January 10, with his wife, Susan, confirming his passing. The Marlboro Man was an image developed by advertiser Leo Burnett to make filtered cigarettes more appealing to men, as they were previously viewed as feminine. Other Marlboro Men included Christian Haren, Darrell Winfield (still alive), and Brad Johnson. Lawson also appeared in popular American television series such as 'Baretta', 'The Streets of San Francisco', 'Charlie's Angels', 'Dynasty', and 'Baywatch' until a Western film injury ended his career in 1997. Lawson was later diagnosed with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), which includes chronic bronchitis and emphysema and results in breathing difficulties. Smoking significantly increases the risk of developing COPD. Lawson continued smoking until his diagnosis, and his wife Susan noted: 'He knew cigarettes had a hold on him. He knew, but he still couldn't stop.' He leaves behind his wife, six children, eighteen grandchildren, and eleven great-grandchildren. Wayne McLaren later expressed regret over promoting cigarettes, became an anti-smoking advocate, and testified in favor of anti-smoking laws. Marlboro’s parent company initially denied his involvement in their ads, but McLaren produced documentation to prove it. After David McLean's death, his family filed a wrongful death lawsuit against Philip Morris, alleging the company encouraged smoking, leading to his cancer. These events inspired fictionalized versions in works like the satirical novel 'Thank You for Smoking.'

Li se youn nan omwen senk moun ki te fè piblisite pou sigarèt Marlboro epi ki te mouri ak maladi ki gen rapò ak fimen. Lòt yo enkli David Millar, Marlboro Man ane 1950 yo, ki te mouri ak anfimaz an 1987; David McLean, ki te mouri ak kansè poumon an 1995; Wayne McLaren, ansyen kavalye rodeo ak militan kont fimen, ki te mouri ak kansè poumon an 1992 anvan li te gen 52 an; epi Dick Hammer, ponpye ak aktè ki te nan seri televizyon 'Emergency!', ki te mouri ak kansè poumon a laj 69 an an 1999. Lawson, ki te kòmanse fimen depi li te gen 14 an, te entèprete Marlboro Man ant 1978 ak 1981. Li te mouri lakay li nan San Luis Obispo, Kalifòni, le 10 janvye, dapre sa madanm li Susan konfime. Evènman sa yo menm te enspire liv satirik tankou 'Thank You for Smoking.'

article_content: City Developments Limited (CDL), controlled by billionaire Kwek Leng Beng, and its joint venture partners have submitted the top bid of S$968 million (about US$715 million) for a residential site in Toa Payoh, a district in north-central Singapore. This move is aimed at replenishing CDL's landbank to meet strong demand for housing in the city. If the government awards the site to the consortium, they plan to build two 40-story residential towers with approximately 800 units on a 15,743-square-meter plot, offering future residents panoramic views of the nearby MacRitchie Reservoir. CDL will hold a 50% stake in the development, while Thailand's Frasers Property, owned by billionaire Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi, and Japan's Sekisui House will each take a 25% stake. Sherman Kwek, group CEO of CDL, said in a statement, 'Considering the limited new home supply in the vicinity, our development will offer homeowners an attractive opportunity to reside in a mature town with excellent connectivity and various amenities. Together with our partners, we look forward to leveraging our expertise to create an iconic project in the sought-after Toa Payoh estate.' The Toa Payoh site is one of three locations auctioned during the final government land sales of the year. Singapore has been increasing the release of residential sites to help moderate the country’s record home prices. Private housing prices have increased by about 3.9% so far this year, following an 8.6% rise in 2022. Among the three sites, the plot at Clementi Avenue 1 in western Singapore (13,451 square meters) attracted the most interest, with six bids. The top bid of S$633.4 million was submitted by MCL Land, a Hongkong Land unit, in partnership with CSC Land, part of China State Construction Engineering Corp. Additionally, MCL Land and its partner Sinarmas Land, controlled by Indonesia's Widjaja family, also submitted the highest bid of S$692.39 million for a 25,039-square-meter site in Pine Grove, within the affluent Bukit Timah area.

Sa a se yon efò pou CDL ranfòse rezèv teren li pou satisfè gwo demann pou lojman nan vil la. CDL ap kenbe 50% pati nan devlopman an, pandan Frasers Property (soti Thailand, ki posede pa milyadè Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi) ak Sekisui House (Japon) ap chak pran 25%. After Margaret Thatcher's funeral at St Paul’s Cathedral, Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip extended their condolences to the Thatcher family. The royal couple interacted with Carol and Sir Mark Thatcher, as well as Sir Mark’s wife Sarah, their children Amanda and Michael, and Carol’s partner Marco Grass, providing comfort in their time of loss.

The funeral was significant as it was the first by a British monarch for a national leader since Churchill’s in 1965. During the ceremony, Amanda Thatcher, Margaret Thatcher’s 19-year-old granddaughter, gave a heartfelt reading from Ephesians 6:10-18, a Bible passage chosen by her grandmother. Amanda, speaking with an American accent, showed poise during the reading as she addressed the audience of dignitaries, former Prime Ministers, and the Queen, supported by her brother Michael and family.

Amanda studies in Richmond, Virginia, and is celebrated for her academics and athletics, including leadership roles and choir participation. Her brother Michael, who also lives in the US, graduated in chemistry from Texas A&M and is known for his sports accomplishments and conservative community work. The siblings both reside with their mother Diane Beckett, Sir Mark’s former spouse, in Dallas, Texas, but traveled to the UK for the ceremony.

Music and hymns representing facets of Lady Thatcher’s life were featured at the funeral, as per her wishes. Following the service, the family, including Sir Mark, Sarah, Michael, Amanda, Carol, and Marco Grass, attended a reception at the Lord Mayor’s residence for further remembrance among close friends.

Amanda’s reading touched on spiritual resilience, aligning with the values Margaret Thatcher embodied. The day was marked by expressions of grief and public sympathy, with the Queen’s gesture highlighting the nation's respect for the former Prime Minister and her family.

article_content: Burt Shavitz, recognized as the bearded face on Burt’s Bees products, did not leave the company solely because he disliked the corporate environment in North Carolina, contrary to widespread belief. Instead, Shavitz states he was removed by his co-founder, Roxanne Quimby, following a romantic involvement with a younger employee. In the end, his departure left him with 37 acres of land in Maine and a confidential financial settlement, though it cost him his place in the company known for its natural-care items. Now, Shavitz lives quietly in the Maine countryside, leading a simple life far from the multi-million-dollar business that Quimby would eventually sell. The two parted ways after the business moved to North Carolina in 1994, and Shavitz doesn’t dwell on their disagreements, instead highlighting that he has no regrets and appreciates his independence. Shavitz’s life story is featured in 'Burt’s Buzz,' a new documentary screening in several U.S. cities. The film contrasts his yearning for a peaceful, solitary life with the fame that made him a corporate symbol, complete with stays in high-end hotels for promotional events, despite his preference for quiet moments watching wildlife. Once, Shavitz and Quimby had a partnership based on practical creativity—she used his beeswax to create products, while his image with a wild beard became the brand’s symbol. Their collaboration dissolved as the company outgrew its small-scale roots, with Quimby taking a leading role and later stating that everyone, including Burt, was handled generously in the company’s sale. Shavitz, for his part, felt he was only a stepping stone for her ambitions. At 79, Shavitz still gets by with few comforts—sometimes no hot water—and finds happiness in the company of his golden retrievers and the animals that roam his land. Despite his brief stint as a business celebrity, he’s content with what he has, holding land and self-reliance above wealth or recognition. Documentary director Jody Shapiro spent a year following Shavitz and sees him as genuinely complex: a man at ease with selling honey, uninterested in status or material gain. Shavitz often reiterates that he never sought luxury, trophies, or social climbing—he already had the life he wanted with his beloved land.
translated_content: Burt Shavitz, ki se figi ak bab pwodwi Burt's Bees yo, pa kite konpayi an sèlman paske li pa t renmen mond biznis North Carolina a, kontrèman ak sa anpil moun panse. Olye de sa, Shavitz di Roxanne Quimby, ko-fondatè a, te mete l deyò apre li te gen yon relasyon ak yon anplwaye ki pi jèn. Lè li te kite konpayi an, li te resevwa 37 kawo tè nan Maine ak yon sòm lajan li pa bay non, men li pèdi plas li nan konpayi ki pi popilè ak pwodwi natirèl yo. Jodi a, Shavitz ap viv trankil nan zòn riral Maine, lwen tout bri ak gwo biznis ke Quimby te vann pou anpil lajan. Yo te separe apre konpayi an te deplase nan North Carolina an 1994. Shavitz pa ap pale anpil de dezakò a, li di li pa gen regrè epi li apresye libète li. Istwa lavi Shavitz prezante nan dokimantè 'Burt’s Buzz,' ki ap pase nan plizyè vil Ozetazini. Fim nan montre kontradiksyon ant dezi Shavitz pou yon vi senp ak trankil ak popilarite li kòm figi yon gwo konpayi, kote li te konn fè vwayaj nan otèl liks pou pwomosyon, menm si li pi renmen gade bèt nan lanati lakay li. Yon fwa, Shavitz ak Quimby te travay ansanm: Quimby te sèvi ak sir myèl li pou fè pwodwi, epi figi li ak bab li te tounen mak konpayi an. Patenarya a fini lè konpayi an vin twò gwo, Quimby pran direksyon, epi li di tout moun, enkli Burt, te byen trete lè li te vann konpayi an. Shavitz menm santi li te sèlman yon etap pou Quimby atenn objektif li yo. Kounye a li gen 79 an, li viv senp—pafwa pa menm dlo cho—e li kontan ak chen Golden Retriever li ak tout bèt kap mache sou tè li. Malgre li te vin yon figi popilè pou yon ti tan, kontantman li se viv sou tè pa li, li bay endepandans plis valè pase lajan oswa t’ap chache ranje. Reyalis dokimantè a, Jody Shapiro, ki te swiv Shavitz pandan yon ane, dekri li kòm yon nonm senp men konplike: li alèz ap vann myèl, li pa kouri dèyè siksè oswa richès. Shavitz remèsye tan li ap viv depi lontan: li pa janm te anvi chèche lavi luxurious oswa monte nan klas sosyal; li te deja genyen sa li te vle—tè li.

article_content: Strong winds and dry conditions ignited a wave of wildfires across large regions of northern, central, and western Texas on Sunday, officials from the Texas Forest Service reported. Around 15,000 acres were consumed by fires statewide, with the most severe blazes near Midland and the Panhandle city of Amarillo. Meteorologists observed wind gusts reaching up to 69 miles per hour in these areas. Lewis Kearney, spokesperson for the Texas State Lone Star Incident Management Team, said that while no fatalities occurred, a significant number of homes in west Texas were lost. He highlighted that the high winds hampered efforts to control the fires using aircraft, and predicted that since these conditions would likely last into Monday, complete containment might be delayed. On Sunday afternoon, the National Weather Service reported mandatory evacuations in northeast Potter County at 2:32 p.m. Central Time, soon followed by additional orders in Borger about half an hour later. Fires also burned between 30 and 800 acres in counties including Haskell, Mitchell, Howard, Randall, and Tom Green throughout the day.

Lewis Kearney, pòtpawòl Texas State Lone Star Incident Management Team, di pa gen okenn lanmò rapòte men anpil kay boule nèt nan lwès Texas. Li te di gwo van yo rann li difisil pou itilize avyon pou konbat dife yo, e li prevwa menm kondisyon yo ap kontinye jiskaske Lendi, kidonk dife yo ka pran plis tan pou kontwole. Dimanch apre-midi, Sèvis Meteyo Nasyonal te bay lòd evakyasyon obligatwa nan nòdwès Potter County a 2:32 p.m. (lè santral), ak lòt lòd evakyasyon ki swiv Borger apeprè demi èdtan apre. Plizyè dife boule ant 30 ak 800 kawo tè atravè konte Haskell, Mitchell, Howard, Randall, ak Tom Green.

article_content: Dan Dotson, the well-known auctioneer from the TV show Storage Wars, is recovering after emergency surgery for a double brain aneurysm. Dotson, who is in his early 60s and reportedly worth $3.5 million, collapsed at his California home earlier this week. His wife and co-star, Laura Dotson, performed CPR with assistance from a 911 dispatcher and then rushed him to the hospital. Doctors discovered one aneurysm behind his eye and another, the size of an apricot, in his neck. Initially, doctors gave him a 4 to 20 percent chance of survival. Dotson had emergency surgery on Tuesday and is said to be making good progress. On Thursday night, Laura updated fans on Twitter, saying he had 'made it through a difficult surgery' and was 'now on the road to recovery.' Just before the incident, the Dotsons celebrated Father's Day with their son, and Dan posted a family photo on Twitter. The couple has been famous since 2010 for their appearances on Storage Wars, a reality show centered on bidding for storage unit contents.

A young child was rescued by airport workers after climbing onto a baggage conveyor belt at Santiago International Airport in Chile last Thursday. A video shared on social media, which has accumulated over 800,000 views, shows the boy climbing onto the conveyor system behind an unattended check-in desk. The scene, reminiscent of 'Toy Story 2' as noted by the video’s soundtrack, depicts the child traveling through a restricted airport area. Security camera footage captures various angles of the incident as the child moves along the belt. The unnamed child appears calm and unworried during the event. Fortunately, attentive airport staff stopped the conveyor belt and safely picked up the child before any harm occurred. 

In a statement to the Chilean newspaper La Tercera, airport authorities affirmed that their facilities meet all international security standards, with systems like cameras and detectors installed. The airport also noted that airline personnel are responsible for ensuring the proper and safe operation of infrastructure. They stated they are gathering information to understand how the incident happened and plan to strengthen safety measures with airline operators, emphasizing the importance of parental and caregiver supervision.

This incident follows similar events at US airports. In 2019, a two-year-old boy suffered a fractured hand after getting onto a baggage belt at Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport. In 2021, a nine-year-old was unharmed after ending up in a baggage system at Minneapolis-St Paul Airport, according to Simple Flying.

article_content: Dr. Bobbi Lancaster, a transgender golfer from Arizona, is preparing for a significant moment in her career after qualifying for the Ladies Professional Golf Association (LPGA) tour. She credits golf with helping her cope with her identity struggles before undergoing gender reassignment surgery in 2010. At 63 years old, Dr. Lancaster, who was born Robert Lancaster, will become the first transgender competitor in an LPGA tournament since the association changed its policies just over three years ago. Following a challenging season where Dr. Lancaster felt under scrutiny, she now feels mentally ready for the tournament. 'I really feel like I'm in a much better place emotionally now where I can bring my best game and compete,' she told ABC News. Dr. Lancaster's journey includes decades of internal conflict, marriage, raising three children, and ultimately finding acceptance. She first sensed she wanted to be a girl at age six. 'I was confused and I didn't know why I had these feelings,' she shared with 12 News. 'I didn't know who to talk to about it.' Despite her struggles, Dr. Lancaster met and married her second wife, Lucy. After falling into depression and considering suicide, the discovery of a note by her wife gave her the courage to move forward, bolstered by Lucy's support. Golf has remained important throughout Dr. Lancaster's life, both before and after her transition. She had gender reassignment surgery in 2010 and notes, 'Nothing really changed. I still have the same heart.' She acknowledges standing out among younger competitors but provided medical evidence to the LPGA showing her hormone levels are comparable to other female players. Her surgery also reduced muscle mass, helping to level the playing field, according to AZ Central. The LPGA has supported her, with senior vice-president Heather Daly-Donofrio expressing support once required paperwork and test results were submitted. Dr. Lancaster now looks forward to proving herself after qualifying for the Symetra Tour in 2014. She told USA Today, 'I feel I have made great strides and am excited about the 2014 competitive year.' Lancaster added that hearing from hundreds of people inspired by her story has been the most rewarding part: 'I felt I was making a difference and healing in many situations.'

Nan laj 63 an, Dr. Lancaster, ki te fèt kòm Robert Lancaster, ap vin premye jwè transjan ki patisipe nan yon tounwa LPGA depi asosyasyon an te modifye règ li yo plis pase twa zan de sa. Apre yon sezon difisil kote Dr. Lancaster te santi tout je sou li, li di li pare mantalman pou konpetisyon an. 'Kounye a, mwen santi mwen pi byen nan tèt mwen e mwen ka bay pi bon jwèt mwen,' li te di ak ABC News. Istwa Dr. Lancaster gen ladann plizyè deseni ap batay ak tèt li, maryaj, leve twa pitit, pou finalman li jwenn akseptasyon. Li te gen sis an lè li te kòmanse santi li vle tounen tifi. 'Mwen te konfonn e mwen pa t konnen poukisa mwen t ap santi sa yo,' li eksplike ak 12 News. 'Mwen pa t konnen kiyès pou m te pale ak yo sou sa.' Malgre sa, Dr. Lancaster te rankontre e marye ak dezyèm madanm li, Lucy. Lè li te tonbe depresyon epi menm panse pou mete fen nan lavi li, madanm li te jwenn nòt swisid li a. Apre sa, li te jwenn kouraj avanse, gras ak sipò Lucy. Gòl te toujou enpòtan pou Dr. Lancaster, anvan ak apre tranzisyon li. Apre operasyon an an 2010, li di: 'Anyen pa vrèman chanje. Kè mwen toujou menm.' Li rekonèt li diferan ak lòt jwè ki pi jèn yo, men li te bay LPGA prèv medikal ki montre nivo òmòn li menm ak lòt fanm jwè. Operasyon an tou diminye mas mis li, sa ki fè konpetisyon an vin pi jist, dapre AZ Central. LPGA te sipòte li, ak vis-prezidant Heather Daly-Donofrio ki te bay tout kolaborasyon apre tout dokiman ak rezilta laboratwa fin remet. Lancaster ajoute repons moun ki te enspire pa istwa li se pati ki pi bèl: 'Mwen pote chanjman epi ede moun jwenn gerizon nan anpil sitiyasyon.'

article_content:
Sharks have often been considered among the most primitive fish. However, new research on a 415-million-year-old fossil challenges the belief that sharks are the original model for modern jawed vertebrates. While modern sharks have internal skeletons made of cartilage without any bony armor on their faces, the fossilized fish Janusiscus reveals that the earliest ancestors of both bony fishes and cartilaginous fishes like sharks likely had well-developed external skeletons. This finding suggests sharks are not as primitive as once thought.

Researchers from the University of Oxford and Imperial College London used X-ray and CT scans to examine the Janusiscus fossil’s skull and braincase. They found that the internal structure resembled cartilaginous fish like sharks and rays, but the skull also showed characteristics typical of bony fish. This unique combination of features led to its name: Janusiscus, inspired by the two-faced Roman god Janus.

Although intact braincases from this era are rare, Dr. Martin Brazeau of Imperial College London emphasized that fossils like Janusiscus should not be seen as 'missing links.' He suggests that understanding evolution is more like assembling a family tree than finding sequential steps on a ladder. Every new discovery helps put earlier findings into clearer context.

Previously, Janusiscus was incorrectly grouped with bony fishes (osteichthyans), which include familiar species like cod, tuna, and all land vertebrates. The new analysis reveals it also shares characteristics with early sharks, indicating both groups’ ancestors had bony skeletons. Modern sharks, therefore, likely lost their bones later in their evolutionary history.

Dr. Matt Friedman of Oxford University explained that Janusiscus provides a rare glimpse into the ‘Age of Fishes,’ a time when vertebrates were rapidly diversifying. The fossil shows that the earliest jawed vertebrates combined features from both bony and cartilaginous fish branches and also had some primitive traits.

Janusiscus was discovered in Siberia in 1972 and is stored at the Tallinn University of Technology in Estonia. Dr. Brazeau recognized its significance for uncovering early vertebrate evolution. Although Janusiscus has a bony skull, it lacks other key features typical of bony fish and also lacks a braincase division seen in early bony fishes and sharks, placing it at an early evolutionary stage before these groups diverged.

This discovery redefines our understanding of sharks, showing they are not simply 'frozen' at a primitive stage of evolution, but have a much more complex evolutionary history.

article_content: NEW ORLEANS, Louisiana (CNN) — Some of the best performances at the New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival happen far from the official Fairgrounds, long after the headline acts wrap up and the crowds have dispersed. On one late night, after Bonerama—an energetic brass-funk rock band fronted by three trombones—finished a rousing 90-minute set that opened with a soulful original by bandleader Mark Mullins and closed with a trombone-powered cover of Hendrix's 'Crosstown Traffic,' the real magic began. At 1:18 a.m., the crowd parted as a dozen musicians in black shirts paraded into the room: the Midnite Disturbers, a Jazz Fest supergroup whose rare performances are local legends. Each member of the Midnite Disturbers typically leads their own band and is seldom in town at the same time, making their shows as uncommon as a lunar eclipse. Founded by friends and drummers Stanton Moore and Kevin O'Day after Hurricane Katrina, the group arose from the idea to assemble the best horn players they knew. Their black shirts feature names in red—'Listen to: Smokey Johnson... Brian O'Neill... Henry "Red" Allen'—in tribute to the masters and mentors of New Orleans music who paved the way. Although most of these jazz greats are little known outside the Crescent City, their influence on the city's sound is profound. Today’s Midnite Disturbers include up-and-coming talents like Troy Andrews and Shamarr Allen, along with veterans from Bonerama, Galactic, and other acclaimed groups. By the end of their set, their shirts are drenched with sweat, a testament to the intensity of their performance. Trumpeter Shamarr Allen described the experience as an honor and a challenge, requiring each musician to listen closely and find their place among so much talent. "That's the beauty of it," he said. "It's about sounding good together, having fun, entertaining the crowd, and all staying in sync. If I'm not one of the top guys yet, I'm on my way." The Midnite Disturbers played an official Jazz Fest show at 5:55 p.m. on Saturday—but as always, their impromptu late-night appearance was the one people will talk about until they gather again.

Yon swa, apre Bonerama—yon bann brass-funk rock ak twa trombòn devan—fini yon show 90 minit plen enèji, yo te kòmanse ak yon mizik orijinal emosyonèl pa lidè yo, Mark Mullins, epi fini ak yon vèsyon Jimi Hendrix 'Crosstown Traffic', kote trombòn yo pase nan pedal wah-wah, se la bagay yo vin pi cho. A 1:18 nan maten, foul la louvri wout pou yon douzèn mizisyen ak mayo nwa rantre: Midnite Disturbers yo, yon supergroupe Jazz Fest ki ra anpil epi ki deja tounen lejand lakay yo. Growing worries about border security led a Chinese envoy to meet with senior officials in Myanmar’s capital to address stability issues.

Yunnan provincial authorities stated the drills would take place in the vicinity of Manghai, Manling, and Qingshuihe villages, running through November 28. Myanmar’s military spokesperson, Zaw Min Tun, confirmed that Myanmar was notified ahead of time about the military exercises.

A groundbreaking animated series from Pakistan, 'Burka Avenger', challenges stereotypes by featuring a female superhero who dons a burqa to champion girls' education and tackle social issues. The heroine, Jiya, is a schoolteacher by day and transforms into the Burka Avenger at night, using her mastery of Takht Kabbadi—a unique martial art where books and pens are weapons—to defend girls’ schools from those seeking to close them.

The series is the creation of Pakistani pop singer Haroon, motivated by attacks on educational institutions by extremists. Haroon told CNN his goal is to use art to convey positive social messages, especially focusing on the significance of education and women's rights. He highlights that Jiya’s burqa is a deliberate choice to keep her identity secret, symbolizing empowerment rather than oppression.

'Burka Avenger' features music by notable South Asian artists: rapper Adil Omar wrote 'Lady in Black,' while rock musician Ali Azmat performs 'Baba Bandook,' a song about a key antagonist in the show. Comprising 13 episodes, the series touches on discrimination, child labor, sectarian violence, energy shortages, and environmental preservation, all presented in an entertaining blend of adventure and comedy.

Haroon aspires for the show to reach children without access to bedtime stories or books at home. Each episode concludes with the Burka Avenger offering a moral lesson, helping to instill strong values. The cartoon is set to premiere in mid-August, following the Muslim festival of Eid ul Fitr.

Li mete aksan sou jan Jiya chwazi mete burka a pou kache idantite li, kòm yon senbòl pisans olye de opresyon.

'Burka Avenger' prezante mizik pa kèk gran atis Sid Azi: rapè Adil Omar ekri 'Lady in Black,' epi mizisyen wòch Ali Azmat chante 'Baba Bandook,' yon chante sou youn nan prensipal opozan nan emisyon an. Seri a genyen 13 epizòd; li pale de diskriminasyon, travay timoun, vyolans relijye, mank kouran, ak pwoteksyon anviwònman — tout sa avèk avantur epi komed.

Haroon swete emisyon an ap rive jwenn timoun ki pa gen aksè ak istwa oswa liv lakay yo. Chak epizòd fini ak Burka Avenger ki bay leson moral, pou ede timoun yo devlope bon valè. Desen an pral lanse nan mitan Out, apre fèt relijye Eid ul Fitr.

Officials from the U.S. Navy, the NCAA, and Morale Entertainment are in discussions to organize a historic college basketball game onboard the aircraft carrier USS Carl Vinson. The Carl Vinson, notable for its key roles in recent U.S. military efforts—including launching initial airstrikes in Afghanistan after September 11 and serving as the ship from which Osama bin Laden was buried at sea—may soon become the first carrier to host an NCAA basketball game.

Though the final agreement is pending, the proposed event, promoted by Morale Entertainment, features the Michigan State Spartans facing the University of North Carolina Tar Heels on Veterans Day, November 11, atop the carrier's deck at the U.S. naval base in San Diego, likely around 4 p.m. PT. 'Discussions are ongoing,' said Cmdr. Danny Hernandez, U.S. Navy spokesperson. 'If we reach a final agreement, we look forward to the opportunity this event presents for our Navy and our veterans. We're still reviewing the proposal.'

Dubbed the 'Carrier Classic,' this would be ESPN's first televised college basketball game of the season, should the arrangements be finalized. Organizing the game poses unique challenges: the outdoor flight deck exposes players and fans to potential wind, rain, or sunshine not found in typical indoor arenas. To accommodate, two courts will be constructed—one on the flight deck, and a contingency court below in the sheltered hangar deck. Fabric shielding will help block wind on the upper deck, and a professional lighting crew may be brought in to ensure adequate visibility for players and television cameras. The ship will be moored to minimize sun-in-the-eyes for players.

Security measures will be extensive, given the ship’s status as a vital Navy asset. Around 7,000 fans could attend, but public ticket sales are not planned; instead, tickets will primarily go to UNC and MSU, some sponsors, youth coaches, and especially military service members, veterans, and their families. Personalized tickets will be used to prevent scalping, and each attendee must present matching ID at entry.

ESPN and the event promoters must also prepare for the possibility that the Carl Vinson could be deployed on short notice. The setup—including courts and seating—must be capable of rapid removal, a process tested to be possible within 24 to 36 hours, using existing aircraft tie-downs rather than permanent fixtures.

The idea for a carrier basketball game originated at Michigan State, championed by Athletic Director Mark Hollis and coach Tim Izzo. Izzo, reflecting on his experiences visiting U.S. troops, highlighted the symbolic significance for athletes and service members alike.

Over recent days, Navy officials have conducted thorough discussions and tours with the NCAA, Morale Entertainment, ESPN, and the San Diego Sports Commission to explore practical aspects and potential challenges.

Adding to the game’s appeal, former UNC star Michael Jordan and former MSU star Magic Johnson have been named honorary team captains. If successful, organizers hope to arrange additional carrier-based games, possibly including women’s teams like Notre Dame and Ohio State in future matchups.

article_content: A Wake County judge declined to lower the bail for Timothy Dwayne Tutterrow, a 46-year-old ride operator charged with three felony counts of assault after five people were injured at the North Carolina State Fair. Tutterrow’s attorney, Roger Smith Jr., maintained that Tutterrow is not a flight risk, but Judge Keith Gregory kept bail at $225,000, though noting the matter could be revisited. Tutterrow’s next court date is scheduled for November 18. Authorities allege that safety features on the Vortex ride were deliberately bypassed, said Sheriff Donnie Harrison. The incident occurred when the ride restarted while passengers were getting off, resulting in injuries to five people, among them a ride attendant. Three survivors remained hospitalized at WakeMed in Raleigh as of Sunday; two others had been released. The injured individuals ranged from 14 to 39 years old and included members of the same family. Tutterrow is an independent contractor hired to operate the Vortex, the only ride his firm supplied at the fair. District Attorney Colon Wiloughby noted the case remains under investigation and it is unclear if others may face charges. Labor Department spokeswoman Dolores Quesenberry reminded that operators must perform daily system checks and log the results.

Avoka Tutterrow, Roger Smith Jr., fè konnen kliyan li pa gen risk pou kouri. Men Jij Keith Gregory te kenbe kosyon an nan $225,000, byenke li di ka a kapab revize pita. Pwochèn odyans Tutterrow fikse pou 18 novanm. Otorite yo di yo kwè mekanis sekirite sou atraksyon Vortex la te sabote volontèman, dapre Cherif Donnie Harrison. Ensidan an rive lè atraksyon an te rekòmanse pandan moun t ap desann, sa lakoz senk viktim blese, pami yo yon anplwaye atraksyon an. Twa moun te toujou nan lopital WakeMed nan Raleigh dimanch la; de lòt yo te deja soti. Moun ki blese yo gen laj ant 14 ak 39 an e pifò se manm yon sèl fanmi. article_content: A month into work stoppages, car shoppers are beginning to feel the effects of the United Auto Workers union's historic strike against all three major Detroit automakers. The latest inventory data from Cars.com, which tracks vehicles impacted by the strike, shows that mid-size pickup trucks are in especially short supply. According to Cars.com, Ford Ranger inventory fell 45.3% through October 15, while the Chevrolet Colorado dropped by 50.3% and the GMC Canyon by 43%. These three models have been affected since the UAW strike started on September 15, highlighting the extent of the now 33-day work stoppage’s impact. Overall vehicle availability at Ford, General Motors (GM), and Stellantis has also declined. As of Monday, Stellantis’ inventory was down 11.9%, Ford’s down 6.2%, and GM’s down 15.7%. Before the UAW’s recent work stoppage at Ford’s Kentucky Truck Plant, GM had been the hardest hit by the UAW's walkouts. Cars.com Editor-in-Chief Jenni Newman advised those shopping for vehicles impacted by the strike to act quickly if a certain model is their preference. Vehicles in short supply and high demand generally move quickly and dealers become less likely to negotiate on price. "If you have your heart set on a vehicle being affected by the strike, you should move quickly," Newman told Insider. She noted that the longer work stoppages last, the scarcer both inventory and deals are likely to get. For shoppers open on brand, now could be the time to consider Detroit’s competition, Newman noted. Ford executive chairman Bill Ford recently commented to workers that competitors are gaining an advantage from the strike. "Toyota, Honda, Tesla, and others are loving this strike because they know the longer it goes on, the better it is for them," he said Monday. In response to Ford's comments, the UAW stressed that its dispute is not with automakers like Ford, Honda, or Tesla, but with 'corporate greed.' "Workers at Tesla, Toyota, Honda, and others are not the enemy—they’re the UAW members of the future," UAW President Shawn Fain stated. Whether the strike will cause the Detroit Three to lose customers to competitors remains to be seen, Newman said. Competition is particularly strong in the mid-size pickup market, where Ford and GM are most affected. The Toyota Tacoma already leads Detroit’s smaller pickups, with nearly 180,000 units sold through September, compared to Ford’s 31,503 Rangers, GM’s 58,685 Colorados, and 19,351 Canyons. A shortage of Ford and GM small pickups may push some buyers to other brands, Newman said, but Cars.com surveys show that some buyers intend to support union-made brands in solidarity. Previous surveys indicate public support for the UAW strike is at a record high. Cars.com found that 31% of union-affiliated households are now considering UAW-built vehicles to support the union's efforts, while 15% of all respondents are considering American brands and 8% have lost interest in these brands due to the strike. "We’re seeing growing awareness of the strike, and it’s affecting buying decisions," Newman said.

Selon Cars.com, kantite Ford Ranger bese 45.3% jis 15 Oktòb, pandan Chevrolet Colorado desann 50.3% ak GMC Canyon desann 43%. Twa modèl sa yo afekte depi grev UAW la te kòmanse 15 septanm, sa ki montre enpak total 33 jou grev la. An jeneral, kantite machin ki disponib nan Ford, General Motors (GM), ak Stellantis diminye tou. Lendi sa, envantè Stellantis tonbe 11.9%, Ford bese 6.2%, epi GM bese 15.7%. Anvan grev resan nan faktori Ford Kentucky Truck la, se GM ki te plis afekte pa grèv UAW yo. Chèf editè Cars.com, Jenni Newman, konseye achtè ki enterese nan machin ki afekte pa grev la pou yo aji rapid si yo gen yon modèl espesyal nan tèt yo. Machin ki ra epi ki mande anpil vann rapid epi negosyasyon pri difisil. "Si ou reyèlman vle yon machin ki afekte pa grev la, fè vit," Newman di Insider. Li te ajoute, plis grev la dire, se plis machin ak of yo ap sibi rarite. Si w fleksib sou mak la, Newman di kounye a ka bon moman pou konsidere konpetitè Detroit yo. Prezidan egzekitif Ford, Bill Ford, di bay anplwaye yo konpetitè yo ap tire avantaj nan grev la. "Toyota, Honda, Tesla, ak lòt yo fyè de grev la paske yo konnen plis li kontinye, se pi bon sa ye pou yo," li deklare Lendi. Pou reponn deklarasyon Ford la, UAW mete aksan sou sa ke lit la se pa ak Ford, Honda oswa Tesla, men se ak 'grangou korporasyon'. "Travayè Tesla, Toyota, Honda, ak lòt yo pa lènmi—se manm UAW nan lavni," Prezidan UAW Shawn Fain deklare. Rete wè si grev la ap fè twa gwo Detroit yo pèdi kliyan bay konpetitè, Newman di. Gen gwo konpetisyon mwa sa yo nan mache kamyonèt mitan-gwosè kote Ford ak GM pi afekte. Toyota Tacoma deja depase ti kamyon Detroit yo ak prèske 180,000 inite vann jis rive septanm, pandan Ford vann 31,503 Rangers, GM vann 58,685 Colorados ak 19,351 Canyons. Mank ti kamyon Ford ak GM ka pouse kèk achte lòt mak, Newman di. Men sondaj Cars.com montre gen moun ki vle sipòte mak sendikal pa solidarite. Sondaj deja montre sipò piblik pou grev la trè wo. Cars.com jwenn 31% fanmi ki gen afilyasyon sendikal panse achte machin UAW pou sipòte sendika a, 15% nan tout repondan apiye mak Ameriken, epi 8% pa enterese ak mak sa yo akoz grev la. "Nou remake moun vin pi konsyan de grev la epi sa ap enfliyanse desizyon achte yo," Newman di.
