article_content: Kerber’s Farm has brought its renowned farm-to-table offerings from Huntington, Long Island, to a new retail shop in Manhattan’s West Village. Known for pies, biscuits, muffins, and scones, the shop is the latest venture by owner Nick Voulgaris, who grew up visiting Kerber’s Farm with his family. After the original owners retired and the farm closed, Voulgaris purchased and revived the property in 2013, using personal investments, including Apple stock, to finance the $575,000 acquisition. Originally focused on poultry, Kerber’s Farm now emphasizes sustainable practices—raising chickens for eggs and keeping bees for honey. Major renovations transformed the farmstand into a destination for breakfast, lunch, coffee, snacks, pies, and sometimes dinner, moving away from poultry processing. According to Voulgaris, 'the bees provide honey, the vegetables feed the chickens, and the chickens lay eggs.' Baked goods remain central, with pies, cheddar buttermilk biscuits, muffins, and scones. After restoring the Huntington location and seeing increased profits, Voulgaris invested around $300,000 to self-finance a New York City outpost, which opened in February 2023. Living in the West Village, he selected a storefront on Bleecker Street, surrounded by other classic food shops like Murray’s Cheese and Rocco’s Bakery. The West Village store is open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., with later hours on weekends, and offers dinner items such as chicken pot pie pockets, pulled pork pockets, shepherd's pies, and vegan options. Delivery services via DoorDash and Grubhub make up only 7-8% of sales. Kerber’s Farm employs a staff of creative professionals—actors, writers, dancers—who are drawn to a flexible and supportive work environment. Turnover is common, but Voulgaris attributes this to the creative backgrounds of employees. An open mic night suggested by staff, featuring readings and skits, became a monthly event due to its popularity. Yelp reviews for the Bleecker Street shop are mostly positive. Jungwon from Boston praised the breakfast sandwich’s biscuits, Trevor from Brooklyn enjoyed the chicken pot pie pocket, while Jaimee from Manhattan thought the s’mores pie was too sweet. Voulgaris says many customers are drawn by the shop’s nostalgic aesthetic and connection to Long Island’s history. Families prefer the Huntington location, which features animals, while the West Village shop appeals mainly to younger locals. Voulgaris is the author of several nonfiction books, with his latest titled 'On the Water.' He encourages customers to use the shop as a home-like space to work remotely and notes that most laptop users leave during busy weekend hours, keeping the store accessible. Looking forward, Voulgaris is considering a third location, possibly on the East End of Long Island. He credits the business’s success to maintaining food quality and resisting fleeting dining trends, even as 'farm to table' becomes a common phrase.
translated_content: Kerber's Farm mennen manje fre dirèkteman soti nan fèm lan nan nouvo boutik li nan West Village, Manhattan. Boutik sa a, ki gen repitasyon pou tòti, biskwit, muffin ak scone li yo, se dènye pwojè pwopriyetè Nick Voulgaris, ki te konn vizite Kerber’s Farm ak fanmi li depi li te piti. Lè ansyen pwopriyetè yo te pran retrèt ak fèm lan te fèmen, Voulgaris te achte epi relanse li an 2013, itilize pwòp lajan li, enkli lajan li te resevwa nan aksyon Apple, pou finanse acha a ($575,000). Okòmansman, Kerber's Farm te konsantre sou vola, men kounye a li mete aksan sou pratik dirab—leve poul pou ze ak kenbe myèl pou siwo myèl. Gwo chanjman te transfòme fèm lan vin yon kote pou manje maten, manje midi, kafe, ti goute, tòti ak pafwa dine, san batay vola ankò. Dapre Voulgaris, 'myèl bay siwo myèl, legim nouri poul yo, epi poul yo lay ze.' Tòti, biskwit cheddar ak buttermilk, muffin ak scone yo toujou esansyèl. Apre li fin restore Kerber’s nan Huntington, benefis yo ogmante e Voulgaris envesti apeprè $300,000 pou l louvri lokal New York City a an fevriye 2023. Kòm li te abite nan West Village, li chwazi yon lokal sou Bleecker Street, bò kote klasik boutik manje tankou Murray’s Cheese ak Rocco’s Bakery. Boutik West Village lan louvri 7 a.m. rive 8 p.m., epi pi ta nan wikenn, ofri dine tankou chicken pot pie pockets, pulled pork pockets, shepherd's pies ak opsyon vejetalyen. Sèvis livrezon DoorDash ak Grubhub se sèlman 7-8% nan lavant yo. Kerber’s Farm anplwaye pwofesyonèl kreyatif—aktè, ekriven, dansè—ki apresye fleksibilite ak bon tretman. Moun souvan kite aprè yon ane oswa de, men Voulgaris eksplike sa akoz nati kreyatif yo. Yon anplwaye te pwopoze fè open mic night, kote pèsonèl la li tèks ak fè ti jwèt, e sa tounen yon evènman chak mwa ki gen anpil siksè. Opinyon sou Yelp pou boutik Bleecker Street lan pifò pozitif. Jungwon soti Boston felisite biskwit sandwich manje maten an, Trevor soti Brooklyn renmen chicken pot pie pocket la, pandan Jaimee soti Manhattan panse smores pie la twò dous. Voulgaris di anpil kliyan vini pou bèl dekorasyon nostaljik la ak koneksyon ak istwa Long Island. Fanmi yo pito lokal Huntington kote gen bèt, tandiske boutik West Village la atire plis jèn lokal. Voulgaris se otè plizyè liv dokimantè, dènye a rele 'On the Water.' Li ankouraje kliyan pou sèvi ak boutik la tankou lakay yo epi travay aleka, epi li di ke laptop users yo souvan ale lè boutik la vin pi okipe nan wikenn. Pou lavni, Voulgaris ap reflechi sou ouvè yon twazyèm boutik, petèt nan East End Long Island. Li kwe kle siksè se kenbe bon jan kalite manje ak pa kouri dèye dènye mòd yo, menmsi 'farm to table' tounen yon fraz popilè.

article_content: National Museum Wales in Cardiff temporarily closed its front doors after demonstrators chanting "Free Palestine" entered the building and displayed Palestinian flags. The incident occurred during a pro-Palestinian march in Cardiff city centre, marking the fifth consecutive weekend of demonstrations related to the conflict in Gaza. In response, the museum apologized for any inconvenience and stated it closed the front entrance to protect the safety of visitors and staff. Museum officials provided continued access through the Reardon Smith Theatre and said the front doors would reopen once it was safe. The context of the demonstration relates to the ongoing war in Gaza. Israel launched a major military campaign in the Gaza Strip to target Hamas, which it designates as a terrorist organization, following a large-scale attack by Hamas gunmen on 7 October. According to Israeli authorities, at least 1,200 people were killed in that assault, and around 240 were taken hostage. Since the start of Israel's counteroffensive, Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry reports that about 11,400 people have been killed in Gaza. The United Nations has expressed concern over a "humanitarian disaster" in the region.

Mize a prezante eskiz pou nenpòt deranjman epi li di li te fèmen antre prensipal la pou sekirite vizitè ak anplwaye. Responsab yo te bay aksè atravè Reardon Smith Theatre epi yo di yo ap relouvri pòt devan an le sa vin sekirize. Konteks manifestasyon an gen rapò ak lagè Gaza a k ap kontinye. Izrayèl lanse yon gwo operasyon militè nan Gaza pou vize Hamas, ke li konsidere kòm yon òganizasyon teworis, apre yon gwo atak pa gwoup ame Hamas sou 7 Oktòb. Selon otorite Izrayelyen yo, omwen 1,200 moun mouri nan atak la e anviwon 240 te pran kòm otaj. Depi Izrayèl te lanse repons li, ministè sante Gaza (ki se Hamas k ap dirije) di anviwon 11,400 moun mouri nan Gaza. Nasyonzini fè konnen gen yon "katastwòf imanitè" ki ap dewoule nan zòn nan.

article_content: Plumbers conducting maintenance work accidentally started a fire that swept through The Avalon at Edgewater, a 408-unit luxury apartment complex in Edgewater, New Jersey, leaving more than 1,000 residents homeless. The blaze began on the first floor Wednesday afternoon and was under control but still smoldering more than a day later. At a press conference with Governor Chris Christie, Edgewater Police Chief William Skidmore reported that the fire ignited inside a wall during a plumbing repair. He emphasized that the cause was 'totally accidental,' with no suspicion of foul play. Authorities confirmed all residents evacuated safely. The fire destroyed 240 of the 408 units, and a state of emergency was declared by Edgewater Mayor Michael McPartland. Local schools were closed Thursday, and road access restricted. Fire Chief Thomas Jacobson noted the building’s sprinkler system functioned, but its lightweight wooden construction contributed to the rapid spread of the fire and hampered firefighting efforts. Two civilians and two firefighters sustained minor injuries. Governor Christie called the first responders' efforts 'extraordinary' and praised the lack of fatalities as 'an enormous blessing.' Emergency support services—including the Red Cross—are aiding displaced residents at the Edgewater Community Center. Three people were rescued from the burning structure, and another woman was saved as the building's facade collapsed. Resident John Sterling, New York Yankees announcer, lost his home and is currently staying at a hotel. The fire sent thick smoke visible across the Hudson River to Manhattan. Many affected residents are still seeking temporary housing. About 160 people are being sheltered at a local community center. This is not the first fire at this location. Over 14 years ago, a blaze at the same site destroyed nine homes during condominium construction. That fire’s cause was undetermined but arson was ruled out, and a jury found developer negligence contributed. AvalonBay Communities, a Virginia-based developer, managed both the current complex and the 2000 project. Authorities have cordoned off streets near the building, though no major traffic issues have been reported. The community continues to rally to support those displaced by this incident.

Dife a te kòmanse nan premye etaj la Mèkredi aprèmidi epi pa t konplètman etenn plis pase yon jou apre. Nan yon konferans pou laprès ak Gouvènè Chris Christie, Chèf Polis Edgewater William Skidmore rapòte dife a te sòti andedan yon miray pandan reparasyon plonbri. Li ensiste ke sa te 'totalman aksidan', pa gen okenn sispèk zak mechanste. Otorite yo konfime tout moun sòti an sekirite. Dife a kraze 240 sou 408 apatman yo, epi Majistra Edgewater Michael McPartland deklare eta dijans lokal. Lekòl yo te fèmen Jedi, epi aksè sou wout ekilibre. Chèf Ponpye Thomas Jacobson di sistèm espre dife a t ap mache, men estrikti bwa limyè a te rann dife a gaye rapid epi difisil pou ponpye yo te konbat. De sivil ak de ponpye blese lejèman. Gouvènè Christie felisite travay eksepsyonèl sekouris yo epi rele absans moun ki mouri 'yon gwo benediksyon.' Sèvis sipò ijans—tankou Kwazrouj—ap ede moun san kay nan Sant Kominotè Edgewater. Twa moun te sove soti andedan batiman an, epi yon lòt fanm te sove pandan fasad la t ap tonbe. Rezidan John Sterling, anonsè New York Yankees, pèdi kay li epi kounye a li ap rete nan yon otèl. Dife a voye lafimen epè ki te vizib atravè Hudson River jiska Manhattan. Anpil rezidan afekte ap toujou chèche abri tanporè. Apeprè 160 moun ap dòmi nan yon sant kominotè lokal. Pa premye fwa dife pran nan kote sa a. Plis pase 14 lane de sa, yon dife menm kote sa te detwi nèf kay pandan konstriksyon. Koz la pa te klè men yo te retire sipozon miz an dife, epi yon jiri te mete neglijans sou devlopè a. AvalonBay Communities, yon devlopè Virginia, te jere tou de pwojè—sa kounye a ak sa ki te fèt an 2000. Otorite yo bloke kèk lari bò batiman an men pa gen gwo blokis. Kominote a reyini pou ede moun ki pèdi lakay yo.

article_content: World number one Novak Djokovic could meet Roger Federer in the semifinals of the US Open, after the draw placed both players in the same half on Thursday. Djokovic, the top seed, has lost only twice in 2011 and has already secured the Australian Open and Wimbledon titles this year. He will play a qualifier in the first round. Federer, a five-time US Open champion from Switzerland, begins his campaign against Colombia’s Santiago Giraldo. Defending champion and second seed Rafael Nadal of Spain will play Kazakhstan’s Andrey Golubev in the opening round, as he pursues his 11th Grand Slam title. Speaking to the US Open’s official website, Nadal said: "I feel great. I am here, and I will try my best. Last year was a really emotional year for me. It was the tournament I didn’t play my best in before. Last year, I played one of my best matches in the final. I finally won." Britain’s Andy Murray, who lost to Djokovic in this year’s Australian Open final, will face India’s Somdev Devvarman. Mardy Fish, the top-ranked American player and eighth seed, will play Germany’s Tobias Kamke in the first round. Juan Martin del Potro, the 2009 US Open champion, is set to play Italy’s Filippo Volandri. In the women’s draw, top seed Caroline Wozniacki begins her quest for a maiden Grand Slam title against Spain’s Nuria Llagostera Vives. Second seed Vera Zvonareva will play a qualifier, while 2006 champion Maria Sharapova is paired with Britain’s Heather Watson. French Open winner Li Na will face Romania’s Simona Halep, while Wimbledon champion Petra Kvitova meets another Romanian, Alexandra Dulgheru. Serena Williams, who has won the US Open three times, will open against Serbia’s Bojana Jovanovski.

Djokovic, ki se pi gwo tèt seri a, pèdi sèlman de fwa an 2011 epi li deja ranpòte tit Australian Open ak Wimbledon ane sa a. Li pral jwe kont yon kalifye nan premye wonn lan. Federer, ki soti nan Swis e ki genyen US Open senk fwa, ap kòmanse chanpyona li kont Santiago Giraldo ki soti Kolonbi. Chanpyon an k ap defann tit la ak dezyèm tèt seri a, Rafael Nadal ki soti Espay, ap jwe kont Andrey Golubev ki soti Kazakhstan nan premye wonn lan, pandan li ap pouswiv onzyèm tit Grand Slam li. Pale ak sit ofisyèl US Open lan, Nadal deklare: "Mwen santi mwen byen. Mwen la, epi mwen pral eseye fè tout sa mwen kapab. Ane pase a te yon ane vrèman emosyonnèl pou mwen. Se te tounwa a mwen pa t janm jwe pi byen avan. Ane pase, mwen jwe youn nan pi bon match mwen nan final la. Finalman mwen genyen." Mardy Fish, pi gwo tenisè ameriken an ak uitèn tèt seri a, ap jwe kont Tobias Kamke ki soti Almay nan premye wonn lan. Dezyèm tèt seri a, Vera Zvonareva, pral jwe kont yon kalifye, pandan ke chanpyòn 2006 la, Maria Sharapova, ap kontre ak Britanik Heather Watson. article_content:
WASHINGTON — Inflation in the United States has dropped to its lowest point in two and a half years, while the unemployment rate has remained below 4% for the longest stretch since the 1960s. Additionally, the U.S. economy has continually surpassed forecasts predicting a recession. Despite these positive indicators, various polls and surveys show most Americans still have a pessimistic view of the economy. This disconnect has sparked confusion, frustration, and debate both online and in media commentary.

Recently, the government reported that consumer prices stayed flat from September to October, another sign that inflation continues to ease from its highs last year. Another report found Americans reduced their retail spending in October compared to the previous month, but still spent enough to support economic growth. Nevertheless, a poll last month by The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research showed about three-quarters of respondents viewed the economy as poor. About two-thirds said their expenses had increased, and only one-quarter reported a rise in income.

This disconnect presents a challenge for President Joe Biden as he prepares for his re-election campaign. Polls consistently show most Americans disapprove of Biden's management of the economy. Economists point to several reasons for this gap, especially the ongoing financial and psychological impact of the highest inflation in four decades. Even as inflation cools, many goods and services remain much more expensive than three years ago. Prices are increasing at a slower rate, but they are still high and climbing for many products.

Lisa Cook, a member of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors, recently commented at Duke University: “Most Americans are not just looking for disinflation — a slowdown in price increases. They’re looking for deflation. They want prices back to where they were before the pandemic. I hear that from my family.”

This holds true especially for everyday staples like bread, beef, groceries, rent, and utilities, where households face frequent reminders of higher prices. Deflation, an overall drop in prices, often discourages spending and is not a desired economic goal. Instead, experts say wages need to rise faster than prices so consumers see real improvement.

Measuring how inflation-adjusted incomes have changed since the pandemic is complex. Data from Wendy Edelberg of the Brookings Institution shows that after adjusting for inflation, median weekly earnings have grown at just 0.2% annually from late 2019 through mid-2023. This modest increase leaves many feeling their financial situation hasn’t improved.

For example, Katherine Charles, a 40-year-old single mother in Tampa, Florida, says slower inflation hasn’t made it easier for her to cover basic needs. Her rent climbed 15% in May, and to cut costs over the summer, she kept her air conditioning off during the day despite Tampa’s extreme heat. Charles has reduced spending on groceries, though her teenage son and daughter eat more as they grow. "My son loves red meat," Charles said. “We can’t afford it like we used to. The economy’s not improving for anyone, especially not for me.”

Charles, who works in a call center serving Medicare and Affordable Care Act health plans, received a raise to $18.21 an hour two years ago, but doesn’t recall the exact increase. This month, she participated in a one-day strike at her employer Maximus, seeking higher pay and more affordable health insurance. She said her two children are on Medicaid because Maximus’ insurance is too costly.

Eileen Cassidy Rivera, a spokesperson for Maximus, stated that a recent survey of its 40,000 employees showed three-quarters would recommend Maximus as a great workplace. She added, “During the past five years, we have increased compensation, reduced out-of-pocket health care expenses and improved the work environment.”

Rising prices have driven a wave of labor action this year, with unions representing autoworkers, Teamsters, and airline pilots securing bigger pay raises. Political partisanship also affects perceptions; the University of Michigan’s monthly survey shows that, with Biden as president, Republicans are far more likely than Democrats to rate the economy as poor.

Karen Dynan, a Harvard economist who worked under Presidents Bush and Obama, noted sentiment often shifts after a new president takes office, with those in the opposition party quickly adopting a more negative outlook. “The partisan divide is stronger than it was before,” Dynan said. “Partly because the country is more polarized.”

Meanwhile, many Americans continue to struggle with the effects of inflation. Nationally, the average price of a gallon of milk in October was $3.93—up 23% since February 2020. Ground beef averaged $5.35 per pound, up 33% from pre-pandemic levels. Gas averaged $3.78 per gallon, 53% higher than before, even after falling from last year’s peak. Overall prices have risen about 19% during this period.

Edelberg suggests that price jumps for frequent purchases help explain why people feel frustrated about the economy, even as spending and job numbers remain strong. “Their purchasing power overall is doing pretty well,” she said. National data, though, can miss individual struggles. Brad Hershbein of the Upjohn Institute noted, “In real terms, most people are probably pretty close to where they were pre-pandemic, but there are a lot of exceptions.”

Lower-income Americans have received the largest wage gains since the pandemic, as competition for frontline jobs increased pay. Yet, research finds they face higher inflation because they spend more on volatile costs like food, gas, and rent. Anthony Murphy of the Dallas Fed explained, “At the lower end of the income distribution, people got somewhat higher pay raises, but it likely doesn’t make up for dramatically higher inflation. They’re buying a different mix of goods than average.”

Surveys reviewed by Murphy and Aparna Jayashankar show almost half of Americans report being very stressed by inflation—a figure little changed from last year, despite easing inflation rates. Studies also reveal that people dislike inflation more intensely than its direct impact might suggest, and rarely expect their wages to keep pace, especially amid time lags in pay adjustments. Hershbein concluded, “People are fixated on how much more they pay for the things that matter most—gas, food, groceries, rent—even if those prices aren’t rising as quickly. If everyone had lost a job, we’d be focused on that instead.”

WASHINGTON — Enflasyon Ozetazini bese nan pi ba nivo li nan de ane ak demi, pandan chomaj la rete pi ba pase 4% pou pi lontan depi ane 1960. Anplis, ekonomi ameriken an kontinye fè pi byen pase previzyon ki t ap anonse resesyon. Malgre tout done sa yo, majorite ameriken dapre sondaj, toujou gen opinyon negatif sou ekonomi an. Sitiyasyon sa a bay konfizyon, fristrasyon, ak deba sou rezo sosyal ak nan medya yo.

Dènyeman, gouvènman an fè konnen pa te gen okenn ogmantasyon pri konsomatè ant septanm ak oktòb, yon siy enflasyon ap bese depi dènye pi li te genyen ane pase. Yon lòt rapò montre ameriken bese depans yo an oktòb konpare ak mwa anvan an, men toujou gen ase depans pou kwasans ekonomik lan. Menm konsa, yon sondaj AP-NORC mwa pase bay kote anviwon twa-ka repond yo di ekonomi an move. Apeprè de tyè deklare depans yo ogmante, pandan sèlman yon sou kat di revni yo ogmante.

Diskoneksyon sa a se yon gwo defi pou Prezidan Joe Biden ki pral nan kanpay re-eleksyon. Sondaj montre pifò moun pa dakò ak fason misye jere ekonomi an. Ekonomis mete aksan sou efè enflasyon ki pi wo depi 40 ane, ki kontinye afekte finans ak moral pèp la. Malgre enflasyon ap bese, pri anpil bagay toujou wo anpil epi kontinye monte.

Lisa Cook, manm nan Konsèy Rezèv Federal la, deklare Duke University: "Pifò Ameriken pa vle sèlman enflasyon bese, yo swete pri yo tounen kote yo te avan COVID. Mwen tande sa nan fanmi mwen." 

Sitiyasyon sa a se reyalite sitou pou pwodwi tankou pen, vyann bèf, makèt, lwaye ak sèvis. Deflasyon — lè pri desann jeneral — pa souvan bon paske li entèdi depans. Ekspè yo pito wè salè monte pi vit pase pri yo pou konsomatè yo benefisye.

Konbyen revni ajiste ak enflasyon ogmante apati pandemi a difisil pou mezire. Wendy Edelberg, Brookings Institution, di salè medyàn chak semèn ogmante sèlman 0.2% pa ane ant fen 2019 ak mitan 2023, sa ki fè anpil moun pa santi yo pwogrese.

Tankou Katherine Charles, manman sèl 40-zan Tampa, di ke menm si enflasyon bese, li pa wè lavi fasil. Lwaye li monte 15% nan mwa me. Pandan ete a, li te oblije pa limen klimatisè lakay li akoz chalè Tampa. Li redui depans manje pandan pitit li yo ap manje plis. "Pitit gason mwen renmen vyann bèf," li di. "Nou pa ka achte jan nou te konn fè. Ekonomi an pa amelyore sitou pou moun tankou mwen."

Charles travay nan sant apèl Maximus pou sèvis Medicare ak Affordable Care Act. Li te gen ogmantasyon pouswiv $18.21 pa èdtan gen dezan men pa sonje egzak kantite lajan an. Mwa sa a, li patisipe nan yon grèv yon-jou pou mande ogmantasyon salè ak asirans sante pi abòdab. Li di pitit li yo sou Medicaid paske asirans Maximus pa ase abòdab.

Eileen Cassidy Rivera, Maximus, di 3/4 anplwaye yo ta rekòmande Maximus pou travay. Li ajoute, "Nan 5 dènye ane yo, salè ogmante, depans asirans bese, kondisyon travay amelyore."

Ogmantasyon pri yo se kòz mouvman grèv an 2023; sendika travayè oto, Teamsters, ak pilòt avyon jwenn ogmantasyon salè. Politik patizan enfliyanse jan moun wè ekonomi an; dapre University of Michigan, Repibliken plis di ekonomi an pa bon depi Biden prezidan.

Karen Dynan, ekonomis Harvard ki te sèvi ak Bush ak Obama, di santiman ekonomik vire rapid apre nouvo prezidan bay kòmand. "Divizyon politik la plis toujou," li di, akoz polarizasyon.

Men anpil moun toujou ap santi efè enflasyon an. Pri lèt an oktòb se $3.93 pa galon — 23% ogmantasyon depi fevriye 2020. Vyann bèf $5.35 pa liv, 33% ogmantasyon; gaz $3.78 pa galon, 53% ogmantasyon. An total, pri yo monte 19% pandan peryòd sa a.

Edelberg di ogmantasyon sou sa moun achte plis la, ede eksplike poukisa yo santi yo fristre, menm si depans ak pwofi travay rete bon. "Poder dache yo pa two mal" li di. Done ofisyèl pa reflete tout istwa pèp la. Brad Hershbein, Upjohn Institute, di, "An reyalite, pifò moun pa twò lwen kote yo te anvan COVID, men gen plizyè eksepsyon."

Ameriken ki pi pòv yo resevwa pi gwo ogmantasyon salè, pandan konpetisyon pou travay premye liy yo, men rechèch montre yo sibi plis enfliyans enflasyon paske yo depanse plis sou manje, gaz, lwaye. Anthony Murphy, Federal Reserve Dallas, di: "Moun ki nan ba echèl revni jwenn ogmantasyon men li pa konpanse ak gwo enflasyon. Yo achte lòt kalite pwodwi pase mwayèn lan."

Sondaj Murphy ak Jayashankar montre prèske mwatye ameriken toujou di yo anpil stress akoz enflasyon malgre nivo enflasyon bese. Etid montre moun pa renmen enflasyon plis pase sa enfliyans ekonomik lan ta explike. Pifò moun pa atann salè swiv pri yo, espesyalman kote ajisteman pran tan. Hershbein fini: "Moun ap fikse sou ogmantasyon pri bagay ki pi enpòtan: gaz, manje, lwaye — pa pi vit, men toujou wo. Si chak moun te pèdi djòb, nou t ap konsantre sou sa."

article_content: Efforts to rescue the mountain chicken frog, one of the world's largest and rarest amphibians, are intensifying in the Caribbean. This hefty frog, growing up to 20 centimeters long and weighing as much as a kilogram, used to inhabit at least five Caribbean islands. Now, only small populations remain on Dominica and in a specially protected area on Montserrat. Once widely hunted for its meat and recognized as a local delicacy in Dominica, the mountain chicken faces far more severe challenges today: the loss of its habitats, attacks by invasive species, road dangers, pollution, and a deadly disease known as chytridiomycosis. The mountain chicken's precarious status first gained international notice after Montserrat's 1995 volcanic eruptions destroyed much of its environment. Conservation organizations like Fauna & Flora International rushed to assess the impact. Things grew worse with the arrival of the chytrid fungus: on Dominica in 2002 and Montserrat in 2009, it devastated local frogs, with Dominica losing up to 80% of its mountain chickens within two years. Despite fears, the species hasn’t vanished. To clarify its numbers, nearly 30 researchers from 13 partner groups dedicated months to a major survey across Dominica, spending 960 hours over 26 nights navigating tough terrain in search of these elusive frogs. Just 23 mountain chicken frogs were found, two sadly as roadkill. The discovery of two juveniles and five froglets, however, proved that some breeding continues. Scientists blame the dry season for the difficulty in hearing the frogs' calls, which are vital for detection. One of the most hopeful discoveries was an 11-year-old male frog—the oldest recorded mountain chicken. Genetic tests on this survivor and others could reveal whether some frogs are developing resistance to the deadly fungus. With fewer than 50 known individuals left, the mountain chicken faces risks from disease, climate change, natural disasters, and human threats. Conservationists urge urgent and coordinated action to prevent extinction. Jeanelle Brisbane from Dominica's Forestry Department, who also leads WildDominique, underscored the frog's importance as a symbol of cultural pride and called for united action. Isabel Vique of Fauna & Flora International found the project deeply inspiring, driving the team’s dedication. Jenny Daltry, director of the Fauna & Flora-Re:wild partnership, appealed for funding, saying there is hope if quick, collective action is taken as with other Caribbean species rescued in the past.
translated_content: Efò pou sove grenouy moun-chiken an, youn nan pi gwo ak pi ra anfibyen sou tè a, ap vin pi entans nan Karayib la. Grenouy sa a, ki ka rive 20 santimèt longè ak peze jiska yon kilogram, te viv sou omwen senk zile Karayib yo, men jodi a li sèlman rete sou Dominik ak nan yon ti zòn pwoteje sou Montserrat. Li te yon délikates popilè nan Dominik, men kounye a, se pa lachas ki pi gwo danje li. Pèt abita, predatè pa natif natal, aksidan sou wout, polisyon, epi maladi fongis chaktridyozyomyozis la (chytridiomycosis) ap menase egzistans li. Sitiyasyon kriz moun-chiken an te vin jwenn atansyon mond lan apre eripsyon vòlkan ki te ravaje abita li sou Montserrat an 1995. Fauna & Flora International ak lòt òganizasyon te aji rapidman pou mezire domaj la. Lè fongis chaktrid lan te sòti sou Dominik an 2002 ak Montserrat an 2009, li te devaste popilasyon grenouy yo. Sou Dominik, jiska 80% te disparèt anvan de lane te pase. Malgre tout difikilte, espès la pa gen disparèt nèt. Preske 30 chèchè soti nan 13 òganizasyon konsèvasyon, pase 960 èdtan sou 26 swa ap chèche grenouy sa yo sou Dominik. Yo te jwenn 23 moun-chiken, enkli de ki te mouri sou wout la. Pi bèl nouvèl la se dekouvèt de jenvenil ak senk pitit grenouy, ki pwouve repwodiksyon ap kontinye. Syantis yo eksplike sezon sèch la te rann li pi difisil pou tande apèl grenouy yo, sa ki te retade deteksyon yo. Men pi gwo espwa a se dekouvèt yon grenouy mal ki gen 11 zan, pi ansyen moun-chiken yo te janm jwenn. Rezilta tès jenetik yo ka montre si gen kèk ki ap devlope iminite kont fongis lan. Depi gen mwens pase 50 moun-chiken ki rete, espès la ap menase akòz maladi, dezòd klima, dezas natirèl, ak aktivite imen. Espesyalis yo mande aksyon ijans ak kolaborasyon entènasyonal pou evite disparisyon total. Jeanelle Brisbane, ajans Forè Dominik la ak fondatè WildDominique, mete aksan sou enpòtans moun-chiken an nan fyète nasyonal ak kiltirèl, epi li apèl tout moun pou mete men nan batay la. Isabel Vique, Fauna & Flora International, di eksperyans la te bay anpil enspirasyon epi sa pouse ekip la pou yo pa lage. Jenny Daltry, direktè Fauna & Flora ak Re:wild, mande finansman prese ak kwè solisyon mache si tout moun mete tèt ansanm—jan sa te fèt pou lòt bèt Karayib yo deja.

article_content:
Get ready for wet weather as the upcoming bank holiday in the UK is expected to bring rain, forecasters have warned. According to the Met Office, weather conditions will become increasingly unsettled through the week, with temperatures dropping. By the weekend, regions in the north and west may experience rain and thunderstorms moving in from the west, while the outlook for the south and east is brighter, with a greater chance of sunshine.

The soaring temperatures from last weekend, when parts of Britain reached up to 32°C, are not expected to return. Temperatures across the UK are forecasted to dip to the low 20s Celsius. Emma Sharples, a Met Office forecaster, explained that “As we go through the week, Wednesday and Thursday will bring a higher chance of showers. By the weekend, low pressure from the west will bring some showers; however, there will also be sunshine. It’s too early to say it will be a total washout, but temperatures won't be as high as last weekend, with less humidity and more cloud, likely in the low to mid 20s. It should still feel fairly warm, around the seasonal average.”

Recently, most of the country enjoyed a burst of sunshine, with temperatures outpacing those in Greece and Barbados. Crowds flocked to Brighton Beach amid the high temperatures. However, forecasters do not expect this weather to last into the bank holiday. Rain was reported at the V Festival site in Weston Park, Staffordshire, and is possible again next weekend.

Yesterday, torrential rain swept across West Yorkshire, with steady rainfall in places like Centenary Square, Bradford. Jonathan Powell of Vantage Weather Services commented that the rest of the month could be “absolutely dreadful” in terms of weather: “The South-east should see good weather until Wednesday, but low pressure is moving in, bringing colder, windier, and wetter conditions for the bank holiday. Some regions, especially the East that recently had the warmest weather, could experience heavy downpours and possible flash flooding. It’s shaping up to be a real washout for the last official period of summer.”

Parts of Britain saw continuous sunshine and blue skies over the weekend, bringing millions outdoors. The South and South-east saw temperatures up to 32.4°C in Cavendish, Suffolk, 30.6°C in Cambridge, and 30°C in London. People flocked to the coast, with roads to Dorset and the South-west busy early on. In contrast, the north, west, and Wales reached highs around 22°C, still above the seasonal average of 21°C. Heavy rainfall in the Midlands drenched the 150,000 attendees at Staffordshire’s V Festival.

article_content: An online report suggesting that R&B singer De'Mario 'Raz B' Thornton was in a coma in China was a hoax, according to his agent. Raz B was injured during a nightclub brawl near Shanghai, but his injuries were minor, manager Elayne Rivers told CNN on Monday. 'The comments about Raz being in a coma did not come from his official representative,' Rivers said. Raz B's brother, who performs as Ricky Romance, stated Monday afternoon that he had been 'misled for unknown reasons.' "I was unfortunately unable to contact my brother at the time and then panicked," Romance said. "I alerted as many people as possible of this information, hoping to gather facts. Since the source that gave me this information seemed reliable, I didn't question it—just believed. I apologize for jumping to conclusions, but a coma is a serious situation and it concerned my brother, who is also my best friend. I sincerely apologize for any confusion I caused." A celebrity news website first reported that the original B2K member was in a coma on Saturday, citing Toy Jones as the source. Although Jones gave CNN the same information on Sunday, she declined to provide the hospital's name, stating only that it was in Zhejiang province near Shanghai. Several hours later, Jones sent CNN a statement saying that Raz B had miraculously recovered from the coma and would be released from the hospital in a few days. The statement read: 'Doctors say numerous brain scans showed that Raz's entire cortex—the parts of the brain responsible for consciousness, thought, memory, and understanding—is now functioning. Doctors call it a miracle and told his family he stands a strong chance of survival. There are no signs of brain death. Against all odds, Raz woke up this morning and is in stable condition. We ask fans and media to respect our family's privacy.' CNN chose not to report the story until details could be confirmed by the U.S. State Department, the U.S. embassy in China, or Chinese officials. Raz B also personally asked CNN via e-mail not to publish anything. On Monday, Rivers released a statement distancing Raz B from the coma report. When CNN asked Jones about the statement, she insisted, 'as far as I know, it is true' that he was in a coma. She said she was hired by Raz B's family to disseminate the information. Dozens of news agencies around the world—including in China—repeated the coma story, giving Raz B more publicity in one weekend than he's likely had since B2K disbanded nine years ago. CNN's Josh Levs and Denise Quan contributed to this report.
translated_content: Yon rapò sou entènèt te fè kwè chantè R&B De'Mario 'Raz B' Thornton te nan koma an Chin, men ajan li di sa pa vre. Raz B te blese nan yon goumen nan yon klib nwit toupre Shanghai, men blesi li yo te leje, dapre manadjè li Elayne Rivers ki te pale ak CNN lendi. 'Deklarasyon sou Raz B ki te di li te nan koma pa soti nan reprezantan ofisyèl li,' sa Rivers te di. Frè Raz B, ki itilize non Ricky Romance kòm atis, te di lendi aprè midi yo te 'fè l mal enfòme pou rezon li pa konnen.' "Malerezman, mwen pa t ka kontakte frè mwen nan moman an epi mwen te panike," Romance te di. "Mwen te di plis moun posib enfòmasyon sa a, espere jwenn verite a. Depi sous la te sanble serye, mwen pa t poze kesyon—mwen te kwè. Mwen regrèt si m te prese tire konklizyon paske koma se yon bagay serye, e sa t ap konsène frè mwen ki se pi bon zanmi m tou. Mwen vrèman regrèt tout konfizyon mwen te bay." Yon sit wèb selebrite te premye di ansyen manm B2K a te nan koma samdi, e li te site Toy Jones kòm sous la. Menmsi Jones te bay CNN menm enfòmasyon an dimanch, li pa t di non lopital la, li te jis di li se nan pwovens Zhejiang toupre Shanghai. Plizyè èdtan apre, Jones te voye yon deklarasyon ki di Raz B te netway ke miracule e li pral soti lopital la talè. Deklarasyon an te di: 'Doktè yo di plizyè tès sèvo montre tout korteks Raz B—pati nan sèvo ki bay konsyans, panse, memwa ak konpreyansyon—ap mache byen kounye a. Doktè yo rele sa yon mirak e di fanmi li li gen bèl chans pou l sove, pa gen siy li mouri nan sèvo. Malgre tout bagay, Raz B te leve maten an epi li an bon eta. Nou mande fanatik ak medya pou respekte entimite fanmi an.' CNN te pran desizyon pou pa pale de istwa a jiskaske Depatman Deta Ameriken an, anbasad Etazini an Chin oswa otorite Chinwa yo konfime detay yo. Raz B te mande CNN pèsonèlman pa pibliye anyen. Lendi, Rivers te bay yon deklarasyon pou mete distans ant Raz B ak rapò sou koma a. Lè CNN mande Jones sou deklarasyon sa, li te toujou di: 'de sa mwen konnen, li se te verite' ke li te nan koma. Li deklare li te anboche pa fanmi Raz B pou pataje enfòmasyon an. Plizyè ajans nouvèl atravè mond lan—menm an Chin—te repete nouvèl koma a, sa ki te bay Raz B plis piblikite nan yon wikenn pase li te janm jwenn depi B2K te separe nèf lane pase. Josh Levs ak Denise Quan nan CNN te ede prepare rapò sa a.

article_content: A developer in Atlanta aims to tear down the historic Randolph-Lucas House for condo expansion. Built in 1924 for Hollins Nicholas Randolph, Thomas Jefferson's grandson, the mansion is recognized for its historical value. The Buckhead Heritage Society is offering the house for free to anyone prepared to relocate and restore it—a project expected to cost at least $350,000 for moving, plus renovations. The mansion has stood uninhabited for 25 years, following the death of its last resident in the 1980s. It previously served as a wedding venue before earning historic status in 1990. Persistent economic challenges and uncertain repair costs have deterred potential buyers despite ongoing outreach. The landowner, 2500 Peachtree Condominium Association, is seeking city approval to demolish the structure and replace it with a pavilion for condo residents. The association was originally required, when constructing the condos in 1997, to both move and renovate the house, but preservationists argue these conditions may not have been fully honored. Experts are unable to assess the property’s true condition due to denied inspection access. Atlanta’s limited history of historic preservation has resulted in many older buildings being lost. Members of the Buckhead Heritage Society, such as Wright Mitchell and Erica Danylchak, persist in raising awareness, yet the search continues for a buyer capable of undertaking the costly restoration.
translated_content: Yon devlopè nan Atlanta vle detwi kay istorik Randolph-Lucas pou elaji espas kondo li yo. Kay sa a te bati an 1924 pou Hollins Nicholas Randolph, pitit pitit Thomas Jefferson, e li gen yon gwo valè istorik. Buckhead Heritage Society ap ofri kay la gratis a nenpòt moun ki dispoze deplase ak renove li — sa ap koute omwen $350,000 pou deplase li sèlman, san konte tout depans renovasyon yo. Kay la pa itilize depi 25 lane, depi dènye moun ki te rete ladan li te mouri nan ane 1980 yo. Li te konn sèvi kòm plas maryaj anvan li te vin klase kòm patrimwàn an 1990. Sitiyasyon ekonomik difisil ak pri reparasyon ki pa klè kontinye fè moun pa enterese achte kay la, malgre anpil efò pou sa. 2500 Peachtree Condominium Association, ki se pwopriyetè tè a, ap chèche pèmisyon vil la pou kraze kay la epi konstwi yon paviyon pou rezidan kondo yo. Lè yo te konstwi kondo yo an 1997, yo te oblije deplase ak renove kay la, men reprezantan patrimwàn yo di kondisyon sa yo pa t respekte nèt. Ekspè pa ka antre pou evalye eta kay la paske yo pa jwenn otorizasyon. Nan Atlanta, paske konsèvasyon patrimwàn pa te janm fèt seryezman, anpil bèl ansyen kay detwi. Moun tankou Wright Mitchell ak Erica Danylchak nan Buckhead Heritage Society kontinye ap angaje yo pou sove kay la, men yo poko jwenn achtè ki ka kore yon renovasyon ki koute chè konsa.

article_content: When Sony first unveiled ‘Sorcery’ at E3 2010, it was billed as the ultimate demonstration of the new PlayStation Move controller’s capabilities. Two years later, the game finally landed—but while it’s fun, it doesn’t quite fulfill the hopes set by that initial reveal. In ‘Sorcery’, players step into the shoes of Finn, a young apprentice thrust into a battle to rescue Princess Erline—a magical faerie princess who is, amusingly, a long-tailed cat. Using the Move controller, players cast spells through gestures: select a spell by holding a button, then move your hand in a specific direction (down for earth, a twist for ice, etc.). The game lets you combine spells, like freezing enemies with repeated ice attacks before shattering them, or sending out fireballs after summoning a whirlwind. While casting spells feels natural and switching between them is easy, aiming at enemies on higher platforms can be inconsistent, and the rapid flicking motions can get tiring. It’s wise to take breaks to avoid arm fatigue. Rather than the traditional leveling-up system found in many role-playing games, progression depends on the spells you acquire and the potions you craft. Potions are made by mimicking actions with the controller—grinding, stirring, and pouring—adding an interactive element to item creation. You only need to make each potion once (aside from health potions, which can’t be crafted repeatedly). The story is straightforward but lively, with plenty of witty exchanges. The voice acting gives Finn and Erline real personality, making their journey relatable and charming. ‘Sorcery’ isn’t a massive or deep game, but as a way to introduce players to the Move controller, it’s effective and enjoyable. ‘Sorcery’ is available only on PlayStation 3, requiring the Move controller, navigation controller, and Eye camera. The game is rated E10+ for its fantasy-themed action, mild blood, and some suggestive content. This review was based on a retail copy provided for the PlayStation 3.
translated_content: Lè Sony te prezante 'Sorcery' pou premye fwa nan E3 2010, yo te di se jwèt ideyal pou montre kapasite nouvo kontwolè Move lan sou PlayStation. De lane apre, jwèt la finalman soti — li amizan, men li pa totalman reponn ak tout sa moun t ap espere depi premye demonstrasyon an. Nan 'Sorcery', ou jwe wòl Finn, yon apranti majisyen ki bezwen sove Princess Erline — ki se yon ti chat majik ak yon ke trè long! Avèk kontwolè Move lan, ou fè jès pou lanse maj; ou chwazi yon maj epi ou fè mouvman espesyal (desann pou maj tè, vire pou maj glas, elatriye). Ou ka melanje maj yo: pa egzanp ou ka friz lènmi avèk atak glas epi kraze yo pita, oswa voye boul dife apre ou kreye yon gwo van. Fè maj ap santi natirèl, epi chanje maj fasil, men sa ka difisil pou vize lènmi ki anlè, epi mouvman rapid yo ka fatigan pou bra ou. Chita pran pòz souvan pou evite zepòl ak bra ou fè mal. Jwèt la pa itilize sistèm tradisyonèl ogmante nivo RPG; avansman w depann sou maj ou jwenn ak potyon ou prepare. Ou kreye potyon pa imite aksyon tankou moulen, melanje ak vide engredyan ak kontwolè a — sa ba ou plis entèraksyon. W ap fè chak potyon yon sèl fwa (sauf potyon sante ki pa ka fabrike souvan). Istwa a senp men li chaje ak blag ak bon jan entèraksyon. Aktè vwa yo bay Finn ak Erline bèl pèsonalite, sa ki ede w atache ak avanti yo. 'Sorcery' pa yon gwo jwèt konplike, men kòm entwodiksyon ak kontwolè Move lan, li toujou efikas ak amizan. 'Sorcery' disponib sèlman sou PlayStation 3, epi li mande kontwolè Move, navigasyon an ak kamera Eye a. Jwèt la klase E10+ pou aksyon majik, ti kras san ak kèk sèn suspekt. Revizyon sa fèt sou yon kopi jwèt pou PS3 ke Sony te bay.

article_content:
Hybrid work arrangements are now common, but who comes to the office can depend on age. Millennials—those in their 30s and early 40s—are the biggest advocates for working from home, says Stanford economist Nick Bloom. Gen Z workers, mostly in their 20s, tend to want to be in the office more—three to four days a week—mainly for mentoring, socializing, or because their shared apartments make working from home difficult. Workers age 50 and up, including Gen X and Boomers, often prefer regular office attendance, since they’re used to it and typically have fewer family responsibilities at home.

Research by Bloom, José Barrero, and Steven Davis finds millennials take the lead in remote work, especially parents living in suburban houses with younger children. After the pandemic, many millennials moved farther away and, according to Gusto payroll data, those aged 30-34 more than doubled their average commute—from around 9 miles pre-pandemic to significantly farther after. The pandemic also made hybrid and remote roles attractive enough that some employees refused to return to the office, even resigning when flexibility was taken away.

Younger employees, especially those whose early careers or education were remote, now want more face-to-face time—but often find their managers are working elsewhere. Some older employees, like Charles Bond in Southern California, opted to leave the workforce instead of going fully remote, valuing in-person camaraderie over flexibility. Today’s hybrid schedules mean many offices remain quiet on Mondays and Fridays, and millennial preferences have shaped what workplace flexibility looks like for all.

Gen Z, jèn ki nan ventèn yo, plis prefere vini biwo a 3-4 jou pa semèn pou jwenn mentorat, fè zanmi, oubyen paske kote yo rete pa fasil pou travay lakay. Travayè ki gen plis pase 50 ane—Gen X ak Boomers—souvan prefere vin regilyèman, depi yo abitye avèk sa epi yo pa gen anpil responsablite fanmi.

Travay hybride ak travay lakay vin plis atiran, kèk anplwaye menm kite travay olye pou retounen obligatwa. 

Jèn ki komanse karyè oubyen etid yo a distans, kounye a vle plis rankont fas-a-fas—men yo souvan jwenn bos yo ap travay aleka. Orè hybride fè biwo yo prèske vid lendi ak vandredi, epi preferans millennials yo ap chanje fason travay fleksib prezante.
post_content: Millennials are leading the charge for remote work, changing how offices look—while Gen Z wants more face time and Boomers still love the office vibe. Hybrid work is the new normal, but who shows up really depends on your generation! #WorkTrends #RemoteLife

article_content: Walking through a quiet cemetery at night with only a flashlight can be an intriguing experience for amateur ghost hunters, especially around Halloween. "Many paranormal societies use graveyards for training," said Alan Brown, an author of more than 20 books on the subject. "If you register an EMF reading in a graveyard, since there is no electricity, it must come from another source." Often, spirits believed to be present in cemeteries are seen as more sorrowful than frightening, reflecting the grief associated with these resting places. Richard Senate, a historian and ghost hunter with more than 30 years of experience, explained, "In fact, many cemeteries aren't truly haunted. People are more likely to haunt places they loved in life. The sensation of a haunted cemetery often stems from grief lingering in the area, rather than from spirits." Still, he mentions that several cemeteries are famous for their supernatural legends. Senate shared a list of some of America's most haunted cemeteries. Visiting these historical places might bring you face-to-face with the unexplained. St. Louis Cemetery No. 1, New Orleans: Known for its above-ground tombs and colorful history, New Orleans’ cemeteries have influenced many writers. When the ground would flood, buried coffins sometimes surfaced because the city sits below the water table, making above-ground tombs necessary. This cemetery is perhaps the city’s most well-known. Visitors have reported seeing ghosts of Civil War soldiers, yellow fever victims, and shadowy figures, according to Senate. The most famous spirit is Marie Laveau, the legendary voodoo queen, who is said to walk near her tomb. Tradition holds that making three X’s with chalk on her tomb and making a request may bring good fortune. Resurrection Catholic Cemetery, Chicago: Not every haunting occurs at night. Chicago’s most famous cemetery spirit is ‘Resurrection Mary.’ She is often seen near or inside the cemetery, sometimes asking for a ride from passing drivers. Reports describe her as a young woman in a vintage ball gown who vanishes near the cemetery. Her story is believed to be linked to a Polish woman killed in a car accident in the 1930s and buried at Resurrection. Hollywood Forever Cemetery, California: As the resting place of famous Hollywood figures, this cemetery is also known for ghost sightings. Rudolph Valentino and the ‘lady in black’ are two spirits said to linger here. According to legend, the lady in black brought roses to Valentino’s grave every year after he once comforted her before surgery. After her death, sightings of both her and Valentino’s ghosts have been reported. Boothill Cemetery, Tombstone, Arizona: Tombstone, once a lawless mining town, is the site of the O.K. Corral gunfight with the Clanton gang, the Earps, and Doc Holliday. Many outlaws are buried here. Senate notes that spirits of outlaws and Clanton gang members are said to appear, making this a popular spot for paranormal enthusiasts. Gettysburg Cemetery, Pennsylvania: The scene of one of America’s bloodiest battles, Gettysburg is now a cemetery for Union and Confederate soldiers. Ghostly soldiers in period uniforms are said to roam the grounds. Senate shares reports of a man with a black hat and star—possibly representing a Texas regiment—who sometimes appears in tourists’ photos before mysteriously vanishing. The nearby Farnsworth House Inn is also reputed to be haunted by Confederate ghostly snipers. Senate’s advice to aspiring ghost hunters: be respectful and do not disturb graves. "You should be like a ghost yourself—no one should know you've been there," he said.
translated_content: Mache nan yon simityè trankil lannwit ak sèlman yon lanp tèt ka yon eksperyans enteresan pou moun k ap chèche fantom, espesyalman pandan Halloween. "Anpil sosyete paranòmal itilize simityè kòm yon kote pou antrènman," dapre Alan Brown, otè plis pase 20 liv sou sijè a. "Si ou jwenn yon lekti EMF nan simityè a, depi pa gen elektrisite, li dwe soti yon lòt kote." Souvan, lespri yo kwè ki prezan nan simityè yo plis ak lapenn pase ak la pè, paske yo reflete doulè moun ki pèdi yo. Richard Senate, yon istoryen ak chasè fantom ki gen plis pase 30 ane eksperyans, eksplike: "An reyalite, anpil simityè pa vrèman ante. Moun plis prè pou yo ante kote yo te renmen pandan lavi yo. Santi kòm si yon simityè ante souvan sòti nan tristès ki rete nan zòn nan, pa nesesèman lespri." Men, li mansyone kèk simityè ki vin popilè ak istwa mistik yo. Senate pataje lis kèk nan simityè ki pi ante Ozetazini. Vizite kote istorik sa yo ka mennen w fas-a-fas ak bagay ou pa konprann. St. Louis Cemetery No. 1, New Orleans: Avèk tombe sou tè a ak gwo istwa li yo, simityè New Orleans yo enspire anpil ekriven. Lè tè a inonde, sèkèy yo te souvan remonte paske vil la anba nivo dlo a, sa ki fè tombe sou tè chakfwa nesesè. Simityè sa a se youn nan pi popilè yo. Vizitè yo rapòte yo wè fantòm sòlda Lagè Sivil, viktim lafyèv jòn ak fgi lonbraj, dapre Senate. Pi popilè a se lespri Marie Laveau, rèn vodou la, yo di li mache bò tombe li. Gen tradisyon ki di pou make twa X ak krey sou tombe li epi fè yon demann. Resurrection Catholic Cemetery, Chicago: Pa chak ante rive lannwit. Lespri ki pi popilè Chicago a se 'Resurrection Mary.' Yo souvan wè li pre oswa anndan simityè a, pafwa ap mande chofè pou mennen l lakay. Yo dekri li kòm yon jèn fi an rob bal ansyen ki disparèt bò simityè a. Yo kwè istwa li konkòde ak yon fi polonè ki te mouri nan aksidan machin an 1930 yo epi antere nan Resurrection. Hollywood Forever Cemetery, California: Antyèman kote zetwal Hollywood yo repoze, simityè a popilè tou pou fantom ki parèt l. Rudolph Valentino ak 'lady in black' se de nan lespri ki di yo rete la. Selon lejand, madanm yo rele lady in black la te mete roz sou kavo Valentino chak ane paske Valentino te bay li kouraj anvan operasyon. Apre lanmò li, rapòte ke yo kontinye wè lespri li ak Valentino toupre kavo a. Boothill Cemetery, Tombstone, Arizona: Tombstone, yon ansyen vil min pa t gen lalwa, kote O.K. Corral te genyen ak Clanton, Earps ak Doc Holliday. Anpil bandi repoze la. Senate di lespri bandi ak Clanton yo souvan parèt, fè l tounen yon kote remakab pou moun ki renmen paranòmal. Gettysburg Cemetery, Pennsylvania: Sèn youn nan pi gwo batay sanginè Etazini, Gettysburg vin simityè pou sòlda sendika ak konfederasyon. Dwe fantom ak rad epòk yo ap mache sou zòn nan. Senate pale sou yon mesye ak yon chapo nwa ak zetwal—petèt reprezantan regiment Texas—ki pafwa parèt sou foto touris epi disparèt. Farnsworth House Inn, ki tou pre a di yo gen fantom tirè konfederasyon anndan li. Konsèy Senate bay pou moun k ap chèche fantom: se pou ou respekte epi pa deranje tonm. "Ou ta dwe tankou yon fantom—pèsonn pa dwe konnen ou te pase la," li di.

From voodoo queens to famous outlaws, the spirits are waiting! 🔦👻 #GhostHunting #HauntedHistory

article_content: Onlookers might have done a triple take as dozens of triplets from around the world gathered at an annual convention in Baltimore. Sibling trios traveled from places like Bolivia and Puerto Rico—including one set of triplet models—to attend the 2013 Triplet Convention at the Holiday Inn in Inner Harbor, Baltimore, earlier this week. More than 33 families and nearly 40 sets of triplets participated in the event. Some quadruplets, called 'super triplets,' were also invited. Attendees posed for a group photo, joined workshops on coping with being separated at school, and took part in a lively parade through the streets, carrying signs with their names. Eighteen-year-old triplets Adrianna, Laurel, and Elizabeth from Tall Timbers, Maryland, described the experience as unique and fun. Elizabeth said, 'It's really fun. We do everything together. It's a unique situation because we share experiences and feelings.' The sisters have modeled in ads and commercials and have attended six conventions so far. Other attendees included three-year-old triplets Kenya, Cadence, and Shayla from Rockville, Maryland, who wore matching pink outfits, and the identical Hernandez-Adorno triplets Gabriela, Astrid, and Myrna from Milton-Freewater, Oregon. Richard Blasdell from Edgewood, Maryland, the father of two sets of triplets, commented: 'The second set was tough because they were six years younger. Triplets are so rare, we often attract a lot of attention.' The convention began in 1991, founded by Kree Lindsey, a single mother of seven who had a set of triplets. The largest convention was held in 1995, when about 200 sets attended. This year's director, Kim Jones, attended with her own trio of 17-year-old boys, emphasizing the importance of nurturing each triplet's individuality. 'Although they are often seen as a group, each is very much an individual.'
translated_content: Moun ki te la ka panse yo wè triplè twòp fwa, paske plizyè douzèn triplè soti atravè mond lan te reyini nan yon kongrè anyèl Baltimore. Twa frè ak sè te vwayaje soti nan kote tankou Bolivi ak Pòtoriko—pami yo te gen youn ki se modèl triplè—pou asiste Kongrè Triplè 2013 lan nan Holiday Inn bò Inner Harbor, Baltimore, pi bonè semèn sa. Plis pase 33 fanmi ak prèske 40 gwoup triplè te patisipe nan evènman an. Kèk kadrupè, yo rele 'super triplè,' te envite tou. Patisipan yo te poze pou foto an gwoup, te swiv atelye sou fason byen jere separasyon lekòl, epi yo te fè yon parad animè nan lari yo pandan yo te kenbe siy ak non yo. Triplè 18-zan Adrianna, Laurel, ak Elizabeth ki soti Tall Timbers, Maryland, dekri eksperyans lan kòm inik e amizan. Elizabeth di: 'Li vrèman amizan. Nou fè tout bagay ansanm. Se yon sitiyasyon inik paske nou pataje eksperyans ak santiman.' Twa sè sa yo se modèl pou piblisite ak reklam epi yo deja asiste sis kongrè konsa. Te gen lòt patisipan tankou triplè 3-zan Kenya, Cadence, ak Shayla ki soti Rockville, Maryland, yo tout te mete menm rad woz, epi gen triplè idantik Hernandez-Adorno yo: Gabriela, Astrid ak Myrna, ki soti Milton-Freewater, Oregon. Richard Blasdell, ki soti Edgewood, Maryland, papa de gwoup triplè, di: 'Dezyèm gwoup la te pi difisil paske yo gen sis ane diferans. Triplè yo ra anpil, nou toujou atire anpil atansyon.' Kongrè sa a te kòmanse an 1991 pa Kree Lindsey, yon manman selibatè ki gen sèt pitit, ladan yo te gen yon gwoup triplè. Pi gwo kongrè a te fèt an 1995 kote anviwon 200 triplè te prezan. Direktris ane sa a, Kim Jones, te la ak twa pitit gason li ki gen 17 an, mete aksan sou enpòtans endividyalite chak triplè. 'Menm si moun wè yo kòm yon gwoup, chak gen pwòp pèsonalite pa yo.'
post_content: Did you know nearly 40 sets of triplets gathered in Baltimore for a fun annual convention? From group photos to wild parades, these siblings showed off their individuality and made lifelong friends. #TripletLife #BaltimoreFun

article_content: Capturing close-up video of molten lava streaming into the Pacific Ocean is a rare and risky feat, but 51-year-old Hawaiian photographer Kawika Singson seized his chance when the ocean briefly calmed. Navigating waters between Waikupanaha and Hawaii Volcano National Park on the Big Island, Singson filmed molten Kilauea volcano lava plunging beneath the ocean’s surface, where it starts forming new land. Singson described his April 2013 shoot: 'On this day, the ocean was calm, so my opportunity opened up and I went for it.' His footage, both dramatic and oddly soothing, shows lava—over 1,650°F (900°C), per the US Geological Survey—flowing into cool waters beneath clouds of toxic fumes. A thrill-seeking kayaker even appears in the video, adding to the daring atmosphere. Getting so close meant Singson wore fireproof boots and protective gear to prevent burning. He admits his actions are sometimes reckless: 'After a day filming, I sometimes wonder if it was a smart thing to do.' But the powerful sights of Hawaii’s landscape motivate him to continue despite risks from heat and hazardous gases. Kilauea, the youngest and one of the most active volcanoes on Hawaii’s Big Island, has erupted nonstop since 1983, creating dramatic views as glowing lava meets the sea and sky. Reflecting on his experience, Singson told The Huffington Post that challenges are constant, and staying focused and equipped is essential. He noted that while the videos are impressive, nothing compares to being close enough to feel the heat of active lava.
translated_content: Pran videyo pre kote lavi ap koule nan Oseyan Pasifik la se yon aksyon ra ak danjere, men fotograf Hawaeyen Kawika Singson, ki gen 51 an, pran chans li lè lanmè a te trankil yon ti moman. Pandan li tap navige ant Waikupanaha ak Hawaii Volcano National Park sou Gwo Zile a, Singson filme la ki sòti nan vòlkan Kilauea ap plonje anba dlo a, kote li kòmanse tounen tè nouvo. Singson dekri jan sa te pase nan mwa avril 2013: 'Jou sa a, lanmè a te poze, se te opòtinite mwen, epi mwen pwofite l.' Videyo li a, ki dramatik ak ap detann an menm tan, montre la ap koule ak plis pase 1,650°F (900°C) dapre US Geological Survey, desann nan dlo frèt anba nyaj gaz danjere. Ou ka menm wè yon kayaker ki renmen risk nan videyo a, sa bay sèn lan yon lòt nivo jan. Pou te rive pwoche konsa, Singson mete bòt ki reziste dife ak rad pwoteksyon pou evite boule. Li dakò pafwa sa li fè a pa twò reflechi: 'Apre yon jounen ap filme, mwen konn panse si sa m fè vrèman te saj.' Men pasyon l pou bèl peyizaj Hawaii a pouse l kontinye, malgre chalè ak gaz pwazon yo. Kilauea se pi jèn ak youn nan vòlkan ki pi aktif sou Gwo Zile Hawaii, li ap pete san rete depi 1983, bay bèl vizyon kote la klere rankontre ak syèl ak lanmè a. Reflechi sou eksperyans lan, Singson di The Huffington Post defi yo toujou la, epi li enpòtan pou w rete vijilan ak byen ekipe. Li di ke menm si videyo yo bèl, pa gen anyen ki konpare ak santi chalè aktyèl la bò vòlkan an.
post_content: Ever seen molten lava pour into the ocean? Hawaiian photographer Kawika Singson risked it all to capture up-close footage of Kilauea’s eruption—and even a thrill-seeking kayaker joins the show! Nature is wild! #LavaLife #BigIsland #Hawaii #EpicAdventure
translated_post: Ou janm wè lavi ap tonbe dwat nan lanmè? Fotograf Kawika Singson pran tout risk pou l filme eripsyon Kilauea pwoche tèlman! Gen menm yon kayaker fou ladan l! Nati se bèl bagay vre! #LaLavi #GwoZile #Hawaii #AksyonFou

article_content: At Gillingham School in Dorset, Jamie Davies, who is the Head of Year 7 and a qualified yoga instructor, is offering yoga sessions to help girls reconnect with PE lessons. Davies leads these classes for students and staff, tackling concerns over body image issues that can discourage girls from joining PE. A survey by the Youth Sport Trust found that only 59% of secondary school girls say they like PE, down from 74% in 2016, while boys’ enjoyment remains steady at 84%. The school has added various activities like yoga, mountain biking, rock climbing, bouldering, and walking to encourage students to stay active. article_content: By Gemma Mullin for MailOnline. Zuleika Henderson, 38, participated in the ice bucket challenge in front of Big Ben, London. The ice bucket challenge, which has swept the United States, has now become popular in the UK. The challenge involves pouring a bucket of freezing cold water over one's head to raise money for charity, before nominating others to take part. The trend began in America to raise awareness of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), also known as motor neurone disease. It went viral after Pete Frates, a former Boston College baseball player affected by ALS, nominated fellow Boston athletes. Celebrities such as Mark Zuckerberg, Justin Timberlake, and Bill Gates also joined in. The phenomenon has now taken off in the UK, with people supporting the MND Association. Zuleika Henderson from Crystal Palace, London, completed her ice bucket challenge outside Big Ben. She explained, 'I was challenged by a friend from the New York police department, who also challenged others from Canada, South Africa, and Australia, so I wanted to do something special for London.' 'It was extremely cold, and it confused some tourists visiting Big Ben—I may even appear in some of their holiday photos!' The communications manager added, 'A few minutes of discomfort is worth it if it raises awareness and donations for those facing this disease daily. I didn't know what ALS was before, so it worked in my case. The ice bucket challenge is doing a lot of good.' Many others are also participating, sometimes donating to charities beyond the original aim. Macmillan Cancer Support has received thousands of donations after encouraging people to use the hashtag #icebucketchallenge to share their videos online. The youngest participant so far, six-year-old Ianto, was filmed doing the challenge by his father, Shaun Gustard, who shared it on Facebook. Ianto used only cold water, in support of his mother Jane, who is battling cancer and recently had lymph nodes removed. Shaun Gustard told Macmillan Cancer Support: 'He's a sensitive child and was very upset after seeing his mother post-surgery. When he saw me do the ice bucket challenge the next day, he asked if he could do one for his mum. I didn't use ice, just cold water.' 'Macmillan have been an incredible support to Jane, so we're very proud of him and hope he's helped make a difference.' Manchester United midfielder Darren Fletcher also participated in the challenge, dedicating it to the James McCarthy Foundation. He received two buckets of cold water and challenged Cristiano Ronaldo and Wes Brown to take part next. Past participants include Paul Scholes and Gary Neville after the Class of 92 match. The only notable person to decline so far has been President Obama, who donated $100 to the ALS Association instead. Comedian Ricky Gervais posted his challenge on Facebook. The campaign has raised nearly $3 million for the ALS Association, 50% more than last year. Other celebrities such as Oprah Winfrey, Justin Timberlake, Emmy Rossum, Chloe Moretz, Mark Zuckerberg, and Dale Earnhardt Jr. joined, helping increase awareness and support for ALS.

Ice bucket challenge lan, ki te deja popilè Ozetazini, kounye a pwopaje rapidman nan UK la. Se yon defi kote moun vide yon bokit dlo trè frèt sou tèt yo pou ranmase lajan pou òganizasyon charitab, epi nominasyon lòt moun patisipe apre. Defi a te kòmanse Ozetazini pou ogmante konsyantizasyon sou Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), yo rele l tou maladi nè motè (MND). article_content: Significant changes in the healthcare market are pushing the pharmaceutical industry through a period of major transition. The traditional commercial model is now largely outdated. In the coming year, increasing economic pressures, shifting competitive landscapes, and stricter global regulations will intensify the need for companies to adopt market-driven strategies. The Numerof & Associates 2024 Global Pharma Outlook highlights core challenges for pharma companies as they revamp their business models. Chief among these is the rapid consolidation in healthcare delivery: out of more than 6,000 U.S. hospitals, only 1,500 remain independent. A surge in mergers and acquisitions has resulted in powerful, complex systems where purchasing authority now rests mainly with C-suite executives and population-based decision-makers, shifting influence away from physicians. This power shift has led manufacturers to form more specialized and experienced account management teams, like National Account Managers or Strategic Account Directors, who must respond to complex questions on pricing, reimbursement, product value, and clinical outcomes. Many organizations are still refining these approaches to adapt to the changing landscape. Customer engagement has also undergone significant change. While virtual interactions started as a pandemic necessity, 50-70% of engagements now happen virtually in most organizations. Despite advancements in digital marketing and analytics, effectively reaching key decision-makers remains a challenge. Some industry voices express doubts about the effectiveness of digital engagement. Operational complacency is diminishing under increasing regulation. The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act and broad regulatory changes across Europe are prompting companies to review their research, pricing, market access, and expense management. The effects of these changes are already starting to influence the industry, with further shifts likely. Decision-making over drug purchases is moving further from physicians toward payers, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), and consumers. These groups are holding firm on costs, demanding evidence for price changes, and increasingly bearing more of the financial burden as insurance costs rise. The pharmaceutical sector faces increased volatility, as regulatory demands raise development costs and timelines, payers strengthen their control, and public skepticism grows. Manufacturers must improve innovation in product development, reimbursement, and market adoption strategies. As noted in the report, demonstrating clear value and engaging with large, organized customers strategically are essential for success. Transitioning to these new models is not immediate. Companies frequently face internal resistance when justifying and maintaining new commercial strategies. Without significant adaptation, the industry's outdated commercial model risks leading to further challenges, as illustrated by missed opportunities during the pandemic’s Operation Warp Speed.

Rapò Numerof & Associates Global Pharma Outlook 2024 la mete aksan sou gwo defi ki devan endistri famasetik la pandan li ap eseye chanje modèl biznis li. Youn nan defi prensipal yo se konsolidasyon rapid sèvis swen sante yo: nan plis pase 6,000 lopital Ozetazini, se sèlman 1,500 ki kontinye endepandan. Chanjman sa yo pa fèt rapid. Envestisè ak lidè nan konpayi yo konn gen difikilte pou kontinye ak nouvo estrateji komèsyal la. Si pa gen bon ajisteman, ansyen modèl komèsyal la ka kontinye mete endistri a nan pwoblèm, jan sa te parèt pandan Operasyon Warp Speed pandan pandemi an.

article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) – Prosecutors are requesting another delay in the start of Michael Jackson's doctor's involuntary manslaughter trial, but the judge will wait until next month to make a decision. 'I'm not surprised by all of this,' Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Michael Pastor said during a hearing on Friday. The trial has already been postponed twice since Dr. Conrad Murray invoked his right to a speedy trial after his arraignment in January. 'When I got involved, I said, “It ain't gonna happen,”' Pastor said, referencing the original late-March start date. He described the case as 'creepy crawly.' Jury selection began in May but was delayed after the defense requested more time for its expert witnesses to prepare for testimony by new prosecution experts. As a result, Pastor dismissed hundreds of prospective jurors and rescheduled the trial to start on September 8. Deputy District Attorney David Walgren said on Friday morning that the prosecution needed an additional three weeks to prepare because of scheduling issues. Defense attorneys did not object to moving jury selection to the end of September. Pastor, who explained he had rearranged several cases, including capital cases, to accommodate the September trial, said he would decide at a July 12 hearing. On Friday, the judge also approved a plan allowing both defense lawyers and prosecutors to view several hours of raw video footage of Michael Jackson's last rehearsals, which were purchased by Sony Pictures for its film 'This Is It.' Pastor has not yet ruled on which video clips, if any, the defense will be allowed to show at trial. Previously, he limited the prosecution to using only the raw video from Jackson's last two days alive. Saturday will mark the second anniversary of Jackson's death, which was determined by the Los Angeles coroner to result from an overdose of propofol, along with other drugs. Dr. Murray, who was hired as Jackson's personal physician as the singer prepared for comeback concerts in London, is charged in connection with Jackson's death.

'Mwen pa etone pa sa,' Jij Tribinal Siperyè Konte Los Angeles Michael Pastor te di pandan yon odyans Vandredi. Jijman an deja ranvwaye de fwa depi Dr. Conrad Murray sèvi ak dwa li pou yon jijman rapid apre li te parèt devan tribinal an janvye. 'Lè mwen te antre ladan, mwen te di, “Sa p ap rive,”' Pastor te di, pandan l ap pale de dat orijinal fin mwa Mas la. Li dekri ka a kòm 'yon bagay k ap trennen.' Seleksyon jiri te kòmanse an Me men yo te ranvwaye li apre defans lan te mande plis tan pou ekspè temwen pa yo prepare pou ekspè nouvo pwosekitè yo. Kòm konsekans, Pastor te voye ale plizyè santèn potansyèl jiri epi remete dat jijman an pou 8 septanm. Adjwen Avoka Distri David Walgren te di Vandredi maten ke pwosekitè yo bezwen twa semèn an plis paske gen pwoblèm òganizasyon. Avoka defans yo pa t opoze ak deplase seleksyon jiri a pou fen mwa septanm. Dr. Murray, ki te anboche kòm doktè pèsonèl Jackson pandan li t ap prepare pou konsè retou li nan Lond, akize nan lanmò Jackson lan.

Michael Economides, a renowned global energy expert and strong advocate for hydraulic fracturing (also known as hydro-fracking), died of a heart attack at age 64 while flying from Spain to Chile over the Atlantic Ocean. Economides served as a professor at the University of Houston’s Cullen College of Engineering, where his international consulting work led him to teach only one course per semester. According to his wife, Christine Economides, he was passionate about travel, writing, and collaborating globally.

A prominent supporter of hydraulic fracturing and scientific innovation in horizontal drilling, Economides advised major energy companies worldwide, such as China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC), Italy’s ENI, and firms in Russia and Venezuela. He was the author or co-author of 15 books, including the bestseller 'The Color of Oil', and made regular appearances on networks like CNBC, CNN, and Fox Business.

Hydraulic fracturing, or hydro-fracking, is a technique that uses a pressurized mixture of chemicals to extract natural gas from underground, but it has been criticized for its potential to contaminate water supplies and cause health issues.

Michael Economides is survived by his wife, Christine, and their two children.
translated_content:
Michael Economides, yon ekspè enèji entènasyonal ki te yon gwo defansè pou fraksyonaj idwolik (yo rele tou idwo-fracking), mouri akòz yon kriz kè a laj 64 an pandan li t ap vole soti Espay pou ale Chili, anlè Oseyan Atlantik la. Economides te pwofesè nan Cullen College of Engineering nan University of Houston, kote l te jwenn anpil demann pou konsiltasyon entènasyonal, sa ki te fè li anseye sèlman yon klas pa semès. Selon madanm li, Christine Economides, li te renmen vwayaje, ekri, epi kolabore ak pwofesyonèl atravè lemond.

Kòm yon defansè enpòtan pou fraksyonaj idwolik ak inovasyon syantifik nan perçaj orizontal, Economides te bay konsèy bay gwo konpayi enèji mondyal tankou China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC), ENI (Itali), epi tou konpayi nan Larisi ak Venezyela. Li te ekri oswa ko-ekri 15 liv, tankou pi popilè a 'The Color of Oil', epi li te souvan parèt sou chèn televizyon tankou CNBC, CNN, ak Fox Business.

Fraksyonaj idwolik, oswa idwo-fracking, se yon teknik kote yo enjekte yon melanj likid anba presyon pou retire gaz natirèl anba tè. Teknik sa a resevwa anpil kritik paske yo di li ka kontamine sous dlo ak lakòz pwoblèm sante.

Michael Economides kite madanm li, Christine, ak de pitit dèyè.
post_content: Energy expert Michael Economides, a major advocate for hydro-fracking, has died at 64 after a heart attack during a flight. He was known worldwide for his work and advice to major energy companies. #RIP #EnergyNews

article_content:
Rep. George Santos pleaded not guilty on Friday to a superseding indictment that accuses him of identity theft, unauthorized use of donors’ credit cards, and making false statements to federal election officials. His trial is set for September 9, 2024, and is expected to last three weeks. The 23-count indictment, filed earlier this month, charges the New York congressman with two counts of wire fraud, two counts of making materially false statements to the Federal Election Commission (FEC), two counts of falsifying records to obstruct the FEC, two counts of aggravated identity theft, and one count of access device fraud, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of New York. 

Santos will continue to be represented by his lawyer, Joe Murray, despite a possible conflict of interest with others connected to the case. These new charges follow the recent indictment of Santos’s former campaign finance chief, Nancy Marks. Prosecutors allege that Santos and Marks enlisted the names of 10 family members, without their knowledge, to make it appear as though Santos had enough support to qualify for party funding. Marks has pleaded guilty to federal conspiracy. 

The indictment also claims Santos falsely reported lending his campaign $500,000 while only having $8,000 on hand. Bail conditions were unchanged following Friday’s hearing, and the next status conference is set for December 12. Previously, in May, Santos was indicted on 13 federal counts, including wire fraud, money laundering, theft of public funds, and making false statements to the House of Representatives. He also pleaded not guilty to those charges. Despite the latest allegations, Santos told reporters he will not step down from Congress.

Jijman an fikse pou 9 septanm 2024 epi yo atann li ap dire twa semèn. Akizasyon an, ki gen 23 pwen, lonje dwèt sou kongresis New York la pou de fwa fwod pa fil, de fwa fo deklarasyon bay Komisyon Elektoral Federal (FEC), de fwa falsifikasyon dosye pou anpeche FEC la, de fwa vòl idantite agrave ak youn fwa fwod ak aparèy aksè, dapre Biwo Pwokirè Etazini pou Distri Lès New York.

Santos pral kontinye gen Joe Murray kòm avoka l, malgre kèk posib konfli enterè ak lòt moun ki enplike nan dosye a. Nouvo akizasyon sa yo vini apre akizasyon kont ansyen chèf finans kanpay Santos la, Nancy Marks. Pwokirè yo di Santos ak Marks te itilize non 10 manm fanmi yo san yo pa te konnen, pou fè li parèt tankou Santos te gen ase sipò pou jwenn lajan pati a. Marks te deja plede koupab pou konplo federal.

Akizasyon an di tou Santos te bay fo enfòmasyon sou yon prè $500,000 li te di li te fè kanpay li pandan li te sèlman gen $8,000. Kondisyon libète li pa chanje apre odyans vandredi a, e pwochen konferans sou dosye a fikse pou 12 desanm. Li te plede non koupab pou akizasyon sa yo tou. Malgre tout sa, Santos di laprès li p ap kite plas li nan Kongrè a.
