article_content: Republican presidential hopefuls Nikki Haley and Vivek Ramaswamy offered contrasting reactions to Donald Trump's recent comment calling his political opponents 'vermin.' Speaking at a town hall in Newton, Iowa, former UN Ambassador Nikki Haley stated her disagreement with Trump’s remarks. She referenced previous instances when she opposed Trump’s comments, such as his praise of Hezbollah and criticism of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu during a crisis. Haley added that, while she believes Trump’s intentions are generally good, the persistent chaos surrounding him must come to an end. In contrast, biotech entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy downplayed the controversy, accusing mainstream media of sensationalizing Trump’s words instead of focusing on policy issues. He argued that the real discussion should center on substantive matters facing the country. During a campaign speech in New Hampshire, Trump reaffirmed his stance by vowing to purge 'communists, Marxists, fascists, and radical left thugs' whom he labeled as 'vermin.' He argued that the radical left, not the right, poses the central threat to the nation. President Joe Biden criticized Trump’s use of the word 'vermin,' drawing a comparison to language used in Nazi Germany in the 1930s. Biden also warned that Trump would pursue 'revenge and retribution' if reelected. CNN polling suggests Haley is currently emerging as Trump’s chief challenger in early primary states like South Carolina and New Hampshire, where she holds second place. According to the latest national poll by Fox News, Ramaswamy stands in fourth place at 7%, behind Haley (11%), Florida Governor Ron DeSantis (14%), and Trump, who leads with 62%. The US presidential election is scheduled for November 5, 2024.
translated_content: Kandida Repibliken yo Nikki Haley ak Vivek Ramaswamy bay repons diferan sou dènye deklarasyon Donald Trump ki te rele advèsè politik li yo 'vermin'. Pandan yon rankont nan Newton, Iowa, ansyen Anbasadè Nasyonzini Nikki Haley di li pa dakò ak sa Trump te di. Li raple lòt okazyon li pa t dakò ak Trump, tankou lè li te pale byen de Hezbollah oswa kritike Premye Minis Izrayelyen Netanyahu anplis de kriz la. Haley ajoute ke menm si li panse Trump gen bòn volonte, dezòd ki toujou ap antouraj li a dwe fini. Anplis, Vivek Ramaswamy, yon antreprenè biyoteknoloji, pa bay pawòl Trump yo anpil enpòtans. Li kritike medya prensipal yo paske y ap mete aksan sou deklarasyon sa yo olye yo pale sou vre pwoblèm politik yo. Li di diskisyon an ta dwe sou kesyon serye peyi a ap fè fas. Nan yon diskou kanpay li nan New Hampshire, Trump kontinye menm jan an, li pwomèt pou elimine 'kominis, marxist, fasist ak bandi radikal goch' li te rele 'vermin'. Li ensiste se goch radikal, pa dwat la, ki reprezante menas prensipal pou peyi a. Prezidan Joe Biden kritike itilizasyon mo 'vermin' pa Trump, li di pawòl sa son tankou sa ki te chante nan Almay Nazi ane 1930 yo. Biden di Trump t ap chèche 'vanjans ak repwazman' si l ta tounen prezidan. Sondaj CNN yo montre Haley ap sèvi kom pi gwo opozan Trump nan premye eleksyon primè yo, espesyalman nan South Carolina ak New Hampshire kote li klase dezyèm. Dapre dènye sondaj nasyonal Fox News, Ramaswamy an katriyèm plas ak 7%, dèyè Haley (11%), Gouvènè Florid Ron DeSantis (14%) ak Trump ki mennen ak 62%. Eleksyon prezidansyèl Etazini fikse pou 5 novanm 2024.

article_content: Liverpool scout Neil Richardson attended the match at Bramall Lane on Sunday, where Sheffield United came from behind to defeat Nottingham Forest 3-1. Liverpool’s Conor Coady, currently on loan at Sheffield United, scored the equalizer in the 66th minute and likely received a positive report from Richardson. Richardson was also monitoring Nottingham Forest defender Jamaal Lascelles and Sheffield United defender Harry Maguire as Liverpool looks to strengthen its defense. Jamaal Lascelles, 20, is attracting interest from Everton, Tottenham, Arsenal, Newcastle, and Liverpool. He has long been seen as a future England international and, after recovering from injuries, has regained strong form under manager Billy Davies. Maguire, also 20, has been watched by Chelsea, Manchester United, and Southampton. While strong defensively, he may not quite possess the ball-playing qualities Liverpool is seeking. Liverpool is also exploring the addition of a left-back, a backup goalkeeper, a winger, a striker, and another midfielder during the summer transfer window. Scouts have continued to watch Udinese striker Luis Muriel, but the Colombian has struggled for goals this season. Manchester United scouts recently attended a Sporting Lisbon match to observe midfielder William Carvalho, 21, a Portugal international represented by Jorge Mendes. Carvalho was booked as Sporting defeated Olhanense 1-0, with Carlos Mane scoring the winner. United are also monitoring Marcos Rojo, Sporting’s 23-year-old Argentine left-back, who almost transferred to Fulham in the previous window. Manchester United is set to lose Nemanja Vidic, with Inter Milan aiming to finalize his transfer. Both Rio Ferdinand and Patrice Evra are expected to depart, though Evra has an option to extend his stay. Inter is also interested in Evra. Real Madrid has recently made inquiries about Luciano Vietto, a highly regarded 20-year-old striker from Racing Club. Other European teams are interested as well. Vietto, represented by Jorge Cysterpiller (formerly Diego Maradona’s agent), is compared to Sergio Aguero and Carlos Tevez. Real is negotiating a contract renewal with Karim Benzema but has Vietto, valued around £8 million, on their radar as a potential future star. Everton, Liverpool, and Atletico Madrid (coached by Vietto’s ex-manager Diego Simeone) are also interested. England goalkeeper Jack Butland is close to a loan move to Leeds United as Stoke allows him to seek regular playing time. With Asmir Begovic recovered from injury and Thomas Sorensen available, Stoke is open to letting the 20-year-old leave on loan. Leeds, preparing for a promotion push and amid a possible takeover by Italian Massimo Cellino, is interested in Butland, who previously shined on loan at Barnsley. Manager Brian McDermott hopes to bring him in to compete for the starting spot. Butland joined Stoke for £4 million from Birmingham in January 2013. He debuted for England at age 19, making him the youngest-ever goalkeeper for the national team. He played for Stoke this season before Begovic returned. Leeds is also searching for a striker, considering loan moves for Sunderland’s Connor Wickham and Hull’s Matty Fryatt. Sven-Goran Eriksson, currently managing Guangzhou R&F in China, wants to sign Newcastle United striker Shola Ameobi. Eriksson is after a British-style center forward, and Chinese clubs have also shown interest in Ameobi’s teammate Papiss Cisse. China’s transfer window closes at the end of February, as does Russia’s. Although speculation persists, Newcastle is unlikely to let key strikers leave before the season’s end. However, a substantial offer could tempt Ameobi, 32, who may also weigh his options after the campaign. Newcastle could also lose Mathieu Debuchy and Hatem Ben Arfa (with Inter Milan interested in Ben Arfa), and the club is scouting replacements, including 21-year-old River Plate midfielder Manuel Lanzini, an Italian passport holder reportedly valued at about £6 million. Several League One teams are considering a summer bid for York City striker Wes Fletcher, 22. After spells at Manchester United and Liverpool as a youth and then Burnley, Fletcher joined York where he has scored 13 goals this season. With a year left on his contract, York will likely seek about £150,000 for his transfer.
translated_content: Scout Liverpool la, Neil Richardson, te ale gade match ki te jwe nan Bramall Lane dimanch pase, kote Sheffield United fè yon gwo retou pou bat Nottingham Forest 3-1. Conor Coady, ki sou prete Liverpool bay Sheffield United, make gòl egalizasyon an nan 66èm minit lan epi sanble li resevwa yon bon rapò nan men Richardson. Richardson t ap swiv defansè Nottingham Forest la Jamaal Lascelles ak defansè Sheffield United la Harry Maguire paske Liverpool vle ranfòse defans li. Manchester United prè pou pèdi Nemanja Vidic ak Inter Milan ap eseye finalize tranzaksyon li. Rio Ferdinand ak Patrice Evra gen anpil chans kite tou, men Evra ka rete paske li gen yon opsyon kontrakt. Inter enterese ak Evra tou. Li te fè premye match li ak Angletè a laj 19 an, li se pi jèn gadyen peyi a jamè genyen. Li te jwe pou Stoke sezon sa avan Begovic retounen. Leeds ap chèche tou yon atakan, epi konsidere prete Connor Wickham (Sunderland) ak Matty Fryatt (Hull). Sven-Goran Eriksson, kounye a manadjè Guangzhou R&F nan Lachin, swete siyen atakan Newcastle United la Shola Ameobi. Eriksson vle yon veritab atakan britanik epi klèb chinwa yo enterese tou ak Papiss Cisse ki menm klib ak Ameobi. Fenèt transfè Lachin ak Larisi yo ap fèmen nan fen fevriye. Malgre gen rimè, Newcastle pa panse lage pi bon atakan li avan fen sezon an. Men, yon gwo òf ka fè Ameobi, 32 an, chanje lide si li vle esplore plis opsyon apre sezon an. Newcastle ka pèdi tou Mathieu Debuchy ak Hatem Ben Arfa (Inter Milan enterese ak Ben Arfa), epi klub la ap gade ranplasan tankou milye River Plate la, Manuel Lanzini, 21 an, ki gen paspò Itali epi valè l apeprè £6 milyon. article_content: At least 27 people have died and more than 70 remain missing after a boat capsized late Friday in Mbandaka, a city in northwest Congo, officials said. The locally made boat was transporting over 100 passengers along the Congo River to Bolomba in Equateur Province, according to Deputy Provincial Governor Taylor Nganzi. "So far, 27 victims have been recovered and taken to the morgue at the general hospital in Mbandaka," Nganzi reported. Authorities have begun an investigation into the cause of the accident. The New Civil Society of Congo, a local civil society group led by Jean-Pierre Wangela, claimed the death toll was 49 and attributed the accident to an engine failure. Contradictory casualty numbers are common in such incidents, and the differences could not be immediately reconciled. Volunteers and rescuers, accompanied by families of victims, continue searching for survivors and bodies. "We are supervising the search with river services and alongside the victims’ families," Nganzi stated. Boat accidents frequently occur on the Congo River and the country's lakes, mainly because makeshift boats—which are often overloaded—are widely used. Many people in Congo's northwest rely on river transport due to poor road infrastructure and lower costs. Despite a government ban on night travel intended to prevent such accidents, the directive is often ignored.

Bato lokal la t ap transpòte plis pase 100 pasaje sou rivyè Kongo pou ale Bolomba nan pwovens Equateur, selon Taylor Nganzi, vis-gouvènè pwovens lan. "Jiskaprezan, 27 viktim jwenn epi pote yo lakay mòg lopital jeneral Mbandaka a," Nganzi rapòte. Otorite yo kòmanse yon ankèt pou chèche konnen koz aksidan an. Nouvo Sosyete Sivil Kongo a, yon òganizasyon sivil lokal ki gen Jean-Pierre Wangela kòm prezidan, di kantite moun ki mouri a se 49 epi yo mete koz aksidan an sou do yon pann motè. Chif viktim yo soti diferan sous, ki konn rive souvan nan sitiyasyon konsa, epi diferans yo pa ka konfime tousuit. Volontè ak sekouris, ansanm ak fanmi viktim yo, kontinye ap chèche sivivan ak kadav. "Nou ap sipèvize rechèch la ak sèvis rivyè yo ak an prezans fanmi viktim yo," Nganzi deklare. Aksidan bato rive souvan sou rivyè Kongo ak lak peyi a, sitou paske yo itilize anpil bato brikole epi yo souvan chaje twòp. Anpil moun nan nòdwès Kongo depann de transpò sou rivyè paske wout yo pa bon epi li pi bon mache. Malgre leta entèdi vwayaj lannuit pou evite aksidan konsa, anpil moun pa respekte mezi sa a.

article_content: Las Vegas hospitality workers have overwhelmingly approved a new five-year contract with Caesars Entertainment, ending months of difficult negotiations and averting a major strike. According to the Culinary Workers Union, 99% of members voted to endorse the deal, calling it a landmark agreement for 10,000 employees. The union is also on track to ratify similar agreements soon with MGM Resorts International and Wynn Resorts, which together with Caesars collectively employ more than 35,000 people on the Las Vegas Strip. The agreements, finalized earlier this month just hours before a planned walkout at 18 casino hotels, cover iconic properties like Bellagio, Paris Las Vegas, and MGM Grand. Union chief negotiator Ted Pappageorge credited workers for their commitment, noting many were willing to risk pay cuts if a strike happened. After devoting personal time throughout seven months of negotiations, they won substantial wage hikes, stronger job security, and lighter housekeeping workloads amid new technological shifts. Pappageorge, who participated in a notable six-year Las Vegas hotel strike in the 1990s, underlined that these gains resulted from broad collective action, including rallies, demonstrations, and strike votes. He stated the new contract provides an average wage increase of 32%, raising pay from $26 to $35 per hour with benefits over the contract’s term, including a 10% raise in the first year. Altogether, this will mean about $2 billion in combined wage and benefit advances from Caesars, MGM, and Wynn. Casino operators acknowledged the vital role union members play in their success, expressing support for the contracts, which include record pay increases and opportunities associated with the expansion of union jobs on the Strip. Had a strike occurred—potentially coinciding with the Formula 1 debut in Las Vegas—it could have led to immediate disruptions in hotel room cleaning, restaurant service, and other hospitality operations, with widespread economic impacts. This contract win comes during a year marked by significant union activity nationwide, including high-profile strikes in Hollywood, at UPS, and among Detroit casino workers.
translated_content: Travayè otèl Las Vegas yo apwouve masivman nouvo kontra senk ane ak Caesars Entertainment, sa ki mete fen nan plizyè mwa negosyasyon difisil epi evite yon gwo grèv. Dapre Inyon Travayè Culinaires la, 99% nan manm yo te vote pou kontra a, li konsidere kòm yon viktwa enpòtan pou 10,000 anplwaye yo. Inyon an tou sou wout pou ratifye byento kontra menm jan an ak MGM Resorts International ak Wynn Resorts, ki ansanm ak Caesars, okipe plis pase 35,000 moun sou Las Vegas Strip la. Kontra sa yo te finalize pi bonè mwa sa a sèlman kèk èdtan anvan yo te gen pou lanse yon grèv nan 18 otèl kazino, kouvri gwo otèl tankou Bellagio, Paris Las Vegas ak MGM Grand. Ted Pappageorge, chèf negosyatè inyon an, felisite travayè yo pou angajman yo, e li mete aksan sou anpil te pare pou riske salè yo si ta gen grèv. Apre sèt mwa ap negosye kote yo mete tan pèsonèl yo sou kote, yo reyalize gwo ogmantasyon salè, pi plis sekirite travay, ak rediksyon chaj travay fanm chanm nan, menm ak chanjman teknolojik yo ap vini. Pappageorge, ki te patisipe nan yon grèv sis ane nan otèl Las Vegas lan 1990 yo, mete aksan sou rezilta ki soti nan aksyon kolektif tankou manifestasyon ak vòt grèv. Li di nouvo kontra a ap pote yon ogmantasyon salè 32% an mwayèn, salè yo ap pase de $26 rive $35 pa èdtan ak benefis pandan tout kontra a, ansanm ak yon ogmantasyon 10% premye ane a. Sa ap bay apeprè $2 milya dola total pou salè ak benefis ki soti nan kampani kazino yo. Kampani kazino yo rekonèt wòl enpòtan travayè yo nan siksè yo, epi yo di yo sipòte kontra yo ki pote pi gwo ogmantasyon salè ak plis chans ogmante travay inyon sou Strip la. Si yo te fè grèv la—ki te kapab koincide ak premye kous Fòmil 1 nan Las Vegas—sa ta lakoz pwoblèm imedyat nan netwayaj chanm, sèvis restoran, ak lòt sèvis, epi sa ta frape ekonomi lokal la. Kontra sa a rive pandan ane kote inyon travayè yo te gen gwo aktivite atravè peyi a, tankou grèv nan Hollywood, UPS ak kazino Detroit yo.

article_content: Astronomers recently discovered two exceptionally old planets orbiting the star HIP 11952, which is about 375 light years from Earth. The research led by Dr. Johny Setiawan estimates these planets are around 12.8 billion years old—almost three times the age of Earth—making them among the oldest known exoplanets. One of these planets is approximately the size of Jupiter, while the second is about three times larger. Scientists identified the planets by observing the star's subtle wobbles using the radial velocity technique at the European Southern Observatory in La Silla, Chile. This finding challenges previous assumptions that planet formation was unlikely in the early universe because stars lacked heavy elements like iron. HIP 11952, for example, has just 1% of the iron content of our Sun. Dr. Setiawan pointed out that such an environment was previously thought to make planet formation nearly impossible. The presence of these planets prompts questions about possible life there. Any potential life forms would differ greatly from Earth's, given the scarcity of heavy elements. While some debate continues about whether these planets could have formed later in the star's evolution, Dr. Setiawan doubts this, as he notes that planets usually form soon after stars are born. The formation of so-called ‘second-generation’ planets is still an open topic in astronomy.
translated_content: Astwonòm yo fèk dekouvri de planèt ki ansyen anpil k ap fè wonn kò yo otou etwal HIP 11952, ki twouve li apeprè 375 ane limyè lwen Latè. Rechèch la, anba direksyon Dr. Johny Setiawan, estime planèt sa yo gen anviwon 12.8 milya ane — prèske twa fwa pi gran pase laj Latè — ki fè yo pami pi vye ekzo-planèt jiskaprezan. Youn nan planèt yo gen mwens plis menm grandè ak Jipitè, pandan ke lòt la se anviwon twa fwa pi gwo. Syantis yo detekte yo avèk metòd vitès radial lè yo obsève mouvman etwal la nan Obsèvatwa Ewòp Sid la, La Silla, Chili. Dekouvèt sa a kont kwayans ki te genyen deja sou difikilte pou planèt fòme nan tan linivè te pa gen anpil metal, paske etwal yo pa t genyen anpil eleman lou tankou fè. Pou egzanp, HIP 11952 sèlman gen anviwon 1% fè Solèy la genyen. Dr. Setiawan mete aksan sou jan li te panse li pa posib pou planèt fòme nan kondisyon konsa. Sa soulve kesyon sou si lavi ta ka egziste sou planèt sa yo. Nenpòt fòm lavi ki ta egziste la ta yon bagay ki byen diferan de sa sou Latè paske pa gen ase eleman lou. Gen kèk diskisyon toujou sou si planèt sa yo te ka fòme pita pandan lavi etwal la, men Dr. Setiawan pa panse sa posib paske dabitid planèt fòme pwèske touswit apre etwal la fenk parèt. article_content: Gregory Yetman, a suspect involved in the January 6th U.S. Capitol attack, has surrendered to authorities in New Jersey without incident, according to the FBI. Yetman turned himself in to Monroe Township police on Friday morning, officials reported. "We're thankful this ended without incident," the FBI stated, also expressing gratitude to the public for their help during the search. Yetman, 47, faces several charges — including some felonies — related to the January 6th assault on the U.S. Capitol. Charges include assaulting officers, obstructing law enforcement during civil disorder, entering and remaining in a restricted building or grounds, engaging in physical violence in a restricted area, and committing acts of violence on Capitol grounds or within buildings. He will be held by the U.S. Marshals Service over the weekend and is scheduled to make his initial court appearance in Newark, New Jersey, on Monday. A federal arrest warrant for Yetman was issued on November 6, and authorities had been searching for him in Helmetta, a borough in Middlesex County, as of Wednesday. At the time of the Capitol attack, Yetman was a military police sergeant in the New Jersey Army National Guard, a spokesperson confirmed to ABC News. He served about 12 years in the National Guard and was honorably discharged in March 2022. Authorities announced on Thursday that a $10,000 reward was being offered for Yetman's capture. According to the Department of Justice, more than 1,200 people have been charged in connection with the January 6th attack in the 34 months since it occurred. Reporting by Meredith Deliso of ABC News.
translated_content: Gregory Yetman, yon sispèk ki gen rapò ak atak 6 janvye sou Kapitòl Etazini an, remèt tèt li bay otorite yo nan New Jersey san okenn ensidan, dapre FBI. Yetman ale bay lapolis Monroe Township vandredi maten, dapre otorite yo. "Nou rekonesan sa fini san okenn ensidan," FBI a deklare pandan li remèsye piblik la pou èd yo pandan rechèch la. Yetman, ki gen 47 an, ap fè fas ak plizyè akizasyon—pami yo kèk krim—ki gen rapò ak atak 6 janvye sou Kapitòl la. Akizasyon yo enkli atake ofisye, bloke travay lapolis pandan dezòd sivil, antre epi rete nan yon zòn oswa bilding entèdi, patisipe nan vyolans fizik nan zòn entèdi, ak fè zak vyolans sou teritwa oswa nan bilding Kapitòl la. Yo pral kenbe li anba Swivans U.S. Marshals Service pandan wikenn lan e li prevwa gen premye aparisyon li nan tribinal Newark, New Jersey, lendi. Yo te bay mandat arestasyon federal pou Yetman 6 novanm epi otorite yo t ap chèche li nan Helmetta, yon bouk nan Middlesex County, jan yo di mèkredi. Lè atak la te fèt sou Kapitòl la, Yetman te sèvi kòm sòsye lapolis militè nan New Jersey Army National Guard, yon pòtpawòl konfime bay ABC News. Li te fè anviwon 12 ane nan National Guard epi li te soti ak onè nan mwa mas 2022. Otorite yo te anonse jedi ke yo mete yon prim $10,000 pou arestasyon Yetman. Dapre Depatman Jistis la, plis pase 1,200 moun deja akize pou patisipasyon yo nan atak 6 janvye a pandan 34 mwa depi li te fèt. Rapò sa a sòti nan Meredith Deliso pou ABC News.

article_content: A new study indicates that in the United States, old age is more closely linked to a person's independence than to physical signs like wrinkles. Michelle Barnhart, a researcher at Oregon State University, led the research, which shows that abilities such as shopping, driving, and cooking are considered essential for maintaining a sense of youth. The study involved interviews with people in their late 80s and their adult children or caregivers. Findings suggest that losing the ability to manage everyday tasks independently is what society often labels as 'old.' Personal independence is therefore viewed as a key marker of aging. The research also reveals that Baby Boomers tend to reject the 'old' label for themselves while sometimes applying it to their aging parents, sparking disagreements. Older individuals may see themselves as capable, even as their children perceive them differently. Barnhart points out that stereotypes about older adults persist, portraying them as forgetful or unwilling to adapt. For example, 89-year-old Abbie recounted that during a doctor's visit, the physician spoke only to her daughters rather than to her. The study argues that society often undervalues the wisdom of older adults in favor of focusing on their limitations, and warns that unless attitudes change, these negative views will continue. The full research will be published in the April 2013 issue of the Journal of Consumer Research.
translated_content: Yon nouvo etid montre ke Ozetazini, laj asosye plis ak endepandans yon moun pase ak siy fizik tankou rid. Michelle Barnhart, yon rechèchè nan Oregon State University, dirije etid la, ki montre ke kapasite pou fè makèt, kondwi machin, ak kwit manje konsidere kòm kle pou konsève sans jenès lan. Etid la fèt ak moun ki nan fen 80 an epi ak pitit granmoun oswa swayan yo. Rezilta yo montre ke lè yon moun pa kapab jere aktivite chak jou pou kont li, sosyete a rekonèt moun sa kòm 'vye'. Endepandans pèsonèl vin yon gwo makè pou laj. Rechèch la mete aksan tou sou reyalite kote jenerasyon Baby Boomer yo refize aksepte etikèt 'vye' sou tèt pa yo, men yo souvan bay paran yo ki aje tit sa, sa ki ka kreye dezakò. Granmoun yo ka wè tèt yo kòm toujou kapab, menm lè pitit yo panse le kontrè. Barnhart montre kijan estereyotip negatif sou granmoun toujou egziste, kote yo wè yo tankou moun ki bliye fasil oswa ki pa vle chanje. Pa ekzanp, Abbie, yon dam 89 an, rakonte yon doktè ki te pale sèlman ak pitit fi li olye li pale avè l. Etid la di sosyete souvan neglije valè ak sajès granmoun ki aje yo epi konsantre plis sou limit yo genyen. Li avèti si mantalite sa pa chanje, menm kalite prejije sa yo ap kontinye. Etid la ap parèt nan Journal of Consumer Research nan mwa Avril 2013.
post_content: Think old age is all about wrinkles? A new study shows independence matters most! Driving, shopping & cooking keep you young—and when that's lost, society labels you 'old.' Let's value wisdom, not just age! #Aging #Independence #Wisdom
translated_post: Ou panse laj grandi se sèlman ak rid? Nouvo rechèch fè konnen endepandans pi enpòtan! Kondwi, fè makèt, kwit manje kenbe w jèn—lè sa fini, moun di ou 'vye.' Annou respekte sajès granmoun yo! #Laj #Endepandans #Sajès

article_content: At least 40 people have died after a glacial lake burst its banks, triggering flash floods in the Indian Himalayas. According to government officials who spoke to Reuters on Friday (Oct 6), rescuers are continuing their search for dozens of missing people for a second day. The disaster happened at Lhonak Lake in the northeastern state of Sikkim after heavy rains and a probable avalanche on Wednesday caused the lake to overflow, resulting in major flooding in the Teesta river. This event is among the worst disasters in the region in more than 50 years. It is the latest in a series of extreme weather events in the Himalayas, many of which scientists blame on climate change. Authorities in Sikkim report that about 22,000 people have been affected. Scientists and officials have been developing an early warning system for glacial floods at Lhonak Lake, but they told Reuters it was not yet fully operational and could have given people more time to evacuate.
translated_content: Omenm 40 moun mouri apre yon lak glas pete epi lakòz inondasyon rapid nan Himalaya Endyen an. Dapre otorite gouvènman ki te pale ak Reuters vandredi (6 Oktòb), sekouris yo kontinye chèche plizyè dizèn moun ki disparèt depi dezyèm jou a. Katastwòf la te fèt bò Lhonak Lake nan eta nòdès Sikkim, apre gwo lapli ak yon lavalas sou mèkredi ki te lakoz lak la debòde epi provoke gwo inondasyon sou larivyè Teesta. Sa a se youn nan pi gwo katastwòf nan rejyon an depi plis pase 50 lane, epi li se dènye nan seri move tan ekstrèm nan Himalaya yo—yon bagay anpil syantis mete sou chanjman klimatik. Otorite nan Sikkim di anviwon 22,000 moun afekte. Syantifik ak otorite yo ap devlope yon sistèm alèt bonè pou inondasyon lak glas nan Lhonak Lake, men yo di Reuters li poko totalman fonksyone e li te ka bay plis tan pou moun yo evakye.
post_content: Tragedy hits Sikkim as a glacial lake burst triggers flash floods—at least 40 dead and 22,000 affected. Scientists say this is another climate crisis warning. Stay safe everyone! #Sikkim #Himalayas #ClimateChange
translated_post: Gwo trajedi frape Sikkim! Yon lak glas pete, plis pase 40 moun mouri, 22,000 afekte. Syantis di sa se avètisman chanjman klimatik ankò. Pran prekosyon tout moun! #Sikkim #Himalaya #ChanjmanKlimatik

article_content: During October nights in Wasco, California, some residents have encountered people dressed as creepy clowns roaming the streets. These individuals wear various costumes, including masks, wigs, jumpsuits, and carry different props like balloons. Since October 1, locals have reported these unusual sightings. Community responses are mixed. While some residents use social media to track clown appearances and actively search for them, others are disturbed or frightened by the clowns' presence. Rumors circulate about the number of people involved—some suggest it's a single person, while others believe a group is responsible. There have been reports, including from children, of scary encounters, but police confirm they have found no evidence linking the clowns to criminal activity or made any arrests related to the sightings. Despite causing unease, many see the clown appearances as a humorous Halloween event, with people taking photos and turning the situation into local entertainment. One resident shared that his participation in dressing as a clown started as part of a photography project with his wife, with no intention of frightening the community. The phenomenon appears to have inspired others to imitate the act, dividing local opinions between fear and amusement.

Gen moun ki itilize rezo sosyal pou lokalize payaso yo epi chèche yo, pandan ke gen lòt ki santi yo boulvèse ou pè lè yo wè yo. Rimè ap sikile sou konbyen moun ki patisipe—gen ki panse se yon sèl, lòt kwè se plizyè moun ansanm. Fenomèn sa a fè anpil lòt moun imite l, e opinyon divize ant moun ki pè ak moun ki pran plezi.

article_content: Heavy rains and severe flooding driven by the El Niño weather phenomenon have devastated southern South America this week, leading to at least three fatalities and mass evacuations. According to officials, two elderly individuals aged 70 and 84 as well as an 11-year-old girl died in Paraguay after their homes collapsed in two storm-stricken towns. Arsenio Zarate, head of Paraguay's National Emergency Office, reported on Friday that more than 40 locations had suffered major damage. Around 30,000 people in Paraguay have been affected by the harsh weather, with over 600 families evacuated from Ayolas, a city along the Parana River. Meteorologist Eduardo Mingo told AFP that El Niño has now reached Paraguay and is likely to last until at least the first quarter of 2024. El Niño typically brings warmer ocean temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific, resulting in severe drought in some regions, such as southern Asia, and heavier rainfall in others, including parts of southern South America, the southern United States, the Horn of Africa, and central Asia. This El Niño event follows a recent, intense La Niña period that caused historic droughts and water shortages in southern South America earlier this year, leading to failed crops and a lack of drinking water. Evacuations by boat were carried out in Ayolas, and northern Uruguay has also seen flood-related displacement. Tourist access to the Iguazu Falls between Brazil and Argentina has been closed due to the danger posed by high water levels. In Brazil, heavy rainfall led to flooding and landslides in the southern states of Parana and Santa Catarina, but as of this week, no fatalities have been reported there. The national meteorological agency Inmet warned of an approaching cyclone expected to deliver more rain, hail, and strong winds to three southern states, as well as the cities of Brasilia and Rio de Janeiro, bringing risks of power outages, crop damage, uprooted trees, and further flooding. Officials in Parana state, Brazil, say that two people have died and 16,000 have been displaced because of floods in the past month. The wet conditions continue to affect the Iguazu Falls region, shared by Brazil and Argentina, with tourist access suspended due to dangerously high water. Argentina's Naval Hydrography Service has also raised warnings over high water levels in the River Plate, a river shared with Uruguay, where nearly 3,000 people have been forced from their homes due to ongoing flooding—and numbers may rise. © 2023 AFP
translated_content: Gwo lapli ak inondasyon grav, ki koze pa fenomèn El Niño a, fin devaste Amerik disid semèn sa a, lakòz omwen twa moun mouri ak anpil evakyasyon. Dapre otorite yo, de granmoun aje (70 ak 84 lane) epi yon ti fi 11 lane, mouri nan Paragwe apre kay yo te kraze anba move tan an nan de vil ki frape pa tanpèt yo. Arsenio Zarate, chèf Biwo Ijans Nasyonal Paragwe a, di vandredi plis pase 40 kote sibi gwo domaj. Apeprè 30,000 moun nan Paragwe afekte pa move tan an, epi plis pase 600 fanmi evakye soti Ayolas, yon vil bò Larivyè Parana. Meteyorolojis Eduardo Mingo te di AFP ke El Niño deja rive Paragwe e li ka kontinye omwen jiska premye trimès 2024. El Niño souvan pote chofaj tanperati lanmè nan pati santral ak lès Oseyan Pasifik la, ki lakoz sechrès grav an kèk zòn (tankou Azi disid) epi plis lapli an lòt, tankou Amerik disid, sid Etazini, Kòn Lafrik ak Azi santral. Fenomen El Niño sa a vini apre yon peryòd La Niña ki te grav, kote te gen sechrès istorik ak mank dlo potab nan Amerik disid kòmansman ane a, sa ki lakoz rekolt pèdi ak mank dlo bwè. Evakyasyon ak kannòt fèt nan Ayolas, epi nò Ikrèn te wè deplasman moun akoz inondasyon. Aksè touris nan kaskad Iguazu, ant Brezil ak Ajantin, fèmen paske nivo dlo twò wo. O Brezil, gwo lapli lakoz inondasyon ak glisman tè nan eta sid Parana ak Santa Catarina, men pa gen lanmò rapòte semèn sa a. Ajans meteyorolojik nasyonal la, Inmet, avèti sou yon siklòn k ap vini ki ka pote plis lapli, grèl ak gwo van sou twa eta sid yo ansanm ak vil Brasilia ak Rio de Janeiro, ak risk pou elektrisite koupe, domaj sou plantasyon, pyebwa tonbe, epi plis inondasyon. Otorite Parana, Brezil, di de moun mouri epi 16,000 oblije kite lakay yo paske inondasyon nan dènye mwa a. Sitiyasyon mouye a ap kontinye afekte zòn Iguazu Falls, kote Brezil ak Ajantin pataje, kote aksè touris la sispann akoz nivo dlo danjere. Sèvis Idrografi Naval Ajantin lan bay avètisman sou nivo dlo ki wo nan Rivyè Plate la, ki Ajantin pataje ak Ikrèn, kote prèske 3,000 moun te fòse kite kay yo ak plis ka vini. © 2023 AFP

article_content: Newcastle United's manager, Eddie Howe, has said he believes Saudi Arabia would be well prepared to host a FIFA World Cup, basing his assessment on the team's previous training trips to the country. Prior to Newcastle's League Cup game against Manchester United, Howe shared that the club's experiences in Riyadh and Jeddah were marked by strong organization and top-notch hospitality. With Australia out of the running for the 2034 World Cup, FIFA is expected to announce Saudi Arabia—the only nation to submit a bid— as the host. Newcastle United is mainly owned by the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF). Additionally, the club hosted Saudi Arabia's national team for international fixtures at St. James' Park against Costa Rica and South Korea earlier this year. Howe indicated that such experiences suggest the World Cup would be efficiently managed if held in Saudi Arabia.
translated_content: Manadjè Newcastle United la, Eddie Howe, fè konnen li kwè Arabie Saoudite ta byen pare pou òganize yon FIFA World Cup, baze sou eksperyans ekip li te genyen pandan kèk vwayaj antrènman nan peyi a. Anvan match League Cup kont Manchester United la, Howe te di eksperyans klub la nan Riyadh ak Jeddah te byen òganize epi yo te resevwa yo avèk anpil respè. Depi Ostrali retire kandidati li pou òganize Coupe du Monde 2034 la, FIFA gen plan pou anonse Arabie Saoudite—ki se sèl peyi ki te mete kandida—kòm peyi òganizatè a. Majorite aksyon Newcastle United se menm PIF (Public Investment Fund) Saoudien an ki posede yo. Klub la te tou òganize de match entènasyonal kote ekip nasyonal Arabie Saoudite te jwe kont Costa Rica ak South Korea nan St. James' Park pi bonè ane sa a. Howe fè konprann ke sou baz eksperyans sa yo, Coupe du Monde lan t ap byen òganize si li fèt nan Arabie Saoudite.

article_content: Three years ago, the world watched as images of the Arab Spring showed women actively participating in revolutions across Tunisia, Egypt, Libya, and Yemen. While these scenes surprised many globally, Arabs were less surprised, recognizing a long-standing tradition of women's involvement in significant social and political changes, stretching back to anti-colonial movements when women played major organizational roles. As ongoing challenges grip the region, it's crucial to center the voices and experiences of Arab women. Rather than viewing their story purely through a lens of religion or culture, we should regard the treatment of women as a key indicator of a society's direction. Often, how a country respects women's rights reflects its broader political future. Unfortunately, recent developments following the Arab Spring have been disappointing in some areas. Measures such as proposed reductions in legal marriage age, renewed calls for polygamy, limitations on women's mobility and participation, rising incidents of harassment, and troubling practices like virginity tests on arrested protestors in Egypt have emerged. Authorities have frequently failed to intervene in cases of public harassment and abuse. Yet, many young women continue to push for their rights, undeterred by these setbacks. Despite facing violence, imprisonment, and intimidation for speaking out, they have overcome the so-called 'line of fear.' Their persistent activism underscores the necessity of including women's rights in the broader struggle for civil rights in the region. There remains hope that women's voices will have a greater influence on policy, potentially helping to guide the region toward stability and opportunity. Today, many young women are forging identities that embrace both religious tradition and the desire for greater personal freedoms. With this perspective, my colleagues Abby Disney, Gini Reticker, and I announced at the Clinton Global Initiative 2014 our commitment to 'The Trials of Spring'—a multimedia project amplifying the stories, challenges, and aspirations of Arab women. It's clear that women's rights and issues should not be treated as peripheral—they are central to any society's progress. Where women thrive, opportunity expands for all; where women are suppressed, wider repression often follows. The essential first step is to actively listen to Arab women's perspectives and prioritize them in shaping the future.
translated_content: Twa ane pase, mond lan te gade imaj Prentan Arab kote fanm te patisipe aktivman nan revolisyon an Tinizi, Lejip, Libi ak Yemèn. Pandan sèn sa yo te etone anpil moun international, Arab yo yo te plis abitye ak tradisyon lontan kote fanm te jwe gwo wòl nan chanjman sosyal ak politik, depi jou mouvman anti-kolonyal yo. Pandan defi kontinye nan rejyon an, li enpòtan pou mete vwa ak eksperyans fanm Arab yo anvan plan. Olye nou limite istwa yo sou relijyon oswa kilti, jan fanm trete ka montre kiyès sosyete a ap vin ye demen. Pi souvan, kijan peyi a respekte dwa fanm, li detèmine direksyon li. Malerezman, gen kèk retrè apre Prentan Arab la. Gen pawòl pou bese laj maryaj legal, rekòmanse pale sou poligami, mete baryè sou mouvman ak patisipasyon fanm, plis ka asèlman, epi pratik chòk tankou tès vèjinite sou fanm arete pandan manifestasyon ann Ejip. Souvan, otorite pa fè anyen kont abi ak asèlman piblik. Men, anpil jèn fanm pa dekouraje, yo kontinye mande dwa yo. Malgre vyolans, prizon ak entimidasyon, yo depase sa yo rele ‘liy krent la.’ Aktisism yo montre kout zegwi dwa fanm dwe ladan batay pou dwa sivil la. Gen espwa vwa fanm yo ap gen plis enfliyans sou politik e sa ka ede regyon an avanse. Jodi a, anpil jèn fanm ap chèche melanje tradisyon relijye ak dezi pou plis dwa ak libète. Avèk vizyon sa, mwen menm ak kolaboratè mwen Abby Disney ak Gini Reticker te lanse nan Clinton Global Initiative 2014 angajman nou pou 'The Trials of Spring'—yon pwojè miltimedya ki mete limyè sou vwa, defi ak rèv fanm Arab yo. Li klè dwa fanm pa dwe neglije—yo nan kè devlopman nenpòt sosyete. Kote fanm avanse, opòtinite ogmante pou tout moun; kote yo oprese, repwesyon vin gaye. Premye pa a se koute vwa fanm Arab yo epi mete yo priyoritè pou lavni.
post_content: Women were at the frontlines of the Arab Spring—but their fight isn’t over. From Tunisia to Egypt, they're still pushing boundaries for rights & representation. Listening to their voices is key to real change! #ArabWomen #SpringForward #Equality
translated_post: Fanm yo te devan pandan Prentan Arab la—men batay yo poko fini! Soti Tinizi pou rive Lejip, yo kontinye leve vwa yo pou dwa ak reprezantasyon. Koute sa yo di, se premye pa pou chanjman vre! #FanmArab #DwaFanm #Chanjman

article_content: Cindy Bennett and Mike Mello, a blind couple in Seattle, report that a bus driver denied them access after claiming unavailable space in the designated section for disabled passengers. The couple expressed feeling embarrassed and targeted, stating that while they qualify for ADA seating, they can legally sit anywhere on the bus. According to their account to KIRO 7, the driver loudly told them to leave, which they found demeaning. Mike Mello shared that the experience left him in disbelief, questioning if such exclusion still happens in modern times. In response, the couple is urging that all bus drivers receive better education on disability rights to avoid similar situations in the future. Seattle Metro Transit has acknowledged that passengers who are blind do not have to sit only in designated areas and extended an apology for the driver's conduct. The driver involved has been identified, with his supervisor now determining possible disciplinary steps. Marci Carpenter, president of the National Federation of the Blind of Washington, strongly condemned the incident when speaking to Fox 13. She stated such conduct is unacceptable and that drivers need clearer understanding on how to treat all passengers respectfully.
translated_content: Cindy Bennett ak Mike Mello, yon koup ki pa wè nan Seattle, di yo pa t ka monte nan bis la paske chofè a di pa t gen plas ki rezève pou andikape yo. Koup la di yo te santi yo imilye e yo te santi yo te vize, paske, menm si yo gen dwa chita kote ADA a, lalwa ba yo dwa chita nenpòt kote sou bis la. Yo eksplike sou KIRO 7 ke chofè a te mande yo desann byen fò, e yo te bezwen sa te fè yo santi yo mal. Mike Mello di eksperyans lan te sezi l; li mande tèt li si zak de eksklizyon konsa toujou ap fèt jodi a. Koup la mande pou tout chofè bis yo resevwa plis fòmasyon sou dwa moun ki gen andikap pou evite lòt ka konsa. Metro Transit Seattle konfime ke pasaje ki pa wè pa oblije chita sèlman kote ki rezève epi li prezante eskiz pou jan chofè a te aji. Yo idantifye chofè a epi supèvizè li ap deside si ap gen sanksyon. article_content: Ashley Cole, 23, underwent DermaEraze to remove stretch marks caused by significant weight loss. DermaEraze is a treatment using a device similar to a tattoo gun but without ink, combined with pulses of intense bright light, to address stretch marks and sagging skin. The regime, introduced in the UK by cosmetic practitioner Lorena Oberg, can leave the skin red and sensitive, but Oberg states that the discomfort is less than it appears. Stretch marks form when collagen and elastin fibers in the skin are stretched rapidly, leading to tears and scarring. Rapid weight gain during pregnancy, hormonal changes during puberty, muscle-building, and general weight gain can all be factors. Actress and mother-of-three Kate Winslet, 38, has mentioned that pregnancy left her with stretch marks. Many treatments for stretch marks, including lasers, gels, and lotions, have limited effectiveness. In contrast, DermaEraze has shown consistent results, reportedly reducing their appearance by up to 90% in some cases and reducing scar width in just one 60-minute session. First, an anesthetic cream is applied to numb the skin, and IPL may be used to prepare the area by targeting uneven pigmentation. The needling part of DermaEraze uses a special device with up to eight fine needles oscillating rapidly to target stretch marks precisely. This process stimulates fibroblast cells, promoting collagen production and resulting in skin repair, rejuvenation, and tightening. A typical session can last up to two hours, including about 30 minutes of needling. Discomfort is usually limited to the duration of the procedure. Oberg notes that treated areas appear red and sore for about 48 hours post-treatment, but the side effects are less severe than they look. Ashley Cole, who developed stretch marks after losing five stone, tried other treatments before undergoing DermaEraze and a follow-up IPL session. He reported significant improvement, with some marks disappearing and others fading. Dr. Bryan Mayou of the Cadogan Clinic in London suggests the treatment may be effective for those concerned about stretch marks. Sessions start at £500, available through harleystreetskinclinic.com.
translated_content: Ashley Cole, 23 an, te itilize DermaEraze pou retire mak detire li yo apre li pèdi anpil pwa. DermaEraze, se yon tretman kote yo sèvi ak yon aparèy ki sanble ak machin tatou (san lank), ansanm ak limyè entans pou atake mak detire ak po ki flachi. Metòd sa, prezante pa pratikan kosmetik Lorena Oberg nan Wayòm Ini, ka kite po a wouj ak sansib, men Oberg eksplike doulè a pa osi grav jan li sanble. Mak detire yo pwodui lè fib kolagen ak elastin po a detire twò vit, sa lakoz chire ak mak. Grosès ak chanjman pwa, chanjman òmòn adolesans, ak misk yo ka lakoz menm bagay. Aktris ak manman twa pitit Kate Winslet, 38 an, admèt gwosès fè li gen mak detire. Anpil lòt tretman tankou lazè, jèl oswa losyon pa bay gwo rezilta. Okontrè, DermaEraze bay bon rezilta epi ka retire jiska 90% mak yo nan kèk ka, epi redwi lajè mak yo menm apre yon sèl sesyon 60 minit. Abitidman yo aplike krèm anestezi pou minimize doulè, epi IPL itilize pou prepare zòn yo lè yo vize pigmantasyon ki pa menm. Pati zegwi DermaEraze a sèvi ak yon aparèy espesyal ki ka mete jiska uit zegwi trè fen, ki mache rapid pou vize chak mak detire. Sa fè selil fibroblast yo pwodwi plis kolagen, repare po a, epi redone li vitalite ak sere. Yon sesyon konplè ka dire jiska 2 zè, ki enkli apeprè 30 minit zegwi. Doulè a, anjeneral, fini ak tretman an. Oberg di zòn trete yo ka parèt wouj epi fè mal pandan anviwon 48 èdtan, men sa pa osi grav jan li parèt. Ashley Cole, ki te gen mak detire apre li pèdi senk stòn, itilize lòt metòd avan, men DermaEraze ak IPL ede li anpil. Kèk mak disparèt nèt, lòt yo fèb. Dr. Bryan Mayou nan Cadogan Clinic London di moun ki enkyè pou mak detire ka eseye metòd sa a. Pri chak sesyon kòmanse a £500, plis enfòmasyon sou harleystreetskinclinic.com.

article_content: Bear Grylls, a well-known adventurer, is under scrutiny from local authorities after installing a large slide into the sea on St Tudwal’s West, his remote North Wales island, without council permission. Gwynedd Council officials are requesting a meeting with Grylls due to health and safety concerns. The former SAS soldier, now 39, purchased the 20-acre island—a designated area of outstanding natural beauty—off the Llyn peninsula with his wife, Shara, for £95,000 in 2000. Earlier this week, Grylls shared a photo of the slide on Twitter, captioned: 'New slide attached at home on our island! You hit the water very fast!!!!' This drew the council’s attention, launching an investigation. Grylls and his wife, who have three sons aged between four and nine, split their time between the island—where they've renovated a 100-year-old former lighthouse keeper’s cottage—and their Dutch barge in London. Gwynedd Council, which is responsible for the protected area, confirmed the investigation. Councillor Wyn Williams expressed worries, pointing out the slide should only be used for a couple of hours daily due to tidal patterns, and that it should not have been erected without consulting planning or health and safety officials. Additionally, Grylls has submitted a planning application for a £580,000 harbour on the island to improve access, noting the current jetty is exposed and sometimes dangerous. Despite Grylls' reputation as a survival expert—he climbed Everest at age 23—local officials assert that planning permission is probably needed for the slide. The council’s vice-chairman, Michael Sol Owen, reiterated that permission would likely be required. The investigation remains ongoing as officials consider safety and environmental impacts.

Responsab Gwynedd Council yo mande yon rankont ak Grylls poutèt enkyetid sou sante ak sekirite. Ansyen sòlda SAS la, kounye a gen 39 an, te achte zile a ki gen 20 ekta—a, kòm zòn bote natirèl ekstraòdinè—toupre penensil Llyn ak madanm li, Shara, pou £95,000 an 2000. Nan kòmansman semèn nan, Grylls te pataje yon foto glisad la sou Twitter, kote li te ekri: 'Nouvo glisad lakay sou zile nou! Ou frape dlo a byen vit!!!!' Sa atire atansyon konsèy la epi lanse ankèt la. Grylls ak madanm li, ki gen twa pitit gason ant kat ak nèf an, divize tan yo ant zile a—kote yo te renove ansyen kay gadyen phar ki gen plis pase 100 ane—ak bato peyi Olandè yo nan Lond. Gwynedd Council, ki jere zòn pwoteje sa a, konfime ankèt la. Konsèyè Wyn Williams eksprime enkyetid li, li di glisad la ta dwe sèlman itilize kèk èdtan pa jou akoz mare, epi li pa t dwe monte san diskite ak depatman planifikasyon oswa sekirite konsèy la. Anplis, Grylls soumèt demach pou bati yon abri £580,000 sou zile a pou amelyore aksè a, paske pon active la ekspoze epi pafwa danjere. Malgre repitasyon Grylls kòm ekspè siviv—li te monte Everest a 23 an—ofisyèl lokal yo mete aksan sou bezwen pèmisyon planifikasyon pou glisad la. Vis-prezidan konsèy Michael Sol Owen konfime ke pèmisyon pral nesesè. Ankèt la kontinye pandan otorite yo ap konsidere risk sekirite ak enpak sou anviwònman an.

Cambodia’s newest and largest airport began commercial operations on Monday, serving as an upgraded gateway to the famed Angkor Wat temple complex in Siem Reap province. The inaugural flight—a Bangkok Airways arrival from Thailand—was among 17 scheduled flights on the first day at Siem Reap-Angkor International Airport.

Constructed at a cost of approximately $1.1 billion, the airport spans 700 hectares (1,730 acres) about 40 kilometers (25 miles) east of Angkor Wat and features a 3,600-meter (11,810-foot) runway. Building began in 2020 to replace the existing airport, which sits just 5 kilometers (3.1 miles) from the UNESCO World Heritage Site. Concerns that vibrations from frequent flights were damaging the temple’s foundations contributed to the decision to retire the old facility.

The new airport has an initial capacity of 7 million passengers a year, with plans to expand to 12 million by 2040. It was developed through a 55-year build-operate-transfer partnership between Cambodia and China.

According to the Ministry of Tourism, Cambodia welcomed about 3.5 million international tourists in the first eight months of 2023. In 2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic, the country received around 6.6 million foreign visitors. Tourism remains a crucial pillar of Cambodia’s economy.

Deputy Prime Minister Vongsey Vissoth, who led the opening ceremony, stated that the airport will be officially inaugurated on November 16 by Prime Minister Hun Manet and top Chinese officials. A separate $1.5 billion airport project, also backed by Chinese investment, is underway in Phnom Penh. The future Techo International Airport, covering 2,600 hectares (6,425 acres), is set for completion in 2024.
translated_content:
Ayewopò ki pi gwo ak pi modèn Kambodj la kòmanse fonksyone lendi kòm yon nouvo pòtay pou Angkor Wat, atraksyon touristik pi popilè a nan pwovens Siem Reap. Premye vòl la, soti Bangkok Airways ann Ayiti, te pami 17 vòl ki te pwograme premye jou a nan Ayewopò Entènasyonal Siem Reap-Angkor.

Ayewopò sa a te bati ak yon envestisman apeprè 1,1 milya dola, kouvri 700 ekta (1,730 kawo tè) apati 40 kilomèt (25 mil) sou bò lès Angkor Wat. Li gen yon pis avyon ki mezire 3,600 mèt (11,810 pye). Travay la te kòmanse depi 2020 pou ranplase ansyen ayewopò a ki te sèlman 5 kilomèt (3,1 mil) akote Angkor Wat, yon sit UNESCO. Enkyetid sou vibrasyon avyon yo ki te ka domaje fondasyon tanp lan fè gouvènman an chwazi retire ansyen ayewopò a.

Nouvo ayewopò sa a kapab resevwa 7 milyon pasaje chak ane, ak plan pou ogmante kapasite a pou rive 12 milyon an 2040. Li te devlope atravè yon akò "build-operate-transfer" pou 55 ane ant Kambodj ak Lachin.

Ministè Touris la rapòte peyi a te resevwa anviwon 3,5 milyon touris entènasyonal pandan 8 premye mwa 2023. An 2019, avan pandemi COVID-19, te gen 6,6 milyon vizitè etranje. Touris se youn nan poto mitan ekonomi Kambodj.

Vis-Premye Minis Vongsey Vissoth, ki te dirije seremoni ouvèti a, deklare ayewopò a pral gen enogirasyon ofisyèl 16 novanm avèk Premye Minis Hun Manet ak gwo otorite Chinwa yo. Y ap bati yon lòt gwo ayewopò, Techo International Airport, nan Pòtoprens avèk finansman Chinwa, k ap koute 1,5 milya dola e k ap kouvri 2,600 ekta (6,425 kawo tè), epi l ap pare an 2024.

On Thursday, a federal judge in Anchorage ruled that the massive Willow oil project on Alaska's North Slope can move forward, despite opposition from environmental groups. U.S. District Court Judge Sharon Gleason rejected claims that the government had not adequately considered the project's climate impact or its potential harm to threatened polar bears. This decision removes one of the last major barriers for Willow, which would be the largest oil development on U.S. federal land in decades and has become a focal point for climate activists. Environmental groups plan to appeal the ruling.

Erik Grafe, an attorney from the environmental organization Earthjustice, criticized the federal approval, arguing it contradicts national climate goals. The project drew national attention earlier in the year, with viral social media campaigns—especially among young people—arguing that such a large fossil fuel project would increase greenhouse gas emissions and undermine President Biden's climate commitments.

ConocoPhillips has pursued development of the Willow project for years, receiving initial approval in 2020 during the Trump administration. Judge Gleason revoked those permits the following year due to inadequate environmental assessments. After further review, the Biden administration approved a slightly reduced plan in March 2023, allowing three drilling sites. ConocoPhillips cites benefits such as an estimated $7.6 billion for the U.S. Treasury and 2,500 construction jobs, emphasizing efforts to minimize environmental impact.

Some Alaska Native groups and conservationists have opposed the project, citing concerns over wildlife and subsistence activities. However, many of Alaska's largest Native associations, corporate entities, and most North Slope local and regional governments support the project for its economic benefits, which they say are needed to sustain infrastructure and services.

Nagruk Harcharek of Voice of the Arctic Iñupiat expressed confidence that subsistence hunting would not suffer significantly, emphasizing that local input was part of the decision-making process. Alaska’s political leadership, including Governor Mike Dunleavy and the state’s bipartisan congressional delegation, also support Willow.

Environmental groups warn that the project may pave the way for further oil development in the Arctic, particularly in the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska, a vast but largely undeveloped region crucial for caribou, polar bears, and migratory birds. The government estimates Willow could produce 260 million metric tons of greenhouse gases over its lifespan—the equivalent of adding two million cars to the road for 30 years, according to Grafe.

Judge Gleason found that the government’s analysis met legal requirements and Congressional goals for the area. ConocoPhillips plans to resume construction in December. Meanwhile, the Biden administration has tried to balance approval of Willow by proposing new restrictions on oil and gas development elsewhere in the Arctic and reconsidering drilling leases granted in past years.
translated_content:
Jedi, yon jij federal nan Anchorage deside pwojè lwil Willow la sou North Slope Alaska ka avanse, malgre opozisyon gwoup anviwònman yo. Jij Distri Ameriken Sharon Gleason rejte agiman ke gouvènman an pa t pran ase an kont enpak pwojè a sou klima ak sou lours polè ki menase. Desizyon sa a retire youn nan dènye obstak yo pou Willow, ki ka vin pi gwo pwojè lwil sou tè federal Ozetazini depi plizyè dizèn lane e ki tounen yon gwo sijè pou aktivis klima yo. Gwoup anviwònman yo anonse y ap fè apèl.

Erik Grafe, avoka òganizasyon Earthjustice, kritike apwobasyon federal la, li di sa kont objektif nasyonal sou klima. Pwojè a te atire anpil atansyon ane sa a, espesyalman ak kanpay viral sou rezo sosyal – sitou pou jèn yo – ki di pwojè sa a ap ogmante emisyon gaz e l ap mete an danje angajman Prezidan Biden pou klima a.

ConocoPhillips ap pouswiv pwojè Willow la depi kèk ane, yo te resevwa premye apwobasyon an an 2020 pandan administrasyon Trump. Ane apre, Jij Gleason retire pèmi yo poutèt evaluasyon anviwonman yo pa t ase. Apre lòt analiz, administrasyon Biden an apwouve yon vèsyon pi limite an mas 2023, ak sèlman twa sit pou fouye. ConocoPhillips mete aksan sou avantaj tankou $7.6 milya pou Trezò ameriken ak 2,500 djòb konstriksyon, epi efò pou limite enpak sou anviwònman an.

Gen kèk gwoup endijèn Alaska ak defansè anviwònman opoze pwojè a, ak sousi sou bèt ak abitid tradisyonèl yo. Men, gwo asosyasyon ak konpayi endijèn Alaska yo ansanm ak pifò otorite lokal ak rejyonal North Slope yo k'ap sipòte pwojè a pou avantaj ekonomik li yo, epi di lajan sa yo enpòtan pou enfrastrikti ak sèvis.

Nagruk Harcharek, dirijan nan Voice of the Arctic Iñupiat, di li gen konfyans ke chasse tradisyonèl pa pral afekte anpil paske kominote yo te gen chans fè tande vwa yo nan pwosesis la. Lidè politik Alaska – tankou Gouvènè Mike Dunleavy ak delegasyon kongrè bipatizan an – yo tout apiye Willow.

Gwoup anviwònman yo avèti pwojè a ka kreye plis devlopman lwil nan Arctic la, sitou nan National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska, yon gwo zòn ki toujou enpòtan pou karibou, lours polè ak zwazo migratè yo. Leta estime Willow ka pwodui 260 milyon tòn gaz lakòz efè tèmik pandan tout dire pwojè a – menm jan ak mete de milyon machin sou wout la pandan 30 ane, dapre Grafe.

Jij Gleason jije analiz gouvènman an ann akò ak lwa ak objektif Kongrè a pou zòn nan. ConocoPhillips prevwa rekòmanse travay la nan mwa Desanm. Pandan ke Willow ap kontinye, administrasyon Biden an ap pwopoze nouvo restriksyon sou devlopman lwil ak gaz nan lòt kote nan Arctic la epi ap revize pèmi ki te bay avan.

article_content:
The Echo Pop and HomePod mini are two distinct smart speakers, each catering to different needs and budgets. Both enable music playback and voice assistant interaction, but their similarities largely end there.

The Echo Pop is an affordable, entry-level option, typically priced at $40 and available in four colors: lavender bloom, charcoal, glacier white, and midnight teal. Its circular design features a flat front speaker, LED indicator light, and control buttons. The compact size fits easily on nightstands or desks. Discounts from Amazon are frequent, increasing its appeal.

Apple's HomePod mini retails for $100 and comes in five colors: space gray, blue, yellow, white, and orange. Its robust, spherical build features a flat top with touch controls and indicator lights, emphasizing higher quality construction. Price reductions are uncommon for the HomePod mini.

The Echo Pop is best suited for smaller spaces like bedrooms or home offices. Its 1.95-inch front-firing speaker offers adequate sound for background use, though clarity may decline at higher volumes. Meanwhile, the HomePod mini delivers clearer audio using its S5 chip and computational audio system. A full-range driver and dual passive radiators provide strong bass and balanced sound, filling larger spaces more effectively with 360-degree audio.

Both products provide smart assistant support. The Echo Pop integrates with Amazon Alexa and a broad set of Alexa-enabled smart devices. The HomePod mini uses Siri and connects to Apple HomeKit products; HomeKit’s range is smaller than Alexa’s, but it fits well into the Apple ecosystem.

In summary, the HomePod mini excels with better sound and Apple integration—ideal for users invested in Apple devices. The Echo Pop is a budget-friendly option for small spaces and casual listening.
translated_content:
Echo Pop ak HomePod mini se de oratè entèlijan ki vrèman diferan, chak fèt pou bezwen ak bidjè diferan. Toude pèmèt itilizatè yo jwe mizik ak pale ak asistan vwa, men sa se tout resanblans yo.

Echo Pop se yon oratè entèlijan ki bon mache pou moun ki jis kòmanse, li vann anviwon $40 epi li vini ak kat koulè: lavender bloom, charbon, blan glas, ak ble fènwa. Li gen yon fòm wonn ak oratè plat devan, limyè endikatè anlè, ak bouton kontwòl. Ti gwosè li fè li fasil pou mete sou ti tab oswa biwo. Amazon souvan mete li an rabè, sa ki rann li plis aksesib.

HomePod mini Apple lan koute $100 epi li disponib nan senk koulè: gri espas, ble, jòn, blan, ak zoranj. Li gen yon estrikti boul ki solid ak tèt plat pou kontwòl tactile ak limyè endikatè. Konstriksyon li bay bon kalite, jan pri li montre. Rabè ra anpil pou HomePod mini.

Echo Pop pi adapte pou ti espas tankou chanm oswa biwo lakay. Li gen yon oratè 1.95 pous ki bay son sufizan pou mizik fons, men si ou ogmante volim, bon kalite a ka bese. Okontrè, HomePod mini bay son pwòp ak chip S5 li a ak odyo òdinatè. Avèk yon oratè prensipal ak de radiatè pasif, li bay bon bas ak bon ekilib nan tout frekans epi li ka plen gwo espas ak son 360-degre.

Tou de pwodwi bay aksè ak asistan voye. Echo Pop mache ak Amazon Alexa epi li fasil pou konekte ak lòt aparèy Alexa. HomePod mini mache ak Siri epi li konekte ak Apple HomeKit—HomeKit pa gen menm anpil chwa ak Alexa, men li travay byen ak aparèy Apple yo.

Pou fini, HomePod mini se yon bon chwa pou moun ki vle pi bon son ak entegrasyon ak sistèm Apple la. Echo Pop se yon solisyon abòdab pou ti espas ak pou moun ki bezwen yon oratè entèlijan, senp.

Each year in Tamil Nadu, southern India, thousands gather for a distinct ritual in which coconuts are cracked on the heads of devotees, believed to bring health and prosperity. Participants of all ages wait in lines while godmen perform the act by striking coconuts on their heads. This tradition, which dates back to the 19th century, continues to draw crowds.

Though intended as a sacred offering, the ritual sometimes results in serious head injuries, prompting concern from medical professionals. Neurosurgery professor Dr. Anil Kumar Peethambaran has cautioned that the skull can only withstand a limited amount of impact and that coconuts that fail to break can cause significant harm. Despite repeated warnings, many devotees remain dedicated, certain of the ritual’s spiritual value. Afterwards, the broken coconut pieces are often collected as offerings to the gods—symbols of sacrifice and hope for good fortune.
translated_content:

Tout laj vini, chita an liy, epi "godmen" frape kokoye sou tèt yo. Tradisyon sa a, ki te kòmanse depi 19yèm syèk la, toujou rasanble gwo foul.

article_content: Burkina Faso's military government has signed an agreement with Russia to construct a nuclear power plant to boost electricity supply. This step marks the latest effort by the junta to strengthen ties with Russia following strained relations with most Western partners. Since taking power last year, the military leaders have sought economic and military assistance from Russia. Currently, only about 21% of people in Burkina Faso have access to electricity, making it one of the least electrified countries in the world. The agreement with Russia comes after Burkinabe leader Capt Ibrahim Traore met Russian President Vladimir Putin during the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow in July. At the summit, Capt Traore asked President Putin for help to build a nuclear power plant to meet both Burkina Faso’s and neighboring countries’ energy needs. Capt Traore emphasized the urgent need for energy, stating, 'We have a critical need for energy... if possible, to build a nuclear power station in Burkina Faso to produce electricity.' He noted that Burkina Faso’s central location in West Africa and the regional power shortage add to the project's strategic importance. The nuclear deal supports Burkina Faso’s plan to achieve 95% electricity access in urban areas and 50% in rural areas by 2030. According to the International Energy Agency, most of the nation's electricity comes from biofuels like charcoal and wood, while oil products contribute about a third of the total energy supply. USAID reports that Burkina Faso also faces some of the highest electricity costs in Africa. Currently, South Africa is the only African country producing nuclear power commercially, but more countries are pursuing similar projects. In 2017, Russia agreed to help Egypt build a $30 billion nuclear power plant, and signed a deal to build power plants in Nigeria, though work there has not yet started. Kenya aims to build its first nuclear plant by 2027 and is still selecting an international partner. In September, Rwanda announced a partnership with Canadian-German company Dual Fluid Energy to build a nuclear reactor by 2028. Rwandan officials say the project will help meet the country’s energy needs and increase resilience to climate change. While electricity access in sub-Saharan Africa has improved in recent years, more than half the population still lacks power, according to the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development.

Depi yo pran pouvwa a ane pase a, lidè militè yo ap chèche asistans ekonomik ak militè nan men Larisi. Jiskaprezan, sèlman anviwon 21% moun nan Bukina Faso gen aksè ak elektrisite, sa ki mete peyi a pami sa ki gen mwens elektrifikasyon sou latè. Akò sa a ak Larisi vini apre chèf leta Bukinabè a, Kapten Ibrahim Traore, te rankontre ak Prezidan Larisi Vladimir Putin pandan somè Lafrik-Larisi a ki te fèt Mas la an Jiyè. Li fè konnen plas estratejik Bukina Faso nan kè Afrik Lwès ak mank kouran nan rejyon an rann pwojè a enpòtan anpil. Selon Ajans Entènasyonal Enèji a, pifò elektrisite peyi a soti nan biyokarburan tankou chabon ak bwa, pandan pwodwi petwòl bay apeprè yon tyè nan total enèji peyi a. USAID rapòte tou Bukina Faso gen youn nan pi gwo pri elektrisite nan Afrik. Jiskaprezan, Afrik di Sid se sèl peyi sou kontinan an k ap pwodwi kouran nikleyè pou vann, men gen plis peyi ki lanse pwojè konsa. Google will launch Credential Manager on Android devices from November 1, providing a unified place for users to store and access their login details, including passkeys, passwords, and federated logins. The platform also offers biometric options like fingerprint or facial recognition for secure authentication.

Passkeys allow users to log in without remembering traditional passwords or using two-factor authentication; instead, a fingerprint or face scan grants access to apps and sites. Credential Manager automatically selects the most suitable login method for each app, easing the login process.

Recently, Google made passkeys the default sign-in method for personal Google accounts. Users are now prompted to enable passkeys during sign-in, encouraging more Android apps to adopt passwordless logins. Leading apps such as WhatsApp and Uber have started utilizing Credential Manager's passkey feature.

This tool is compatible with other popular password managers like 1Password and Google's own Password Manager. Passkeys are considered more secure since they're resistant to phishing, only function where they were created, and don't get shared with apps or websites. Overall, Credential Manager aims to provide a safer, smoother login experience for users, and reduce complexity for developers.

Avèk passkeys, ou pap bezwen sonje modpas oswa itilize de-faktè otantifikasyon ankò; yon anprent oswa eskan figi ap ase pou antre sou aplikasyon ak sit wèb ou yo. Credential Manager a chwazi otomatikman metòd koneksyon ki pi apwopriye pou chak app, konsa li rann tout pwosesis la vin pi senp.

Resamman, Google fè passkeys tounen premye metòd koneksyon pou kont Google pèsonèl yo. Pwochenn fwa ou konekte, sistèm lan ap mande w pou kreye epi itilize passkeys, sa ki ankouraje plis aplikasyon Android adopte login san modpas. Gwo aplikasyon tankou WhatsApp ak Uber deja itilize Credential Manager ak passkeys yo.

Zouti sa a mache byen ak manadjè modpas popilè tankou 1Password ak Password Manager Google. Passkeys yo bay plis sekirite paske yo reziste kont phishing, yo mache sèlman sou sit oswa app kote yo te kreye, epi yo pa janm pataje ak okenn sit oswa app. An final, Credential Manager ap fè koneksyon pi fasil e pi sekirize pou itilizatè ak devlopè.

article_content: Businesses are built to make money, but there's a fine line between profiting and turning away customers. If companies cross that line, they risk losing the very people they need to survive. For quite a while, airlines have added charges for checked bags-–something travelers were unhappy about at first, but eventually got used to. To keep flight prices low and attractive, airlines shifted many expenses into extra fees, since running planes is costly. In addition to checked bags, airlines have continuously introduced fees for changing tickets, meals onboard, early boarding, more legroom, and even basic comforts like pillows or blankets. Reporter Susan Carey of the Wall Street Journal notes that airlines are always on the lookout for new items to charge for. Consumer advocate George Hobica speculates that major airlines could even charge for carry-on luggage soon—a reality already here with Spirit Airlines, which asks for $25 to $50 per carry-on. Spirit claims their low base fares let customers select only the extras they want to pay for. If the trend spreads, customers may have to pay extra just to bring any belongings besides what they're wearing. For many, that would cross from sensible business to unfair treatment. This isn't just an airline problem. Years ago, First Chicago Corp., which became Bank One, began charging customers $3 to use a bank teller—even to make deposits. Many felt this was going too far. Jamie Dimon, who took over at Bank One (and now leads JPMorgan Chase), tried defending the fee, but customer backlash forced the bank to drop it. Despite this, quite a few banks still slip similar charges into monthly statements under new names. The pattern across industries seems clear: more things we once got for free now come with a price. Some airlines like Southwest let you check two bags for free, and JetBlue's policy covers at least the first bag. This has helped them keep a good reputation among travelers. If bigger airlines start charging for carry-ons, competitors might attract angry flyers by touting free baggage options. To sum up, businesses always look for ways to earn more, but if that means treating customers poorly, it can backfire badly.

Anplis frè pou valiz tcheke, avyon yo ajoute frè pou chanje tikè, manje nan avyon, monte an premye, plis espas pou pye, epi menm bagay senp tankou zòrye ak dra. Repòtè Susan Carey (Wall Street Journal) fè konnen avyon toujou ap chèche fason pou ajoute frè sou bagay ki te gratis avan. Defansè konsomatè George Hobica panse gwo konpayi avyon yo ka kòmanse fè moun peye pou valiz yo pote sou avyon—yon pratik Spirit Airlines gentan ap fè, kote ou ka peye $25 a $50 pou chak valiz depann de kijan ou achte tikè a. Moun te trouve sa pa jis. Jamie Dimon, ki te nouvo chèf Bank One (kounye a JPMorgan Chase), te eksplike frè a, men reyaksyon kliyan fè bank lan retire sa. Kèk avyon tankou Southwest pèmèt premye de valiz yo gratis, epi JetBlue pa chaje pou premye valiz la. Sa fè yo kenbe bon repitasyon ak pasaje yo. Anne Wojcicki, founder of the DNA testing company 23andMe and wife of Google co-founder Sergey Brin, arranged for their unborn daughter to undergo DNA testing to determine her risk of developing conditions such as breast cancer, Alzheimer’s, and Parkinson’s disease later in life. She also had their son’s genes tested within the first few months of his life to create a 'road map' of potential future health risks. As a result, Wojcicki discovered her son is lactose intolerant. She believes parents should be aware of their children’s genetic risks to provide better care, arguing that being forewarned is being forearmed. Wojcicki predicts that within a decade, DNA testing at birth will be common practice for newborns in the UK and US.

Despite these advancements, some experts have voiced strong concerns. Professor Dagan Wells, a genetics expert at Oxford University, cautions that conducting such DNA tests on children imposes information on them before they can give consent, and the results cannot be undone once obtained. Wojcicki shared that she sent her unborn daughter’s amniotic fluid for testing—a procedure typically offered to older mothers to assess the risk of Down’s syndrome.

For £125, 23andMe provides DNA analysis using saliva samples to identify genes linked to hereditary conditions like cystic fibrosis, sickle cell anemia, breast cancer, Alzheimer’s, and Parkinson’s. The company checks for genes such as BRCA1 and BRCA2, which significantly increase the risk of breast and ovarian cancer. Actress Angelina Jolie underwent a double mastectomy after discovering she carried the BRCA1 gene in 2013.

However, Dr. Helen Wallace from GeneWatch UK warns that the links between genes and many diseases are still poorly understood, arguing that such tests should not be offered for children. Although children’s DNA testing is legal in the UK, official guidelines recommend it only for pressing medical reasons. In 2013, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration barred 23andMe from offering health advice to American customers over concerns about the tests’ accuracy. European regulators consider the testing kits safe, but the EU has not yet legislated on these services. Dr. Wallace points out that the company continues to operate in Europe despite the ban in America, effectively exploiting a legal loophole.

23andMe also has an agreement with pharmaceutical giant Pfizer to share its genetic database for research, with customers able to consent to their children’s information being used. Dr. Wallace warns that babies cannot consent, and it is unclear how this information might affect them in the future. Wojcicki maintains that users who are dissatisfied can download their data and delete their accounts.
translated_content:
Anne Wojcicki, fondatè konpayi tès ADN 23andMe epi madanm Sergey Brin, youn nan fondatè Google, te fè tès ADN sou pitit fi yo pandan li te ansent pou konnen risk li genyen pou devlope maladi tankou kansè nan tete, Alzheimer, ak Parkinson pita nan lavi. Li te fè tès jenetik sou pitit gason yo tou pandan premye mwa yo pou jwenn yon 'kat jeyografik' sou risk sante li. Yo dekouvri pitit gason an pa tolere laktoz. Wojcicki panse paran yo ta dwe konnen risk jenetik pitit yo pou yo ka ba yo pi bon swen, li di 'konnen an avans se pare pou sa.' Li panse nan kèk ane, tout tibebe ki fèt nan UK ak Etazini ap fè tès ADN depi nesans.

Gen ekspè ki pa dakò ak sa. Pwofesè Dagan Wells, yon espesyalis jenetik nan Oxford University, di tès sa yo mete enfòmasyon sou timoun yo san yo pa ka bay konsantman epi yon fwa ou gen rezilta yo, li pa posib pou w efase sa. Wojcicki te voye likid amnyotik pitit fi li pou tès, yon analiz ki fèt sou fanm ansent ki gen plis pase 35 an pou tcheke risk pou Down Syndrome.

Pou £125, 23andMe analize ADN nan echantiyon saliv pou chèche jèn ki la pou kondisyon ereditè tankou fibwoz kystik, anemi falciform, kansè nan tete, Alzheimer, ak Parkinson. Yo verifye jèn tankou BRCA1 ak BRCA2, ki ogmante risk kansè nan tete ak ovè. Aktè Angelina Jolie te fè double mastektomi paske li te jwenn BRCA1 an 2013.

Men, Dr Helen Wallace nan GeneWatch UK avèti lyen ant jèn yo ak anpil maladi pa byen konprann toujou e li panse tès sa yo pa dwe fèt sou timoun. Malgre tès ADN sou timoun legal nan UK, gouvènman an rekòmande sèlman si gen rezon medikal serye. An 2013, FDA Etazini te entèdi 23andMe bay konsèy sou sante kliyan ameriken paske yo te gen dout sou presizyon tès la. Kit tès la jwenn validasyon Ewòp, Inyon Ewopeyen poko gen lwa sou sèvis sa yo. Doktè Wallace fè remake 23andMe ap fonksyone ann Ewòp menm si gen entèdiksyon Ozetazini, sa ki tankou yon twou nan lwa yo.

23andMe gen akò ak Pfizer pou pataje done jenetik pou rechèch, kote kliyan ka dakò voye enfòmasyon pitit yo. Dr Wallace di tibebe pa ka bay konsantman e nou pa konnen kijan enfòmasyon sa yo ap afekte yo pita. Wojcicki di itilizatè ki pa satisfè ka telechaje done yo epi efase kont yo.
