article_content: Authorities are working to determine how a small aircraft crashed and burned at Nashville International Airport but went undetected for hours. The incident occurred early Tuesday, though the exact time is still unknown. The plane, a single-engine Cessna registered to the Windsor Flying Club in Ontario, Canada, reportedly crashed sometime after 3 a.m. local time, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) stated. The wreckage was only discovered after sunrise, when a taxiing plane spotted an engine cover near runway 2C and alerted controllers. Airport staff then located the fire-damaged plane. Officials confirmed the crash killed the sole occupant. Although the control tower is staffed 24 hours a day, the number of controllers present overnight is unclear. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) cited low visibility and fog conditions. It is also unknown if the plane contacted controllers or made a distress call. Officials have declined to provide further details, noting the investigation is ongoing. The NTSB is investigating the cause, and the victim’s name has not been released.

article_content: London (CNN) — The dream remains alive for the U.S. men's basketball team, who continue their quest for Olympic gold. The American team, often referred to as the Dream Team, delivered a balanced performance on Friday night, defeating Argentina 109-83 to advance to Sunday’s final. Kevin Durant, reigning NBA scoring champion from the Oklahoma City Thunder, led all players with 19 points. Miami Heat’s LeBron James, a three-time NBA MVP, contributed 18 points, seven assists, and seven rebounds. Argentina featured prominent NBA players Manu Ginobili, Luis Scola, and Carlos Delfino, but they could not overcome the U.S., who gradually increased their lead after the first quarter. The U.S. will face Spain in the gold medal game on Sunday. Spain, with Los Angeles Lakers’ Pau Gasol, fought back from a halftime deficit to defeat Russia 67-59 in Friday’s semifinal. The American women's basketball team has also reached the gold medal game, set to play against France on Saturday. In track and field, the U.S. women's 4x100-meter relay team earned gold, setting a world record of 40.82 seconds, ahead of Jamaica (41.41) and Ukraine. Team members included Allyson Felix (gold in 200m), Carmelita Jeter (bronze in 200m), Tianna Madison, and Bianca Knight. The men's 4x400-meter relay saw the Bahamas team of Chris Brown, Demetrius Pinder, Michael Mathieu, and Ramon Miller overtake the U.S.—who had dominated this event for decades—on the final lap to win gold. Trinidad and Tobago took bronze. Manteo Mitchell of Team USA notably finished his leg of the men's relay despite suffering a fractured fibula. South Africa's Oscar Pistorius made history by running the final leg of his nation's relay; he is the first double amputee athlete to compete in the Olympics. In other track events, Meseret Defar of Ethiopia narrowly beat Kenya’s Vivian Jepkemoi Cheruiyot for gold in the women's 5,000-meter race. Turkey’s Asli Cakir Alptekin took gold in the 1,500-meter final, ahead of her compatriot Gamze Bulut and Bahrain’s Maryam Yusuf Jamal. Russia’s Tatyana Lysenko claimed gold in the women's hammer throw, while France’s Renaud Lavillenie won the men's pole vault, edging out two German athletes. In synchronized swimming, Russia took gold, followed by China (silver) and Spain (bronze). Oussama Mellouli of Tunisia won the men's 10-kilometer open water swim in Hyde Park’s Serpentine, securing Tunisia’s first gold of the 2012 Games; Germany’s Thomas Lurz and Canada’s Richard Weinberger completed the podium. Mellouli also earned bronze earlier in the men's 1,500-meter freestyle. In men's BMX cycling, Latvia’s Maris Strombergs defended his Beijing title to win gold, with Australia's Sam Willoughby taking silver and Colombia's Carlos Oquendo Zabala the bronze. Colombia’s Mariana Pajon won gold in women’s BMX, while New Zealand’s Sarah Walker took silver and the Netherlands’ Laura Smulders bronze. Sailing saw Australia’s Mathew Belcher and Malcolm Page win gold in the men’s 470; Great Britain earned silver and Argentina bronze. New Zealand won the women’s 470, with Great Britain second and the Netherlands third. America's Jordan Burroughs won gold in the men's 74kg freestyle wrestling, defeating Iran’s Sadegh Saeed Goudarzi. Russia’s Dzhamal Otarsultanov won gold in the 55kg category, beating Georgia’s Vladimer Khinchegashvili. In boxing, Italy’s Roberto Cammarelle narrowly defeated Azerbaijan’s Magomedrasul Medzhidov (13-12) to reach the superheavyweight final against Great Britain’s Anthony Joshua. Ireland’s John Joe Nevin and Great Britain’s Luke Campbell will contest the 56kg bantamweight gold. The Netherlands won gold in women's field hockey, defeating Argentina 2-0, while Great Britain beat New Zealand 3-1 to claim bronze. Italian race walker Alex Schwazer was excluded from the Games after testing positive for a banned substance (recombinant erythropoietin or rhEPO) that enhances red blood cell production. Schwazer had been scheduled to compete in Saturday’s 50km race walk. CNN's Steve Almasy, Joe Sterling, and Chris Eldergill contributed to this report.

article_content: Yoko Ono has shared that being blamed for The Beatles’ breakup felt like she was on trial for a crime she did not commit. She stated: "It feels like I was accused of something I didn’t do, which was breaking up The Beatles. It’s like being accused of murder and put in prison without a chance to get out." Since the band's split in 1970, many fans have blamed Ono due to her relationship with John Lennon. A year after the breakup, Ono and Lennon moved to New York to focus on their involvement in the growing peace movement. Lennon was tragically killed in 1980. In an interview with a US magazine, Ono reflected on the decades since and said the allegations made her feel unappreciated by others. She explained that the only way to cope was to transform the hatred towards her into love. Ono said: "Not being appreciated for 40 years or so... It feels like I was accused of something I didn't do, which was breaking up The Beatles. That was like being in prison for a crime you didn’t commit. It's like being accused of murder, imprisoned, and having no way out." Recently, Paul McCartney ended his long-standing feud with Ono, clarifying that she was not to blame for the band’s breakup. In a Rolling Stone interview, McCartney said: "If John loved her, there’s got to be something. He’s not stupid." Ono now feels more accepted, saying that after 40 years of being unappreciated, it finally feels like doors have opened to her. She said: "It’s like you've been knocking on a door for 40 years and then someone tells you it’s already open. It’s better to be criticized than to be complimented as a person; you have to be cautious."
translated_content: Yoko Ono te di ke lè yo te blame li pou separasyon The Beatles, li te santi tankou yo mete li sou jijman pou yon krim li pa t komèt. Li deklare: “Li santi tankou mwen te akize pou yon bagay mwen pa t fè, ki se kraze The Beatles. Sa tankou yo akize w pou yon asasina epi mete w nan prizon san chimen soti.” Depi gwoup la te separe nan 1970, anpil fanatik te blame Ono paske li te nan relasyon ak John Lennon. Yon ane apre yo te kase, Yoko ak Lennon te deplase New York pou yo te konsantre sou mouvman lapè k ap grandi a. Lennon te asasinen an 1980. Nan yon entèvyou ak yon magazin ameriken, Ono te reflechi sou ane ki pase depi akizasyon yo e li di akizasyon yo te fè li santi li pa t apresye pa lòt moun. Li eksplike ke sèl fason pou l te jere sa, se te tounen rayisman moun voye sou li a an lanmou. Ono di: “Pa janm santi ou apresye pandan anviwon 40 lane... Li santi tankou yo te akize m pou yon bagay mwen pa t fè, ki se kraze The Beatles. Sa te tankou mwen te nan prizon pou yon krim mwen pa t komèt. Se tankou yo akize w pou asasina, mete w nan prizon, epi pa gen wout pou w sòti.” Resamman, Paul McCartney mete fen nan konfli ant li ak Ono, li fè tout moun konnen li pa t responsab separasyon gwoup la. Nan yon entèvyou ak Rolling Stone, McCartney di: “Si John te renmen li, fòk li gen yon bagay. Li pa sòt.” Kounye a, Ono santi li plis aksepte, li di apre 40 lane san yo pa apresye li, li finalman santi pòt yo louvri pou li. Li di: “Sa tankou ou te ap frape pòt la pandan 40 lane epi yon moun vin di w pòt la deja louvri. Li miyò pou yo kritike w pase pou yo fè w kompliman kòm yon moun; ou dwe pran prekosyon.”
post_content: Yoko Ono says being blamed for The Beatles’ breakup felt like being on trial for a crime she didn’t commit. After 40 years, Paul McCartney sets the record straight—Ono wasn’t to blame! #TheBeatles #YokoOno #Peace

article_content:
Since 2000, General Motors, Stellantis, and Ford have closed dozens of US plants, with few ever reopening. Now, the United Auto Workers (UAW) union celebrates a new success—reviving the Belvidere, Illinois assembly plant. On Thursday, US President Joe Biden and UAW President Shawn Fain attended a rally in Belvidere to mark this achievement. While Illinois isn’t a traditional political battleground like Michigan or Ohio, Belvidere has become the focal point of the union’s recent victories in its tentative labor agreements with Stellantis, GM, and Ford.

The Belvidere plant, originally closed in February, left 1,200 hourly workers unemployed or forced to transfer far from their community. The plant is scheduled to reopen in 2027, producing a new midsize pickup truck. Until then, the facility will manufacture batteries for electric vehicles and serve as a company parts depot. Displaced workers are eligible for partial pay and unemployment benefits, which together can provide over 70% of their usual income.

"It’s definitely unusual for a plant to be brought back to life," says Jeff Schuster, global head of automotive at GlobalData, an industry consultancy. Historically, the union’s attempts to reopen plants during negotiations have rarely succeeded—but this year’s coordinated strike strategy at all three automakers proved effective. The union started by striking one assembly plant per company, escalating as negotiations progressed.

Record profits for carmakers strengthened the union’s position. Schuster notes that saving jobs is much harder when companies are struggling financially. The UAW points out that the Big Three automakers have closed 65 plants and facilities since 2000, with factors like outsourcing, automation, and a decline in market share contributing to job losses. For instance, in 1999, the Big Three sold 11.5 million vehicles in the US (68% market share). By last year, that dropped to 5.7 million vehicles (41% market share).

Despite these challenges, strong car demand and high prices empowered the union, whose "Record profits, record contracts" slogan captured this moment. Belvidere is among only a handful of plants revived after closure. Historically, simply preventing future closures—like Stellantis’ Sterling Heights, Michigan plant in 2009, or GM’s Hamtramck Assembly in Detroit—was a victory. Other plants, such as those in Spring Hill, Tennessee, and Orion Township, Michigan, reopened as part of past labor deals. However, efforts to save plants in Lordstown, Ohio, Warren, Michigan, and Baltimore, Maryland were unsuccessful, and those facilities remain closed.

For workers like Dawn Sims, a 24-year veteran at the Belvidere plant and a third-generation Chrysler employee, saving the plant means avoiding unbearable choices between work and family. She describes the immense stress felt when the closure was announced, noting the impact on families and the community.

Depi lane 2000, General Motors, Stellantis, ak Ford te fèmen plizyè dizèn faktori Ozetazini, epi sèlman kèk ladan yo te reouvè. Kounye a, sendika United Auto Workers (UAW) ap selebre yon nouvo siksè—reouvèti faktori asanble Belvidere a nan Illinois. Jedi, Prezidan Ameriken Joe Biden ak Prezidan UAW Shawn Fain te vini nan yon rasanbleman ann Belvidere pou make siksè sa a. Malgre Illinois pa tèlman yon eta kote politik souvan ap fè batay tankou Michigan oswa Ohio, Belvidere vin tounen sant viktwa sendika a ak akò travay li yo avèk Stellantis, GM, ak Ford.

Faktori Belvidere a ki te fèmen depi mwa fevriye, te mete 1,200 travayè orè san travay oswa fòse yo transfere lwen kominote yo. Faktori a prevwa reouvè an 2027 pou pwodui yon nouvo kamyonèt medyòm. Jouk lè sa, etablisman an pral fabrike batri pou machin elektrik epi sèvi kòm depo pyès konpayi an. Travayè ki te pèdi plas yo ap ka benefisye yon pati nan salè yo ansanm ak benefis chomaj, pou ede yo kenbe plis pase 70% nan revni nòmal yo.

“Li ra pou yon faktori retounen ap fonksyone,” se sa Jeff Schuster, chèf mondyal otomobil pou GlobalData, di. Devan, efò sendika a pou reouvri faktori pandan negosyasyon yo preske pa janm bay anpil rezilta—men ane sa a, estrateji grèv kowòdone sou tout twa gwo konpayi yo te mache byen. Sendika a te kòmanse ak grèv sou yon faktori pa chak konpayi, epi ogmante presyon an pandan negosyasyon yo ap avanse.

Gwo pwofi konpayi machin yo te bay sendika a plis pouvwa. Schuster di li pi difisil pou sove djòb lè konpayi yo ap fè fas a difikilte ekonomik. UAW fè konnen twa gwo konpayi machin yo fèmen 65 faktori ak enstalasyon depi lane 2000, kote sous-traitans, automatisation, ak pèdi pati sou mache a te kontribye nan pèdi djòb yo. Pa egzanp, an 1999, twa gwo konpayi yo te vann 11.5 milyon machin (68% pati sou mache); ane pase, sa te bese rive 5.7 milyon machin (41% pati sou mache).

Malgre tout bagay, demann fèm pou machin ak pri ki wo te pèmèt sendika a leve vwa li ak slogan "Gran pwofi, gwo kontra" li a. Belvidere se pami kèk faktori ki reouvri apre fèmti. Nan anpil ka, sèlman anpeche fèmen lòt faktori—tankou Sterling Heights, Michigan (Stellantis, 2009) oswa Hamtramck Assembly nan Detroit (GM)—se te deja yon siksè. Lòt faktori tankou Spring Hill, Tennessee ak Orion Township, Michigan reouvri ak ansyen akò travay. Men, efò pou sove faktori Lordstown, Ohio, Warren, Michigan, ak Baltimore, Maryland pa t reyisi e yo toujou fèmen.

Pou moun tankou Dawn Sims, ki gen 24 ane eksperyans nan Belvidere e ki nan twazyèm jenerasyon fanmi li ki travay pou Chrysler, sove faktori a te vle di pa oblije chwazi ant travay ak fanmi. Li pale sou estrès li te fè fas ak li a lè fèmti a te anonse, ansanm ak enpak la sou fanmi ak kominote a.

Every year, thousands of endangered Olive Ridley sea turtles make an incredible journey to the shores of Costa Rica to participate in one of nature’s most impressive spectacles: the arribada, or mass synchronized nesting. Arriving just days before each new moon, these turtles use their powerful fins to move across the sand and prepare their nesting sites.

As they settle on the beach, the calming sounds of waves and the turtles’ gentle movements fill the night. Professional wildlife photographer Ingo Arndt, who spent 20 days documenting this event, described it as one of the world’s most breathtaking natural phenomena.

Each turtle lays between 80 and 100 soft-shelled eggs in shallow sandy nests before returning to the sea. While millions of eggs are deposited during each arribada, only a small portion survive, as many eggs and hatchlings fall prey to wild dogs, vultures, and other threats.

To protect both the turtles and their eggs, local residents carefully collect some eggs during the first two days—eggs that might otherwise be destroyed by subsequent arrivals. The community also spends countless hours cleaning the beaches and guarding the turtles’ nests, deeply valuing their role in this remarkable event.

Ingo noted that the turtles are accustomed to people on the beach and focus intently on laying their eggs. However, they are noticeably more reserved in the water and rely on their instincts for safety. Despite the challenges, the ongoing arribadas at Ostional Beach ensure the survival of the Olive Ridley turtles for generations to come. As Ingo remarked, witnessing this event left him speechless and served as a powerful reminder of nature’s resilience.
translated_content:
Chak ane, dè milye tòti lanmè Olive Ridley ki an danje vwayaje sou kot Costa Rica pou patisipe nan youn nan pi gwo espèktak natirèl: arribada, oswa nich ann gwoup. Yo rive kèk jou anvan chak lalin nouvo, e yo sèvi ak bwaso yo pou avanse sou sab la epi prepare nich yo.

Lè yo pran plas sou plaj la, ou tande son vag yo ansanm ak mouvman dous tòti yo pandan lannuit. Fotogwaf sovaj pwofesyonèl Ingo Arndt, ki te pase 20 jou ap dokimante evènman sa a, dekri li kòm youn nan pi bèl fenomèn natirèl mond lan.

Chak tòti depose ant 80 ak 100 ze ak kouch mou nan nich ki fon nan sab la anvan li tounen lanmè. Pandan chak arribada, milyon ze depoze, men se ti kras ki rive siviv, paske anpil ze ak ti tòti vin viktim bèt tankou chen sovaj, vauti, ak lòt menas.

Pou pwoteje tòti yo ak ze yo, moun lokal yo pran kèk ze pandan de premye jou yo—ze sa yo ta ka detwi si lòt tòti travèse plaj la pita. Kominote a pase anpil tan ap netwaye plaj la epi veye tòti ak nich yo, yo fyè anpil pou wòl yo nan evènman sa a.

Ingo fè remake tòti yo byen abitye ak moun sou plaj la epi yo konsantre sou mete ze yo. Men, nan lanmè a yo pi timid epi itilize sans yo pou proteje tèt yo. Malgre defi yo, arribada ki kontinye fèt sou Plaj Ostional la pèmèt tòti Olive Ridley yo kontinye egziste pou jenerasyon k'ap vini yo. Ingo di li te sezi anpil lè li te temwen evènman sa a—li di se yon leson sou kapasite ak rezistans lanati.

article_content: The Indian cricket community celebrated on social media after all 41 workers trapped in the Silkyara tunnel in Uttarakhand were rescued successfully. Legendary spinner Anil Kumble praised the operation for its 'patience, grit, and perseverance,' expressing happiness for the reunited families and wishing the rescued workers a speedy recovery. Former middle-order batter Suresh Raina expressed relief and gratitude, thanking the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF), and the Indian Army for their efforts. Ex-cricketer VVS Laxman highlighted the power of faith, dedication, and perseverance, showing deep appreciation for all individuals involved in the rescue. The Mumbai Indians (MI), five-time IPL champions, saluted the NDRF, SDRF, Indian Army, tunnelling experts Arnold Dix and Chris Cooper, and the team of rat hole mining experts for their relentless belief throughout the 17-day rescue mission. Chennai Super Kings (CSK), also five-time IPL champions, expressed relief and admiration for the workers' bravery. On Tuesday, all 41 workers were evacuated from the Silkyara Tunnel. The rescued workers included 15 from Jharkhand, two from Uttarakhand, five from Bihar, three from West Bengal, eight from Uttar Pradesh, five from Odisha, two from Assam, and one from Himachal Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi commended the courage and patience of the workers and their families, along with the bravery and determination of the rescuers. He also noted that everyone involved in the operation set an example of humanity and teamwork.

article_content: There is ongoing debate about who is the best football player in the world, but when it comes to transfer value, Lionel Messi sits at the top. A week before the Ballon d'Or awards, Swiss research group the Football Observatory, part of the International Centre for Sports Studies (CIES), has named Messi as the most expensive player. Messi is estimated to be worth $262 million, far above his rival Cristiano Ronaldo, who is valued at $158 million. Both players, along with Germany's World Cup-winning captain Manuel Neuer, are in contention for this year's Ballon d'Or in Switzerland. CIES calculates player values with a proprietary algorithm that considers more than 1,500 transfer deals since 2009, factoring in performance, player characteristics, and achievements at both club and international levels. Eden Hazard and his Chelsea teammate Diego Costa rank third and fourth at $158 million and $100 million, respectively. Paul Pogba of Juventus is the only Serie A player in the top 10, valued at $86 million, ahead of Manchester City's Sergio Aguero (£77 million). Liverpool's 20-year-old Raheem Sterling is sixth on the list, valued at $75 million, just ahead of Chelsea's Cesc Fabregas, who is listed at $74 million. Arsenal's Alexis Sanchez is ranked ninth with a $73 million valuation, while Real Madrid's Gareth Bale is tenth at $71 million. Notably, Brazil and Barcelona's Neymar just missed the top 10, with Manchester United's Angel di Maria, Bayern Munich's Mario Gotze, and World Cup star James Rodriguez also outside the top spots.

The Buzz Centris Class 2 Folding e-bike is designed for easy portability, folding down to about half its riding size. While e-bikes have surged in popularity, one challenge has been transporting them because of their weight and size. During the pandemic, I enjoyed using my first battery-powered bike, but realized that taking it beyond my neighborhood was difficult. For example, fitting it into my Prius required a large car rack and trailer hitch, which would have cost over $900 and may have risked voiding my car warranty.

Discovering the Buzz Centris this fall made transportation much easier. The bike comes mostly assembled out of the box—just unfold the frame and handlebars, lock them into place, twist out the pedals, and adjust the seat. The Buzz Centris offers a top speed of 20 MPH, five levels of power assist, a 6-speed Shimano Tourney derailleur, plus fat tires, a bright headlight, and both front and rear racks that install in minutes.

I tested its portability by folding the Buzz Centris and fitting it not only into my Prius, but also into my mother’s compact Honda Fit. Riding the bike felt smooth and intuitive, with a tighter turning radius than my larger RadRover e-bike. The streamlined LCD controls were easy to use, although some button labels were confusing at first.

In riding mode, the Buzz Centris measures 68”L x 23”H x 53”D. Folded, it reduces to 34”L x 22”H x 34”D. At over 70 pounds including accessories, the bike isn’t lightweight, and my 85-year-old mother couldn’t lift it. Still, after folding it down, I was able to slide the bike into the back of the Honda Fit with the rear seats folded. Achieving this made me feel hopeful and inspired—it’s the first e-bike I’ve had that truly goes wherever I need it.
translated_content:
Buzz Centris Class 2 Folding e-bike fèt pou fasilite transpò, paske li ka pliye pou l tounen mwatye dimansyon li nòmalman genyen. E-bikes yo fèk vin anpil popilè, men yonn nan pwoblèm yo se jan yo lou ak gwo. Pandan peryòd pandemi a, mwen te renmen monte premye bisiklèt elektrik mwen, men li te difisil pou mete li deyò zòn mwen, espesyalman nan Prius pa mwen. Sa te mande pou achte yon gwo rack ak yon trailer hitch, ki ta koute plis pase $900 epi sa te ka mete garanti machin nan an danje.

Lè mwen te dekouvri Buzz Centris la sezon sa a, tout sa vin pi fasil. Li rive prèske konplè; ou jis bezwen ouvè kad ak volan an, kenbe yo an plas, tòde pedal yo, epi ajiste chèz la. Buzz Centris la ka roule jiska 20 mil pa èdtan, li gen 5 nivo asistans, 6-vitès Shimano Tourney deraye, gwo kawotchou, limyè devan byen klere, epi rack devan ak dèyè ki fasil pou enstale.

Mwen fè tès pou wè si m ka pliye Buzz Centris epi mete li non sèlman nan Prius mwen, men tou nan ti Honda Fit manman m nan. Kondwi bisiklèt la se te yon bèl eksperyans, ak yon jan fasil pou fè viraj pase gwo RadRover mwen. LCD kontwòl li yo klè, malgre kèk bouton yo te difisil pou konprann okòmansman.

Lè l ap itilize, Buzz Centris mezire 68”L x 23”H x 53”D; pliye, li vin 34”L x 22”H x 34”D. Avèk plis pase 70 liv ak tout akseswa, li pa lejè, e manman mwen ki gen 85 an pa t' ka leve li. Men, mwen te ka glise l fasil nan dèyè Honda Fit la lè tout plas yo desann. Sa te ban m' espwa ak kè kontan—se premye e-bike mwen ki ka ale ak mwen nenpòt kote!

article_content: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ondo State has alleged that former chairmen of the state’s 18 local governments are still being paid salaries after leaving their roles. In a statement issued by the party’s Publicity Secretary, Kennedy Peretei, the PDP claims these ex-council leaders have failed to hand over responsibilities to senior officials or return official government vehicles since their terms ended in August. The PDP attributes this situation to Governor Rotimi Akeredolu’s ongoing medical absence in Ibadan, which they say has caused a lack of leadership and delayed appointments for new local officials. The party also notes that Ondo State has missed major federal meetings, including gatherings with President Bola Tinubu and sessions of the National Economic Council. Party leaders say they oppose any attempt by supporters of the governor to exploit the turmoil for personal gain or allow the state’s administration to decline. The allegations were strongly denied by the former local government chairmen, all members of the All Progressives Congress (APC). Augustine Oloruntogbe, ex-chairman of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria in Ondo State, called the PDP’s claims untrue, stressing none of the chairmen have been paid or had ties to council funds after leaving office on August 30, 2023. He explained he only participated in government programs as a private individual, not in an official capacity. Prince Kayode Aroloye, ex-chairman of Idanre Local Council, echoed this view and demanded a retraction and public apology from the PDP within 24 hours, warning of legal consequences otherwise. Both Oloruntogbe and Aroloye emphasized protecting their integrity and rejected what they described as politically motivated attacks.

PDP a blame sitiyasyon sa sou absans kontinyèl Gouvènè Rotimi Akeredolu, ki ap pran swen sante li Ibadan, e yo di sa lakoz mank lidèchip epi pa gen nouvo otorite ki nonmen ankor pou dirije lokalite yo. Pati a fè konnen Eta Ondo rate gwo rankont federal tankou ak Prezidan Bola Tinubu ak reyinyon Konsèy Ekonomik Nasyonal la. Lidè pati a di yo ret ap vire tout efò pou zansèt gouvènè a pa pwofite dezòd sa a oubyen kite administrasyon eta a degrade. Akizasyon sa yo te konteste ak tout fòs pa ansyen chèf gouvènman lokal yo, ki se manm pati All Progressives Congress (APC). Toulede soulinye entegrite yo epi rejte tout fòm atak politik sou non yo.

article_content: Mervyn Westfield, a former fast bowler for Essex County Cricket Club, has become the first English cricketer to admit involvement in a match-fixing scandal. On January 12, 2012, Westfield pleaded guilty to corruption charges at London’s Old Bailey court. The court heard that Westfield, then 23, was paid £6,000 by a betting syndicate to manipulate his bowling during a Natwest Pro40 match against Durham on September 5, 2009. Specifically, he was asked to allow 12 runs to be scored in his first over. However, only 10 runs were actually scored. Westfield admitted accepting the money but claimed he did not fulfill the agreement. His barrister, Mark Milliken-Smith QC, told the court that Westfield received numerous approaches to fix games but decided not to follow through. The identity of the individual who organized the fix, described as well-known in cricket circles, was not revealed during the hearing. The prosecution's case relied mainly on Westfield's own confession to a teammate. Authorities also noted cooperation among agencies, including the International Cricket Council, England and Wales Cricket Board, Essex County Cricket Club, and the UK Gambling Commission, in the investigation. Westfield was granted unconditional bail and is set to be sentenced on February 10. The judge, Anthony Morris QC, indicated that a custodial sentence is possible. This case follows a major spot-fixing scandal that led to jail sentences for three Pakistani cricketers and their British agent. The prosecution said the successful use of anti-corruption legislation in this case could have far-reaching impacts on cricket worldwide. Angus Porter, CEO of the Professional Cricketers’ Association, welcomed Westfield’s guilty plea, emphasizing the importance of integrity in sport and ongoing education against corruption. Westfield, released from Essex, now plays club cricket. The authorities hope this prosecution sends a strong deterrent message to professional athletes.
translated_content: Mervyn Westfield, yon ansyen jwetè vit pou Essex County Cricket Club, te vin premye jwè kwikèt Angle ki admèt patisipasyon li nan yon eskandal aranjman match. Sou 12 janvye 2012, Westfield te plede koupab pou koripsyon devan tribinal Old Bailey nan Lond. Tribinal la te tande ke Westfield, ki te gen 23 ane le moman an, te resevwa £6,000 nan men yon gwoup paryaj pou chanje fason li t ap jwe pandan yon match Natwest Pro40 kont Durham, 5 septanm 2009. Yo te mande li kite 12 kous sòti nan premye seri boul li a, men sèlman 10 kous te ale. Westfield admèt li te pran lajan an men li di li pa t reyalize magouy la jan yo te dakò a. Avoka li, Mark Milliken-Smith QC, te di tribinal la ke Westfield te resevwa anpil lòt pwopozisyon pou ranje match men li te refize yo. Yo pa t bay non moun ki òganize magouy la, men se yon moun popilè nan mond kwikèt la. Ka a baze prensipalman sou konfèsyon Westfield te fè ak youn nan koekipye li yo. Otorite yo site sipò plizyè ajans tankou International Cricket Council, England and Wales Cricket Board, Essex County Cricket Club, ak UK Gambling Commission nan ankèt la. Fox News panelist Eric Bolling sparked controversy after making a sexist joke during Wednesday's broadcast of 'The Five.' The discussion centered on Maj. Mariam Al Mansouri, the first female fighter pilot from the United Arab Emirates, who recently led an airstrike against ISIS. Panelist Kimberly Guilfoyle praised Major Al Mansouri's achievement, saying, 'Hey ISIS, you were bombed by a woman. The first female pilot for the UAE led the strikes, dropping bombs on ISIS.'

Following Guilfoyle's praise, co-panelist Greg Gutfield joked, 'Problem is, after she bombed it, she couldn't park it.' An upset Guilfoyle attempted to continue her commentary, but the discussion was interrupted when Bolling remarked, 'Would that be considered boobs on the ground, or no?' Guilfoyle expressed her dismay, and Andrea Tantaros, another female panelist, reacted in shock as the panelists talked over one another.

The segment was rebroadcast by anchor Greta van Susteren on her own show. She questioned whether the male panelists, excluding Bob Beckel, should be given a chance to rethink their comments, suggesting the panel might be in trouble for their remarks.

Viewers took to social media to condemn Bolling’s comments, using terms like 'crazy sexism' and 'disrespectful and disgusting.' Twitter users also criticized Gutfield's remarks, and the phrase 'boobs on the ground' led to widespread discussion about sexism at Fox News. However, some social media users defended the jokes, labeling them as humorous.

Maj. Al Mansouri has spoken about the challenges she faced entering a male-dominated field, saying she had to wait almost ten years before becoming a fighter pilot. She noted that women entering such fields often encounter hesitation, prejudice, and stereotypes, but emphasized that determination and skill allowed her to succeed alongside her male peers.

Nan rezo sosyal yo, anpil moun te eksprime kòlè yo kont Eric Bolling, panelis Fox News la, apre li te fè yon blag seksis pandan emisyon 'The Five' mèkredi. Sijè a te sou Majò Mariam Al Mansouri, premye fanm pilòt avyon gè nan Emira Arab Ini ki sot dirije yon atak sou ISIS. Panelis Kimberly Guilfoyle te felisite Majò Al Mansouri, li di: 'Hey ISIS, se yon fanm ki te bonbe nou. Premye fanm pilòt pou UAE te dirije atak yo, li lage bonm sou ISIS.'

Apre lwanj Guilfoyle la, ko-panelis Greg Gutfield te fè yon lòt blag: 'Pwoblèm nan, apre li fin bonbe yo, li pa t ka pake avyon an.' Guilfoyle pa t kontan epi li te eseye kontinye pale, men diskisyon an te entèwonp lè Bolling mande: 'Èske sa konsidere kòm "tete atè a", wi ou non?' Guilfoyle te mete men sou figi li, epi Andrea Tantaros, yon lòt panelis fi, te sezi pandan tout moun t ap pale yon sèl kou.

Greta van Susteren, yon lòt animatris Fox News, te rebay segman sa li menm sou pwòp emisyon pa li epi li mande si mesye yo, eksepte Bob Beckel, pa ta dwe reflechi sou sa yo te di, paske sa ka bay pwoblèm.

Odyans lan eksprime kòlè yo sou rezo sosyal kont remark Bolling lan, kòmantè tankou 'seksis fou!' ak 'sa pa respekte medam yo.' Gen lòt ki kritike blag Gutfield la tou, e ekspresyon 'tete atè a' pwovoke anpil pale sou seksis sou Fox News. Men, gen moun ki di yo jwenn blag la amizan.

Majò Al Mansouri te pale sou difikilte li te jwenn pou antre nan yon metye kote sèlman gason te abitye la. Li di li te oblije tann prèske dis lane pou li vin pilòt avyon de gè. Li mete aksan sou jan fanm kap eseye rantre nan metye gason toujou ap jwenn dout ak prejije, men li montre ke ak detèminasyon ak konpetans, li menm rive fè sa gason ap fè yo.

article_content: This is the fifth story in The Unmarked Graveyard: Stories from Hart Island series, produced by Radio Diaries. It begins in room 208 of The Belvedere Hotel, situated in Manhattan's theater district on West 48th Street. While many guests at the Belvedere are temporary visitors, a handful have made it their long-term residence. Several of these residents arrived from different parts of the world decades ago and remained in rent-stabilized rooms as the hotel and the city evolved. Among these residents was Hisako Hasegawa, who lived in room 208 for more than 40 years. Even so, she remained a mystery to those around her, and this anonymity persisted even after her death. Born in Japan in 1934, Hasegawa is believed to have moved to New York in the 1970s. Hotel staff remember her fondly: she would walk through the lobby every Friday morning with a shopping cart, greeting everyone with a big smile, and often thanked staff with handwritten, hand-drawn cards. Ali Mahmood, who works for the hotel's owners, said, 'If you wrote her a rent receipt, you might find a beautifully hand-drawn card on your desk the next day.' Jerry, a bellhop, remembers her handwriting as especially graceful, 'like poetry.' Renee Querijero, who lived across the hall, was likely closest to Hasegawa. 'I’m the only one she talks to and she knows my name,' Querijero said, though their conversations seldom went beyond basic pleasantries. Querijero played piano in the evenings, and Hasegawa would often thank her in the hallway for the music. Other long-term residents, like Nancy Boyce, shared the experience of living at the Belvedere. Boyce moved in during the early 1980s, into a small, rent-stabilized apartment—one large room with a private bath and a tiny kitchen. 'People think it’s glamorous to live in a hotel downtown,' she said, 'but the small space becomes challenging over time.' Boyce raised a family there, but after decades, found herself weary of the limitations. She also noticed the isolation many older residents faced, like Hasegawa, who had few if any companions. Historically, New York City had many affordable living arrangements for singles—including SROs, or single room occupancies. In the mid-20th century, there were about 200,000 such units. By the 1970s, many SROs had been closed due to their association with crime. Today, advocates argue that SROs could actually help address the city’s affordable housing crisis. In 2016, Jerry noticed Hasegawa hadn't come downstairs as usual. When staff checked her apartment, they found she had passed away at age 82. Querijero came home to find police in the hallway and realized she knew little about Hasegawa's personal life. No staff remembered seeing Hasegawa with visitors. 'New York is a place for dreamers,' said Mahmood, 'but sometimes those dreams end in solitude.' Hasegawa was buried in a communal grave in plot 379 on Hart Island, New York's public cemetery for unclaimed bodies. This story is part of The Unmarked Graveyard: Stories from Hart Island, produced by Nellie Gilles, and edited by Joe Richman, Deborah George, and Ben Shapiro. Thanks to Alissa Escarce, Mycah Hazel, and Lena Engelstein at Radio Diaries. More stories from the series are available on the Radio Diaries Podcast.
translated_content: Sa a se senkyèm istwa nan seri The Unmarked Graveyard: Stories from Hart Island, ki soti nan Radio Diaries. Istwa a kòmanse nan chanm 208 nan otèl The Belvedere, ki chita nan distri teyat Manhattan, sou West 48th Street. Pandan anpil envite nan Belvedere yo se vizitè tanporè, kèk moun te fè otèl la vin kay yo pou plizyè ane. Gen nan rezidan sa yo ki te soti lòtbò dlo depi plizyè dizèn ane pase epi yo te rete nan chanm ak lwaye fikse pandan otèl la ak vil la te kontinye chanje. Youn nan rezidan sa yo se Hisako Hasegawa, ki te viv nan chanm 208 pandan plis pase 40 ane. Menmsi li te viv la lontan, li te toujou yon mistè pou lòt moun, e anonimite sa te suiv li menm apre li fin mouri. Hasegawa te fèt Japon an 1934, epi yo kwè li te vin New York nan ane 1970 yo. Anplwaye otèl la sonje li ak kè kontan: chak vandredi maten li te pase nan lobbi a ak yon kabwa, salye tout moun ak yon bèl souri, e li te konn remèsye yo ak kat desen ak men. Ali Mahmood, ki travay pou mèt otèl la, di: 'Si ou te ekri li resi lwaye, ou te ka jwenn yon bèl kat men-desen sou biwo ou demen.' Jerry, bellhop la, di ekriti li bèl anpil, 'tankou powèm.' Renee Querijero, ki te rete anfas chanm li, se li menm ki te pi pre Hasegawa. 'Mwen se sèl moun li pale ak li konnen non mwen,' Querijero di, men konvèsasyon yo te dwe kout e senp. Querijero te konn jwe pyano aswè, epi Hasegawa te toujou remèsye li pou mizik la nan koridò a. Lòt rezidan ki te rete lontan, tankou Nancy Boyce, te pataje eksperyans viv nan Belvedere a. Boyce te antre kòmansman ane 1980 yo, nan yon ti apatman ak lwaye fikse—yon sèl gwo chanm ak twalèt prive ak ti kwizin. 'Moun panse se yon bèl bagay pou viv nan otèl nan sant vil la,' li di, 'men ti espas la difisil jan tan ap pase.' Boyce leve yon fanmi la, men apre plizyè dizèn ane, li bouke ak limit yo. Li remake tou jan granmoun tankou Hasegawa te konn izole yo. Nan tan lontan, New York te gen anpil opsyon abòdab pou moun selibatè, tankou inite SRO (single room occupancy). Nan mitan 20yèm syèk la, te gen apeprè 200,000 inite konsa. Nan ane 1970 yo, anpil SRO te fèmen paske yo te asosye ak krim. Jodi a, defansè lojman di SRO ta ka solisyon pou kriz lojman abòdab lan. An 2016, Jerry remake Hasegawa pa t desann jan li te konn fè. Lè anplwaye yo al tcheke, yo jwenn li te mouri nan chanm li a laj 82 an. Querijero tounen lakay li epi li jwenn lapolis nan koridò a, li reyalize li pa t konnen anpil sou lavi pèsonèl Hasegawa. Pa gen anplwaye ki sonje li te resevwa vizitè. 'New York se kote tout moun ap vwayaje pou chèche rèv yo,' Mahmood di, 'men pafwa rèv sa yo fini ak solitid.' Yo te antere Hasegawa nan yon fose komen nan poz 379 sou Hart Island, simityè piblik New York pou moun san fanmi. Istwa sa fè pati The Unmarked Graveyard: Stories from Hart Island, pwodui pa Nellie Gilles, monte pa Joe Richman, Deborah George ak Ben Shapiro. Mèsi ak Alissa Escarce, Mycah Hazel ak Lena Engelstein nan Radio Diaries. Ou ka jwenn plis istwa sou seri sa a nan Radio Diaries Podcast.

article_content: Helena Costa has reconsidered her role as manager of French Ligue 2 club Clermont Foot. Clermont announced Costa’s appointment in May, marking a historic moment as she would have been the first female head coach of a professional French football club, and the first to manage a team in the top two divisions in any of Europe's five major football leagues: Spain, Germany, England, Italy, and France. Claude Michy, president of Clermont, described Costa's decision to step down as 'sudden and surprising' and offered no further explanation for her change of heart. In a statement on the club’s website, Michy said, 'I deeply regret this situation. I thank everyone who has supported me and am very grateful. The club's operations will continue with other stakeholders to prepare for the new season.' Costa, 36, is an accomplished sports science graduate with experience coaching the Iran and Qatar women’s national teams. She also managed Benfica’s male youth team to two world titles and worked as a scout at Scottish club Celtic. There have been other women in prominent roles within men’s professional football. In England, Eva Carneiro served as Chelsea’s first-team doctor, and Karren Brady is the vice-chairman of West Ham United. Former England women's head coach Hope Powell was once linked to a managerial role at Grimsby Town but denied she was in contention. In Italy, Carolina Morace managed Serie C1 side Viterbese for two matches in 1999. In Spain, Maria Jose Claramunt is the director of the national team, though her responsibilities are focused on marketing rather than sporting matters.

Prezidan Clermont lan, Claude Michy, di desizyon Costa a kite se te yon bagay "soudèn ak etonan," epi li pa bay plis eksplikasyon sou chanjman lide sa. Nan yon deklarasyon sou sitwèb klèb la, Michy di: 'Mwen regrèt anpil sitiyasyon sa a. Mèsi a tout moun ki te sipòte mwen e mwen vrèman rekonesan. Klib la ap kontinye fonksyone ak lòt moun pou prepare sezon kap vini an.' Costa, ki gen 36 lane, se yon gradye syans espò ak anpil eksperyans kòm antrenè ekip nasional dam Iran ak Qatar. Li te dirije ekip jèn gason Benfica a pou li ranpòte de tit mondyal epi li te sèvi kòm eskout pou klib Celtic nan peyi Laskòs. Gen lòt fanm ki okipe gwo posisyon pou klib gason tou. article_content: Taylor Swift announced on social media Saturday evening that she was postponing her concert in Rio de Janeiro due to dangerously high temperatures and safety concerns. This decision came a day after 23-year-old Ana Clara Benevides Machado, a fan, died before Swift’s Eras Tour show at Nilton Santos Stadium. Swift explained on Instagram Stories that she was writing from her dressing room and that putting the safety and well-being of fans, performers, and crew above all else led to the postponement. On Friday, temperatures at the stadium reached 35°C (95°F), and some concertgoers complained about the lack of access to water. Reports indicate that Benevides Machado asked for help at the stadium before the show began, feeling unwell, and was taken to Hospital Salgado Filho where she later died. While reports attribute her death to cardiorespiratory arrest, the official cause has not yet been confirmed. Other attendees said they couldn't bring water inside and found it difficult to obtain once inside the venue. Video from the concert shows Swift pausing her performance to call for water distribution after fans requested it. She was also seen personally throwing a water bottle to the crowd. In response to the incident, Rio’s Mayor Eduardo Paes called the fan’s death 'unacceptable' on social media and ordered officials to work with organizers to improve safety, including faster entry, more water distribution points, and increased medical presence. Brazilian officials, including National Consumer Secretary Wadih Damous and Justice Minister Flávio Dino, emphasized the need for accessible free water at events and announced immediate policy reviews. Event organizers stated that sealed water cups would now be allowed. Swift expressed how devastated she was by the loss and offered condolences to the fan’s family and friends, describing it as something she never imagined when bringing her tour to Brazil.

Rapò yo endike Benevides Machado te mande èd nan estad la anvan konsè a te kòmanse, li t ap santi li mal, epi yo te mennen li lopital Salgado Filho kote li te mouri pita. article_content: Marketing Edge has rejected claims by the National Institute of Marketing of Nigeria (NIMN) that it breached the institute’s Act 2003 concerning ‘rating’ activities. The media organization is demanding an apology and a retraction from NIMN, calling the allegations damaging, according to an official statement. A letter signed by Marketing Edge’s attorney, Felix Akinnisola of Akinnisola – Olubodun & Co Chambers, asked the NIMN Council to retract its statements. The letter accuses NIMN of launching a campaign of unfounded allegations, malicious damage, and spreading falsehoods. Marketing Edge argues that the claims made by NIMN are misplaced, ill-advised, and baseless. The letter states that Marketing Edge is not registered with NIMN, either by membership or practice, and therefore is not subject to its supervision or regulations. It further criticizes NIMN for failing to verify which organizations are registered members before making public accusations. Marketing Edge’s letter describes NIMN’s allegations as vague, lacking clarity regarding the specific section of the law that was allegedly breached. The letter emphasizes that Marketing Edge’s activities do not attempt to regulate the marketing profession, which is NIMN’s authority. As a research and media organization, Marketing Edge asserts its constitutional right to express opinions based on its research and media practice, without requiring NIMN’s approval. The letter argues that NIMN’s claims of a breach amount to an attack on free speech, which is protected by the Nigerian Constitution and the UN Charter of Human Rights. Marketing Edge criticizes NIMN for publishing its accusations in The Punch Newspaper on November 24, 2023, before awaiting a response to its letter dated November 8, 2023. According to Marketing Edge, the publication was intended to harm its business, corporate, and personal reputation, built over years of ethical practice.
translated_content: Marketing Edge rejte akizasyon Enstiti Nasyonal Maketing Nijerya (NIMN) souke li te vyole Lwa 2003 Enstiti a konsènan aktivite 'rating'. Òganizasyon medya a egzije eskiz ak retrè nan men NIMN, li di akizasyon yo ap fè dòm, dapre yon deklarasyon ofisyèl. Yon lèt ki siyen pa avoka Marketing Edge, Felix Akinnisola nan Akinnisola – Olubodun & Co Chambers, mande Konsèy NIMN pou li retire deklarasyon li yo. Lèt la akize NIMN de lanse fo akizasyon, domaj malveyan, epi gaye fo nouvèl. Marketing Edge di reklamasyon yo soti nan NIMN pa kòrèk, pa konsiltan, e pa gen baz. Lèt la deklare Marketing Edge pa anrejistre ak NIMN, ni kòm manm ni pa pratik, epi kidonk li pa sijè a sipèvizyon oswa règ li yo. Li plis kritike NIMN paske yo pa verifye ki òganizasyon ki manm anvan yo fè akizasyon piblik. Lèt Marketing Edge a dekri akizasyon NIMN yo tankou vag, san klarte sou seksyon lwa yo di ki te vyole. Lèt la soulve ke aktivite Marketing Edge yo pa pran ni fè kòm si li ap reglemante pwofesyon maketing lan, ki se otorite NIMN. Kòm yon òganizasyon rechèch ak medya, Marketing Edge reklame dwa konstitisyonèl li pou eksprime opinyon dapre rechèch li ak pratik medya, san bezwen apwobasyon NIMN. Lèt la defann reklamasyon NIMN sou vyolasyon se yon atak sou libète lapawòl, ki pwoteje pa Konstitisyon Nijerya ak Charter Dwa Moun Nasyonzini. Marketing Edge kritike NIMN paske yo pibliye akizasyon yo nan The Punch Newspaper 24 Novanm 2023, anvan li tann repons a lèt li te voye 8 Novanm 2023. Dapre Marketing Edge, piblikasyon an te gen entansyon detwi repitasyon biznis, konpayi, ak pèsonèl li, sabatani pa ane de pratik etik.

Surface ice in Greenland has been melting at an increasing rate over recent decades, while Antarctica has experienced a declining trend in surface melt, according to researchers from the University of California, Irvine, and Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a recent paper published in Geophysical Research Letters, the scientists examined the role of Foehn and katabatic winds—downslope gusts that bring warm, dry air in contact with glacier surfaces. Their findings show that wind-driven melting of the Greenland ice sheet has increased by more than 10% in the past 20 years, whereas the effect of these winds on the Antarctic ice sheet has decreased by 32%.

"We used regional climate model simulations to study ice sheets in both Greenland and Antarctica. The results demonstrate that downslope winds are responsible for a significant portion of surface melt in both regions," said co-author Charlie Zender, UCI professor of Earth system science. He noted that surface melt leads to runoff and hydrofracturing of ice shelves, which increases the flow of freshwater into the oceans and contributes to rising sea levels.

While the impact of winds is considerable, Zender explained that global warming produces different responses in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, resulting in contrasting outcomes for these polar regions. In Greenland, the effect of winds on surface melt is magnified as the region becomes so warm that sunlight alone—without the presence of wind—is enough to cause melting. The 10% increase in wind-driven melt, combined with higher surface air temperatures, has resulted in a 34% rise in total surface melt on Greenland. Zender attributes this in part to changes in the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO), as a positive phase of the NAO has led to lower-than-normal atmospheric pressure in high latitudes, ushering warm air toward Greenland and other Arctic areas.

By comparison, total surface melt in Antarctica has dropped by about 15% since 2000. This reduction is primarily due to a 32% decrease in downslope wind-generated melt on the Antarctic Peninsula, where two vulnerable ice shelves have already collapsed. Zender points out that the ongoing recovery of the Antarctic ozone hole, first discovered in the 1980s, has been beneficial, offering temporary insulation of the surface against further melting.

"The ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica together keep over 200 feet of water out of the ocean, and their melt has raised global sea level by about three-quarters of an inch since 1992," Zender explained. "Although Greenland has been the primary driver of sea level rise in recent decades, Antarctica is gaining ground and is expected to eventually dominate sea level rise. Monitoring and modeling the melt of both ice sheets, including how climate change alters the interaction between wind and ice, is vital."

Zender hopes that this research on the influence of Foehn and katabatic winds in polar regions will help the climate science community enhance the accuracy of Earth system models. He collaborated on the project with Matthew Laffin and Wenshan Wang from UCI’s Department of Earth System Science, along with Melchior van Wessem and Brice Noel from Utrecht University’s Institute for Marine and Atmospheric Research.

Behrang Safari, involved in the incident that led to Liverpool's Champions League exit, has denied diving to get Lazar Markovic sent off and claims he was bleeding from the mouth afterward. During the must-win match for Liverpool, who were trailing 1-0 to Basle, Serbian winger Markovic was shown a red card in the 61st minute—only 16 minutes after coming on as a substitute—for making minimal contact with Safari while trying to break free from his marker.

When asked by Swedish newspaper Sportbladet whether he was struck, Safari responded, 'Yes, of course. I was bleeding from my mouth.' The 29-year-old Swedish defender said he did not realize Markovic had been sent off until he was confronted by angry Liverpool players. 'I wouldn’t have gone to ground if he hadn’t hit me. I am not the kind of player who dives,' Safari stated. He added, 'It was a bit strange, I didn’t realize it was a red card at first. I thought the referee had blown the whistle for a head injury and that I would just give the ball back to Liverpool afterwards. Then I noticed the Liverpool players were angry with me.'

Referee Bjorn Kuipers showed Markovic a red card, prompting strong protests from Liverpool defender Dejan Lovren and manager Brendan Rodgers. 'I thought the sending off was a really disappointing decision by the referee,' Rodgers said. 'Lazar Markovic gets sent off for that, his fingernail barely touches the nose of the defender, and the defender’s reaction should be scrutinized.'

Liverpool managed to equalize in the 82nd minute through a Steven Gerrard free-kick but were unable to score a winning goal to reach the Champions League knockout stages, resulting in Basle advancing instead.

Pandan match Liverpool te oblije genyen an, kote yo te dèyè 1-0 kont Basle, Markovic, jwè Sèb la, te pran kat wouj nan 61yèm minit—sèlman 16 minit apre li rantre kòm remplacan—pou yon kontak minim li fè ak Safari pandan li t ap chèche sove anba gad li.

Defansè swedwa 29-zan an di li pa t konnen Markovic te pran kat wouj la jiskaske jwè Liverpool yo te begyn fache avèk li. 'Mwen pa t ap jete kò m atè si li pa t frape m. Mwen pa se sa ki simile,' Safari kontinye. 'Sa te tris, mwen pa t konprann se te yon kat wouj okòmansman. Mwen te panse abit la te sone pou blesi nan tèt e mwen t ap voye balon an tounen bay Liverpool apre sa. Men apre m wè, jwè Liverpool yo te fache ak mwen.'

Abit Bjorn Kuipers bay Markovic yon kat wouj, sa ki lakoz Dejan Lovren ak manadjè Brendan Rodgers, tou de nan Liverpool, pwoteste yon fason fache. 'Mwen panse desizyon pou voye Markovic ale a te move anpil,' Rodgers di. 'Li sèlman manyen nen defansè a ak zong li, epi se reyaksyon defansè a yo ta dwe ezamine.'

Liverpool egalize nan 82yèm minit gras ak frikik Steven Gerrard, men yo pa t ka jwenn gòl viktwa a pou yo pase nan faz eliminatwa Champions League la, donk se Basle ki pase pito.

article_content: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled in favor of BBC World (India) in a transfer pricing case, dismissing the revenue department’s appeal. Income Tax authorities had attempted to categorize advertisement and other expenses borne by BBC World (India) Pvt Ltd as part of the cost base for charging a mark-up. Using this cost-based method would have increased BBC World (India)’s taxable income. However, ITAT regarded these advertisement expenses as pass-through costs since they were not directly tied to the company's main business activities. Expenses for advertisement, publicity, business promotion, and participation in trade events were undertaken by BBC World (India) at the request of associated overseas entities under their agreements and were found to be non-core expenses. ITAT upheld the Commissioner of Income Tax Appeals’ view that the budget for these expenses was controlled by the associated enterprise (AE) and that the AE bore the risk and outcome of these expenses. The expenses in question mainly concerned the purchase of advertisement space in newspapers, viewed as high in cost but requiring minimal operational effort by BBC World (India). Thus, ITAT ruled these should be treated as pass-through costs. The primary activities of BBC World (India) involve the sale of airtime for advertisement, the marketing of the BBC Channel to cable operators, and promotion to viewers. Tax experts state this ruling highlights the need for clear and robust documentation for companies involved in transfer pricing transactions. Tax specialist Nitin Narang, Partner for Transfer Pricing at Nangia Andersen India, noted, 'The Delhi Tribunal, in BBC World (India) Pvt Ltd’s case for AY 2004-05, considered advertisement expenses as pass-through costs and excluded them from the cost base used for applying a mark-up. This again highlights the importance of solid documentation supporting inter-company transactions.' In other news, India’s industrial growth declined in September 2023 to 5.8%, down from a 14-month high of 10.3% in August, impacted by excess rainfall and a shift in the festival calendar. Ranjan Pai, Chairman of Manipal Education and Medical Group, invested ₹1,400 crore (approx. $168 million) in Aakash Institute, a subsidiary of Byju’s. Younger graduates are increasingly being hired by manufacturing companies as they bring fresh digital skills, according to Dilip Pattanayak, chief human resources officer at JSW Group.

Men, ITAT konsidere depans piblisite sa yo kòm depans ki travèse dirèk, paske yo pa t relye ak prensipal aktivite biznis konpayi an. Depans pou piblisite, pwomosyon biznis, ak patisipasyon nan evènman komèsyal te fèt pa BBC World (India) dapre demann antite asosye etranje yo, epi yo pa t konsidere kòm depans debaz. ITAT dakò ak Komisyonè Apèl Taks sou Revni ke bidjè depans sa yo te kontwole pa antite asosye a (AE), epi AE a te pran risk ak konsekans depans sa yo. Depans sa yo te konsantre prensipalman sou achte espas piblisite nan jounal, kote depans yo wo men efò BBC World (India) te fè a pa t twò anpil. ITAT deside yo ta dwe trete yo kòm depans ki travèse dirèk. Aktivite prensipal BBC World (India) se vann tan piblisite, fè maketing Chèn BBC la bay operatè kab, epi ankouraje moun pou gade chèn nan. Ekspè nan taks yo di desizyon sa a mete aksan sou nesesite bon dokiman lè w ap jere tranzaksyon pri transfè. Espesyalis taks Nitin Narang, patnè nan pri transfè nan Nangia Andersen India, deklare: 'Tribinal Delhi a, nan ka BBC World (India) Pvt Ltd pou ane fiskal 2004-05, te konsidere depans piblisite kòm depans ki travèse dirèk, konsa yo pa te enkli yo nan baz pri pou kalkile maj benefis la. Sa montre ankò enpòtans bon dokiman pou sipòte tranzaksyon ant konpayi yo.' Nan lòt nouvèl, kwasans endistriyèl peyi Zend bese nan mwa septanm 2023 a 5.8%, dèpi sot pase 10.3% an out, akoz lapli depase ak chanjman nan kalandriye fèt yo. Jèn gradye yo ap rantre plis nan konpayi fabrikasyon paske yo pote ladrès dijital fre yo, dapre Dilip Pattanayak, chèf resous imen JSW Group.

article_content: One hundred years after the start of World War One, Britons are being invited to help read and tag digitized diaries of soldiers who served in France and Flanders. The goal is to extract details from these diaries to build a more complete and personal picture of the conflict. Operation War Diary is an online crowdsourcing project that relies on public volunteers to fill in historical gaps and tag diary entries. This helps experts understand how the war was fought and serves as a memorial for those who lost their lives. More than 1.5 million pages of Western Front war diaries are being digitized, tagged, and made available online through the First World War 100 portal, with Operation War Diary as a central component. This project is a collaboration between The National Archives, Imperial War Museums (IWM), and Zooniverse, aiming to create new 'citizen historians'. The initiative aims to make previously inaccessible information available to academics, researchers, and family historians worldwide, leaving a lasting legacy for the First World War centenary. The platform allows users to tag critical details such as names, places, and events from assigned segments of war diaries. This data can then reveal what happened to army units, who was involved, casualty numbers, and the conditions at specific times and places. Experts use the information to create indexes that aggregate data across multiple entries, providing fresh insights into life on the Western Front. This enables academics to study broad patterns and answer specific questions using extensive data. In addition to stories of bravery and hardship from the trenches, Operation War Diary is expected to uncover unknown stories and extraordinary events from 1914–1919. William Spencer, a military records specialist at The National Archives, said making these diaries available online allows people worldwide to explore the daily activities and battles of each unit, potentially leading to new perspectives on the war. Operation War Diary utilizes technology originally designed to map stars, repurposed to collect new firsthand accounts of World War One. Users assigned segments of a diary tag key details, enriching catalogue descriptions, helping family historians trace ancestors, and providing researchers with a clearer picture of the conflict. War diaries were initially kept to provide accurate records for official histories and to improve army preparations. They now offer unmatched insight into daily life, with stories and decisions extending beyond military reports. The National Archives has digitized diaries from units under British and Indian divisions on the Western Front, including various materials: cover pages, orders, signals, maps, narrative reports, and diary entries. Information from Operation War Diary will also contribute to the IWM’s Lives of the First World War project, creating a permanent digital memorial to over eight million men and women from Britain and the Commonwealth. Currently, 100 unit war diaries are available on Operation War Diary, with more to follow. Luke Smith, Digital Lead for IWM’s Centenary Programme, stated the project will reveal new day-to-day information about life in the First World War, offering details not found in letters or traditional history books. Data contributed by volunteers will enrich catalogue descriptions, help family historians trace army ancestors, and provide researchers with a deeper understanding of how the war was fought.
translated_content: Yon santèn ane apre kòmansman Premye Gè Mondyal la, Britanik yo ap envite ede li ak make jounal sòlda ki te sèvi an Frans ak Fland. Objektif la se jwenn plis detay sou eksperyans sòlda yo pou bati yon imaj plis pèsonèl ak konplè sou lagè a. Operation War Diary se yon pwojè sou entènèt ki mande èd piblik la pou rempli mank enfòmasyon epi make sa sòlda yo ekri. Sa ede ekspè konprann kijan lagè a te fèt epi se yon omaj pou tout moun ki pèdi lavi yo. Plis pase 1.5 milyon paj jounal sòlda yo ap dijitalize, make epi mete sou entènèt atravè First World War 100 portal la, kote Operation War Diary se yon pati kle. Sa se yon kolaborasyon ant The National Archives, Imperial War Museums (IWM), ak Zooniverse, ak objektif pou kreye nouvo 'sitwayen istoryen'. Inisyativ la ap rann enfòmasyon ki difisil pou jwenn vin disponib pou akademisyen, chèchè ak istoryen fanmi atravè lemond, konsa l ap kite yon eritaj dirab pou sentenè Premye Gè Mondyal la. Platfòm lan fasilite itilizatè yo pou make non, kote ak evènman ki enpòtan sou chak segment jounal sòlda yo. Ekspè yo sèvi ak done sa yo pou kreye endèks ki rasanble enfòmasyon sou plizyè paj, konsa yo jwenn nouvo konprann sou lavi sou Western Front la. Sa pèmèt akademisyen etidye gwo modèl ak reponn kesyon presi gras ak anpil done reyèl. Anplis istwa kouraj ak soufrans nan transe yo, Operation War Diary espere dekouvri lòt istwa ak evènman ekstraòdinè ki pa t janm konnen soti 1914 rive 1919. William Spencer, espesyalis dosye militè nan The National Archives, di mete jounal sa yo sou entènèt ap pèmèt pèp la dekouvri aktivite ak batay chak inite, e sa ka pote nouvo pèspektiv sou lagè a. Operation War Diary itilize teknoloji ki te konn sèvi pou kat zetwal, epi kounye a l ap ede rasanble nouvo temwayaj sou Premye Gè Mondyal la. Itilizatè ki resevwa moso jounal ap make detay enpòtan, sa ap anrichi deskripsyon jounal yo, ede fanmi jwenn tras zansèt sòlda yo, epi bay chèchè plis konpreyansyon sou lagè a. Jounal lagè yo te fèt pou bay dosye presi pou listwa ofisyèl epi ede amelyore preparasyon lame. Jodi a, yo ofri anpil detay sou lavi chak jou sòlda yo, ak istwa ak desizyon ki pi rich pase rapò senp militè yo. The National Archives deja dijitalize jounal plizyè inite anba divizyon Britanik ak Endyen sou Western Front la, ki gen ladan paj kouvèti, lòd, siy, kat, rapò naratif ak paj jounal. Enfòmasyon ki soti nan Operation War Diary ap sèvi tou ak pwojè IWM 'Lives of the First World War', pou kreye yon memwa dijital pèmanan pou plis pase uit milyon fanm ak gason Grann Bretay ak Commonwealth la. Kounye a, 100 jounal inite deja disponib sou Operation War Diary, gen plis k ap vini. Luke Smith, Chèf Dijital IWM, di pwojè a pral revele nouvo detay sou lavi chak jou pandan Premye Gè Mondyal la, detay ki pa te janm parèt nan lèt oswa liv listwa tradisyonèl. Done volontè yo ap sèvi pou anrichi deskripsyon jounal yo, ede fanmi w jwenn zansèt sòlda yo, epi bay rechèchè plis klè sou kijan yo te fè lagè a.

article_content: A meteor, estimated to weigh 500 pounds, lit up the sky as it passed over New York, Pennsylvania, and Ohio early Tuesday morning. The meteor, which was about two feet in diameter, was captured on video traveling at 45,000 miles per hour by three NASA surveillance cameras at around 4:45am EST on February 17. Despite its small size, it shone brighter than a full moon. NASA experts said the meteor likely broke apart and disintegrated over Kittanning, Pennsylvania. The American Meteor Society received at least 96 reports from people who saw the meteor as it traveled overhead. According to NASA, the meteor originated from the asteroid belt located between Mars and Jupiter and was first detected at an altitude of about 65 miles above Pennsylvania. As it descended, it was last observed at about 13 miles above Kittanning. Excited residents shared their experiences on Facebook and Twitter, describing the event as bright and stunning. One witness commented that the meteor lit up both the sky and the snowy landscape in a vibrant blue, while another said it was so bright they thought a transformer had exploded. Some expressed surprise that the meteor wasn't detected earlier.

Malgre li piti, li te eklere plis pase lalin lan lè li plen. Ekspè NASA yo di meteyorit la sanble li te kraze epi disparèt anlè Kittanning, Pennsylvania. American Meteor Society resevwa omwen 96 rapò moun ki te wè meteyorit la pase anlè tèt yo. Selon NASA, meteyorit la te soti nan senti astewoyid ki se ant Mas ak Jipitè epi yo te detekte li pou premye fwa a anviwon 65 mil altitid sou Pennsylvania. Pandan li t ap desann, yo te wè li pou dènye fwa a 13 mil anlè Kittanning. Rezidan ki te eksite pataje sa yo te wè sou Facebook ak Twitter, kote yo dekri evènman an kòm yon bagay klere epi bèl anpil. Yon moun di meteyorit la te eklere syèl la ak nèj la an ble byen fon, e yon lòt di li tèlman te klere yo te panse se yon transfòmatè ki te pete. Gen kèk ki te etone ke yo pa t detekte meteyorit la pi bonè.

article_content: Pat Cummins, captain of the Australian cricket team, made a surprising choice to bowl first after winning the toss in the ODI World Cup final against India, played in Ahmedabad. India had regularly preferred batting first in their previous wins, but Cummins thought the conditions favored fielding at the start. This gamble paid off, with Australia restricting India to a total of 240 runs thanks to disciplined bowling and sharp fielding. Cummins later admitted they debated the decision until just before the toss, reasoning the pitch could improve as the evening progressed. He also highlighted that mistakes in bowling are usually less damaging than errors made while batting under pressure during such a big match. Despite early setbacks that left Australia at 47/3, Travis Head (137 runs) and Marnus Labuschagne (58 not out) combined for a vital 192-run stand, steering Australia to a six-wicket win and securing their sixth World Cup title. Though Indian star Virat Kohli finished as the tournament’s top batter with 765 runs, it was Australia’s day as they outperformed India in front of a stunned Ahmedabad crowd.

Lend te abitye chwazi bat an premye nan viktwa pase yo, men Cummins te panse kondisyon yo t'ap ede lè w ap jwe defans okòmansman. Chwa sa a te mache byen, paske Ostrali te limite Lend nan 240 kouri gras ak bon boulè ak defans solid. Malgre Ostrali te gen difikilte bonè (47 pou 3), Travis Head (137 kouri) ak Marnus Labuschagne (58 san pèdi) mete ansanm pou fè 192 kouri, sa ki pèmèt Ostrali ranpòte viktwa a ak sis wikèt epi pran sizyèm tit Mondyal yo. Malgre vedèt Lend Virat Kohli fini kòm batè ki te fè plis kouri (765), se Ostrali ki te pi fò, epi foul Ahmedabad la te sezi devan bèl jwèt Ostrali a.

Martin Scorsese’s film ‘Killers of the Flower Moon,’ adapted from David Grann’s 2017 bestseller, explores the notorious Osage murders in 1920s Oklahoma—an era the Osage refer to as the 'Reign of Terror.' During this time, the Osage Nation, who had become wealthy through oil discovered on their land, suffered a wave of brutal killings.

Whereas Grann’s book primarily investigates how FBI agents, led by Tom White, uncovered the truth behind these crimes, the film diverges by focusing on the personal dynamics between Mollie Kyle, an Osage woman, and Ernest Burkhart, a World War I veteran recruited to Osage County by his uncle, William K. Hale. Portrayed by Lily Gladstone and Leonardo DiCaprio, their relationship becomes central to the film, weaving together themes of love and betrayal in the shadow of the murder plot orchestrated by Ernest and Hale—a fact that the film divulges early on.

Grann crafted the book as a mystery, documenting the investigation into the deaths of Mollie’s relatives and other Osage, which was driven by greed for their oil money and headrights. The narrative also highlights the formation of the FBI under J. Edgar Hoover. Scorsese, influenced in part by the real Mollie and Ernest’s granddaughter, chose to focus on the emotional journey of Mollie and Ernest rather than on the procedural aspects of the investigation.

This artistic direction has sparked discussion within the Osage community. Christopher Cote, the film’s Osage language consultant, commends Scorsese’s respectful efforts but points out that the story is still largely told from Ernest’s perspective. Cote expresses skepticism about depicting Ernest’s actions as stemming from love, raising questions about interpretation and authenticity. As a result, the film brings both the personal and systemic dimensions of the Osage murders to the forefront, challenging viewers to consider historical truth alongside emotional narrative.

article_content: Baby sea turtles are hatching in record numbers in Florida, but experts say it's too soon to celebrate. Nearly 99% of new hatchlings are female, which could cause problems for future turtle populations. Joel Cohen, director of communication at the Sea Turtle Preservation Society, told Insider that warmer sand temperatures—caused by unusually hot weather linked to climate change—are responsible. For many turtle species, sex is determined by sand temperature during incubation: below 81.8°F mostly produces males, above 88.8°F mostly produces females, and temperatures in between can result in both sexes, according to the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). This year, turtles laid 52,500 nests along Florida’s Space Coast, three times more than the previous record set in 2022, as reported by ABC News. Despite these impressive numbers, between 2018 and 2022, researchers studied hatchlings and found no male sea turtles, according to ecologist Lucy Hawkes from the University of Exeter. Cohen pointed out that turtles do not bury their eggs deep enough to avoid the increasingly warm surface temperatures. For example, sand in Miami’s South Beach reached up to 137°F this summer, USA Today reported. If current warming trends continue, the skewed female-to-male ratio could worsen, creating reproductive challenges in the future. Hawkes notes that if all males disappeared, the population would be at risk, though she doesn't think this will happen soon. Despite these threats, Cohen remains hopeful, noting sea turtles have survived for more than 230 million years and endured multiple mass extinctions, according to the British Natural History Museum. Some turtles are adapting: they're nesting farther north in cooler sands, such as in the Carolinas, and starting the nesting season earlier, sometimes as early as February. Although data on these behaviors is limited, Cohen finds it encouraging. Cohen emphasized, 'They are amazing animals. And they have ways to deal with all kinds of things that have been thrown at them.'

Joel Cohen, direktè kominikasyon nan Sea Turtle Preservation Society, te di Insider ke sab ki vin pi cho—le rezilta tanperati ekstrèm ki gen rapò ak chanjman klimatik—se sa ki lakoz sa. Pou anpil espès tòti, sèks la detèmine pandan enkybasyon an selon tanperati sab la: si l anba 81.8°F, majorite ap sòti gason; si l pi wo pase 88.8°F, majorite ap tounen fi; si l ant de ekst, ap gen tou de sèks, selon U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). Ane sa a, tòti yo te mete 52,500 nich sou Space Coast Florid la, twa fwa plis pase dènye rekò a ki te an 2022, dapre ABC News. article_content: Senior executives at leading UK supermarkets often ignore expiry dates on foods in their homes, with some describing these policies as excessive. A survey found that leaders from supermarkets such as Sainsbury’s, Morrisons, Co-op, Tesco, Waitrose, and Marks & Spencer frequently overlook ‘best-before’ and ‘use-by’ dates, choosing instead to trust their senses, like smelling food, to determine if it is still good. Dalton Philips, the CEO of Morrisons, shared that he typically relies on a ‘smell test’ rather than the date stamped on packaging and criticized some of the rules as ‘ridiculous’—especially for cheeses, which he says often improve over time. Similarly, Mark Price, Waitrose’s managing director, admitted he eats meat, dairy, and produce even a few days after their listed use-by dates.  Even though supermarkets heavily reduce the price of food nearing its sell-by date, massive amounts are still discarded. Tesco, for example, disposed of around 30,000 tonnes of food waste in six months. Activist groups point out that households could save up to £60 each month by reducing food waste. At the same time, government data reveals that Britons’ weekly spending on food and drinks keeps rising. Charities such as Foodcycle advocate for clearer and simpler expiry labels on food to help both consumers and supermarkets, noting that large quantities of edible food are wasted every day. According to the Food Standards Agency, ‘best-before’ labels indicate when a product may lose quality but remain safe, ‘use-by’ dates are for safety, and ‘sell-by’ is intended for shop staff. Campaigners continue to push for improved labeling to curb waste while ensuring consumer safety.

Spongy red dodge balls wait in line, setting the stage for two teams eager to outplay each other. In a matter of moments, players dip and dive across the court until one is left standing, savoring victory. Here, adults participate in a dodge ball league organized by the City of Sparks Parks and Recreation in Nevada. While dodge ball is often seen as a game for kids in gym class, it has made a vibrant comeback among adults in this Nevada community over the past four years. The league now attracts hundreds of professionals—including doctors, lawyers, and teachers—who gather at the recreation center on Sunday nights. 'I think a lot of it goes back to trying to stay young,' says Tony Pehle, the recreation supervisor who started the program, inspired by the 2004 movie 'Dodgeball: A True Underdog Story.' 'They might be adults, but they still like to play and have fun.'

This love of childlike games isn't just local. Across the country, adults are rediscovering activities like dodge ball, double Dutch, and even rock-paper-scissors. The 2009 World Yo-Yo Contest in Orlando, Florida draws more than 150 adult competitors, each eager to showcase new tricks. Later in August, hundreds of adults don costumes and race their handcrafted vehicles in Oregon's Portland Adult Soapbox Derby, an event with roots in the 1930s youth races. 'Once a year, I get to build something for the kid in me,' says Jason Hogue, 41, a carpenter who has raced for eight years. Last year, he crafted a car shaped like a hammerhead shark. 'We get to be creative and have fun with our friends.'

For some, these games are a welcome break from daily pressures or a dose of nostalgia. For others, experts say it may reflect a generation more comfortable with blurring the lines between childhood and adulthood. Adult audiences for shows like Nickelodeon's 'SpongeBob SquarePants' jumped 51% from 1999 to 2009. The World Adult Kickball Association, one of the largest of its kind, now hosts games in 33 states and even maintains troops overseas. Started by a group of friends in Washington, D.C., adult kickball now draws tens of thousands—many looking for a break from work and financial stress. 'I played soccer growing up, and I like competition,' says Marlon LeWinter, 28, from New York City. LeWinter and his team, Chipwich Nation, play for fun and camaraderie, with after-game treats to match. 'Sometimes when the score is tight in kickball, I get the jitters,' he admits.

Economic factors play a role as well. Many of these leagues and contests are affordable, often costing less than $100 for several months—much cheaper than joining a golf club. Companies like Duncan Toys, a leading yo-yo maker, have seen sales rise since the recession, with many adults seeking models they played with as kids. 'Nowadays, things are so serious that people return to something light like yo-yos,' says Mike McBride, a 34-year-old designer and yo-yo competitor. 'It’s my way to relieve stress—no pressure.'

In his 2006 book 'Rejuvenile,' Christopher Noxon looked at why grown-ups are drawn to youthful pastimes. He points out that since the 1990s, as the age for marriage climbed, adults embraced more flexible, creative, and 'quirky' pursuits. This shift has made playground sports and hobbies cool rather than silly. 'Our whole idea of adulthood has changed,' says Noxon. 'We value flexibility and creativity—things kids are good at. It's brought us back to what we had as children.'

The trend isn’t limited to young people. Many grandparents collect model trains or American Girl dolls, drawn to the hobbies and stories from their own childhoods. Psychologists aren’t surprised: in America, youthfulness is linked to being fun and active. The internet has also made it easier to find like-minded enthusiasts, with sites like Facebook and Meetup.com helping organize adult scavenger hunts, game nights, and toy discussions. 'This is a generation of people who are less homogenous and more niche-oriented,' says psychologist Judith Sills. 'They can bond over their quirky differences. Ten years ago, it would have been much harder to find another kickball player if that’s what you wanted.'

"Nou chanje vizyon nou sou laj adilt," Noxon di. "Nou bay fleksibilite ak kreyativite valè—bagay timoun konnen byen. Sa fè nou tounen nan sa nou te renmen le nou te ti."
